13.4.s: svādor itthā viṣuvata iti viṣuvān vai pañcamam ahas tāsu rāyovājīyam
13.4.d: स्वादोर् इत्था विषुवत इति विषुवान् वै पञ्चमम् अहस् तासु रायोवाजीयम्
13.4.m: ‘Of the sweet [soma] indeed from the central point’—the central point (viṣuvant) is the fifth day; on them [is sung] the Rāyovājīya.

13.4.s: indro yatīn sālāvṛkebhyaḥ prāyacchat teṣāṃ traya udaśiṣyanta pṛthuraśmir bṛhadgirī rāyovājas te 'bruvan ko na imān putrān bhariṣyatīty aham itīndro 'bravīt tān ādhinidhāya paricāryaṃ carad vardhayaṃs tān vardhayitvābravīt kumārakā varān vṛṇīdhvam iti kṣatraṃ mahyam ity abravīt pṛthuraśmis tasmā etena pārthuraśmena kṣatraṃ prāyacchat kṣatrakāma etena stuvīta kṣatrasyaivāsya prakāśo bhavati brahmavarcasaṃ mahyam ity abravīt bṛhādgiris tasmā etena bārhadgireṇa prāyacchat brahmavarcasakāma etena stuvīta brahmavarcasī bhavati paśūn mahyam ity abravīd rāyovājas tasmā etena rāyovājīyena paśūn prāyacchat paśukāma etena stuvīta paśumān bhavati
13.4.d: इन्द्रो यतीन् सालावृकेभ्यः प्रायच्छत् तेषां त्रय उदशिष्यन्त पृथुरश्मिर् बृहद्गिरी रायोवाजस् ते ऽब्रुवन् को न इमान् पुत्रान् भरिष्यतीत्य् अहम् इतीन्द्रो ऽब्रवीत् तान् आधिनिधाय परिचार्यं चरद् वर्धयंस् तान् वर्धयित्वाब्रवीत् कुमारका वरान् वृणीध्वम् इति क्षत्रं मह्यम् इत्य् अब्रवीत् पृथुरश्मिस् तस्मा एतेन पार्थुरश्मेन क्षत्रं प्रायच्छत् क्षत्रकाम एतेन स्तुवीत क्षत्रस्यैवास्य प्रकाशो भवति ब्रह्मवर्चसं मह्यम् इत्य् अब्रवीत् बृहाद्गिरिस् तस्मा एतेन बार्हद्गिरेण प्रायच्छत् ब्रह्मवर्चसकाम एतेन स्तुवीत ब्रह्मवर्चसी भवति पशून् मह्यम् इत्य् अब्रवीद् रायोवाजस् तस्मा एतेन रायोवाजीयेन पशून् प्रायच्छत् पशुकाम एतेन स्तुवीत पशुमान् भवति
13.4.m: Indra delivered the yatis over to the hyenas. Three of them were left over: Pṛthuraśmi, Bṛhadgiri, and Rāyovāja. They said, 'Who will support us, these sons?' 'I,' Indra said. Having put them under his care, performing service, he reared them. Having reared them, he said, 'Little boys, choose boons.' 'Dominion for me,' said Pṛthuraśmi. To him he gave dominion by means of this Pārthuraśma [sāman]. One who desires dominion should praise with this; light of dominion indeed comes to him. 'Brahminical lustre for me,' said Bṛhadgiri. To him he gave [it] by means of this Bārhadgira [sāman]. One who desires brahminical lustre should praise with this; he becomes endowed with brahminical lustre. 'Cattle for me,' said Rāyovāja. To him he gave cattle by means of this Rāyovājīya [sāman]. One who desires cattle should praise with this; he becomes possessed of cattle.

13.4.s: pārthuraśmaṃ rājanyāya brahmasāma kuryāt bārhadgiraṃ brāhmaṇāya rāyovājīyaṃ vaiśyāya svenaivenāṃs tad rūpeṇa samardhayati stomaḥ
13.4.d: पार्थुरश्मं राजन्याय ब्रह्मसाम कुर्यात् बार्हद्गिरं ब्राह्मणाय रायोवाजीयं वैश्याय स्वेनैवेनांस् तद् रूपेण समर्धयति स्तोमः
13.4.m: He should make the Pārthuraśma the chant of the Brahman priest for a noble, the Bārhadgira for a brahmin, and the Rāyovājīya for a vaiśya. He thereby supplies them fully with their own characteristic form. [Such is] the stoma.

13.5.s: asāvy aṃśur madāya iti gāyatrī bhavati madavad vai rasavat tṛtīyasavanaṃ madam eva tad rasaṃ dadhāti
13.5.d: असाव्य् अंशुर् मदाय इति गायत्री भवति मदवद् वै रसवत् तृतीयसवनं मदम् एव तद् रसं दधाति
13.5.m: 'The stalk has been pressed for intoxication'—this is in the gāyatrī [metre]. Possessed of intoxication, full of sap indeed is the third pressing; thus he places intoxication and sap [into it].

13.5.s: abhi dyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśa ity abhīti rathantarasya rūpaṃ bṛhad iti bṛhata ubhayos saha rūpam upaity ubhau hi varṇāv etad ahaḥ
13.5.d: अभि द्युम्नं बृहद्यश इत्य् अभीति रथन्तरस्य रूपं बृहद् इति बृहत उभयोस् सह रूपम् उपैत्य् उभौ हि वर्णाव् एतद् अहः
13.5.m: 'Unto splendour, unto high renown'—'unto' is the characteristic form of the Rathantara; 'high' is that of the Bṛhat. He approaches the characteristic form of both together, for both kinds belong to this day.

13.5.s: prāṇā śiśur mahīnām iti simānāṃ rūpaṃ mahyo hi simāḥ svenaivainās tad rūpeṇa samardhayati
13.5.d: प्राणा शिशुर् महीनाम् इति सिमानां रूपं मह्यो हि सिमाः स्वेनैवैनास् तद् रूपेण समर्धयति
13.5.m: 'The breath, the child of the great ones'—this is the characteristic form of the Simā verses, for great are the Simās. He thereby supplies them fully with their own characteristic form.

13.5.s: pavasva vājasātaya iti vaiṣṇavyo 'nuṣṭubho bhavanti
13.5.d: पवस्व वाजसातय इति वैष्णव्यो ऽनुष्टुभो भवन्ति
13.5.m: 'Flow to win booty'—these are anuṣṭubhs addressed to Viṣṇu.

13.5.s: yajño vai viṣṇur yad atra nāpi kriyate tad viṣṇunā yajñenāpi karoti
13.5.d: यज्ञो वै विष्णुर् यद् अत्र नापि क्रियते तद् विष्णुना यज्ञेनापि करोति
13.5.m: Viṣṇu indeed is the sacrifice; whatever is not performed here, that he performs by means of Viṣṇu, the sacrifice.

13.5.s: indur vājī pavate gonyoghā iti simānāṃ rūpaṃ svenaivainās tad rūpeṇa samardhayati
13.5.d: इन्दुर् वाजी पवते गोन्योघा इति सिमानां रूपं स्वेनैवैनास् तद् रूपेण समर्धयति
13.5.m: 'The bright drop, the prize-winner, flows, a stream of cattle'—this is the characteristic form of the Simās. He thereby supplies them fully with their own characteristic form.

13.5.s: triṣṭubhaḥ satyo jagatyo rūpeṇa tasmāj jagatīnāṃ loke kriyante
13.5.d: त्रिष्टुभः सत्यो जगत्यो रूपेण तस्माज् जगतीनां लोके क्रियन्ते
13.5.m: Being triṣṭubhs, [they are applied] with the form of jagatīs; therefore they are performed in the place of jagatīs. / It is the Gāyatra [sāman], just what is the brahminical explanation of the Gāyatra.

13.5.s: gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
13.5.d: गायत्रं भवति यद् एव गायत्रस्य ब्राह्मणम्

13.5.s: santani bhavati pañcamasyāhnas santatyai
13.5.d: सन्तनि भवति पञ्चमस्याह्नस् सन्तत्यै
13.5.m: It is the Santani [sāman], for the continuity of the fifth day.

13.5.s: vāg vā eṣā pratatā yad dvādaśāhas tasyā eṣa viṣuvān yat pañcamam ahas tām evaitena santanoti
13.5.d: वाग् वा एषा प्रतता यद् द्वादशाहस् तस्या एष विषुवान् यत् पञ्चमम् अहस् ताम् एवैतेन सन्तनोति
13.5.m: This twelve-day rite is indeed speech stretched out. That which is the fifth day is its central day. Speech itself he thereby connects together.

13.5.s: cyāvanaṃ bhavati
13.5.d: च्यावनं भवति

13.5.s: prajātir vai cyāvanaṃ prajāyate bahur bhavati cyāvanena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
13.5.d: प्रजातिर् वै च्यावनं प्रजायते बहुर् भवति च्यावनेन तुष्टुवानः
13.5.m: The Cyāvana is indeed procreation. He propagates offspring, he becomes manifold, who has praised with the Cyāvana.

13.5.s: ebhyo vai lokebhyo vṛṣṭir apākrāmat tāṃ prajāpatiś cyāvanenācyāvayad yad acyāvayat tac cyāvanasya cyāvanatvaṃ cyāvayati vṛṣṭiṃ cyāvanena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
13.5.d: एभ्यो वै लोकेभ्यो वृष्टिर् अपाक्रामत् तां प्रजापतिश् च्यावनेनाच्यावयद् यद् अच्यावयत् तच् च्यावनस्य च्यावनत्वं च्यावयति वृष्टिं च्यावनेन तुष्टुवानः
13.5.m: Rain departed from these worlds. Prajāpati brought it down with the Cyāvana. Because he brought it down (acyāvayat), that is the Cyāvana-nature of the Cyāvana. He brings down rain, who has praised with the Cyāvana.

13.5.s: kroṣa bhavati
13.5.d: क्रोष भवति

13.5.s: etena vā indra indrakrośe viśvāmitrajamadagnī imā gāva ity ākrośat paśunām avarudhyai krośaṃ kriyate
13.5.d: एतेन वा इन्द्र इन्द्रक्रोशे विश्वामित्रजमदग्नी इमा गाव इत्य् आक्रोशत् पशुनाम् अवरुध्यै क्रोशं क्रियते
13.5.m: By this, indeed, at Indra's shout, Indra shouted out to Viśvāmitra and Jamadagni: 'These are cattle!' The Krośa is performed for the acquisition of cattle.

13.5.s: gaurīvitaṃ bhavati yad eva gaurīvitasya brāhmaṇam
13.5.d: गौरीवितं भवति यद् एव गौरीवितस्य ब्राह्मणम्
13.5.m: It is the Gaurīvita [sāman], just what is the brahminical explanation of the Gaurīvita.

13.5.s: ṛṣabhaḥ śākvaro bhavati
13.5.d: ऋषभः शाक्वरो भवति
13.5.m: It is the bull of the Śakvarī [sāman].

13.5.s: paśavo vai śakvaryaḥ paśuṣv eva tan mithunam apy arjati prajātyai na ha vā anṛṣabhāḥ paśavaḥ prajāyante
13.5.d: पशवो वै शक्वर्यः पशुष्व् एव तन् मिथुनम् अप्य् अर्जति प्रजात्यै न ह वा अनृषभाः पशवः प्रजायन्ते
13.5.m: The Śakvarī [verses] are indeed cattle; he thereby unites a pair among cattle for propagation. Cattle are not procreated without a bull.

13.5.s: pārthaṃ bhavati
13.5.d: पार्थं भवति

13.5.s: etena vai pṛthur vainya ubhayeṣāṃ paśūnām ādhipatyam āśnutobhayeṣāṃ paśunām ādhipatyam aśnute pārthena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
13.5.d: एतेन वै पृथुर् वैन्य उभयेषां पशूनाम् आधिपत्यम् आश्नुतोभयेषां पशुनाम् आधिपत्यम् अश्नुते पार्थेन तुष्टुवानः
13.5.m: By this, indeed, Pṛthu Vainya obtained overlordship over both kinds of cattle. He obtains overlordship over both kinds of cattle, who has praised with the Pārtha.

13.5.s: aṣṭeḍaḥ padastobho bhavati
13.5.d: अष्टेडः पदस्तोभो भवति
13.5.m: It is the Padastobha with eight iḍās.

13.5.s: indro vṛtrāya vajram udayacchat taṃ ṣoḍaśabhir bhogaiḥ paryabhujat sa etaṃ padastobham apaśyat tenāpāveṣṭayad apāveṣṭayann iva gāyet pāpmano 'pahatyai
13.5.d: इन्द्रो वृत्राय वज्रम् उदयच्छत् तं षोडशभिर् भोगैः पर्यभुजत् स एतं पदस्तोभम् अपश्यत् तेनापावेष्टयद् अपावेष्टयन्न् इव गायेत् पाप्मनो ऽपहत्यै
13.5.m: Indra raised his vajra against Vṛtra; he encircled him with sixteen coils. He saw this Padastobha; with it he unwound him. One should chant as if unwinding, for the striking off of evil.

13.5.s: pāpmā vāva sa tam agṛhṇāt taṃ padastobhenāpāhatāpa pāpmānaṃ hate padastobhena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
13.5.d: पाप्मा वाव स तम् अगृह्णात् तं पदस्तोभेनापाहताप पाप्मानं हते पदस्तोभेन तुष्टुवानः
13.5.m: Evil indeed seized him; he struck it off with the Padastobha. He strikes off evil, who has praised with the Padastobha.

13.5.s: pador uttamam apaśyat tat padastobhasya padastobhatvam
13.5.d: पदोर् उत्तमम् अपश्यत् तत् पदस्तोभस्य पदस्तोभत्वम्
13.5.m: He saw the last of the verses; that is the Padastobha-nature of the Padastobha.

13.5.s: dvādaśanidhano bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai
13.5.d: द्वादशनिधनो भवति प्रतिष्ठायै
13.5.m: It has twelve cadences, for stability.

13.5.s: dāśaspatyaṃ bhavati
13.5.d: दाशस्पत्यं भवति

13.5.s: yāṃ vai gāṃ praśaṃsanti dāśaspatyeti tāṃ praśaṃsanty ahar evaitena praśaṃsanti
13.5.d: यां वै गां प्रशंसन्ति दाशस्पत्येति तां प्रशंसन्त्य् अहर् एवैतेन प्रशंसन्ति
13.5.m: The cow that they praise, they praise as Dāśaspatyā; through this they praise the day itself.

13.5.s: nidhanāntāḥ pavamānā bhavanty ahno dhṛtyai stomaḥ
13.5.d: निधनान्ताः पवमाना भवन्त्य् अह्नो धृत्यै स्तोमः
13.5.m: The pavamāna [chants] end in cadences, for the sustaining of the day. [Such is] the stoma.

13.6.s: apacchid iva vā etad yajñakāṇḍaṃ yad ukthāni yad eti salomatvāyaiva
13.6.d: अपच्छिद् इव वा एतद् यज्ञकाण्डं यद् उक्थानि यद् एति सलोमत्वायैव
13.6.m: This section of the sacrifice, namely the uktha [chants], is as it were cut off; when it proceeds [thus], it is for regular continuity.

13.6.s: indrāya sāma gāyata iti pūrṇāḥ kakubhas tenānaśanāyuko bhavati
13.6.d: इन्द्राय साम गायत इति पूर्णाः ककुभस् तेनानशनायुको भवति
13.6.m: 'Sing a sāman unto Indra'—these are complete kakubhs; thereby he does not become hungry.

13.6.s: puruṣo vai kakup puruṣam eva tan madhyataḥ prīṇāti
13.6.d: पुरुषो वै ककुप् पुरुषम् एव तन् मध्यतः प्रीणाति
13.6.m: The kakubh is man; he thereby gratifies man from within.

13.6.s: asāvi soma indra ta iti simānāṃ rūpaṃ svenaivaināṃs tad rūpeṇa samardhayati
13.6.d: असावि सोम इन्द्र त इति सिमानां रूपं स्वेनैवैनांस् तद् रूपेण समर्धयति
13.6.m: 'This Soma has been pressed for thee, Indra'—this is the characteristic form of the Simās; he thereby supplies them fully with their own characteristic form.

13.6.s: devāś ca vā asurāś ca samadadhata yatare naḥ sañjayāṃs teṣāṃ naḥ paśavo 'sān iti te devā asurān sañjayena samajayan yat samajayaṃs tasmāt sañjayaṃ paśūnām avarudhyai sañjayaṃ kriyate
13.6.d: देवाश् च वा असुराश् च समदधत यतरे नः सञ्जयांस् तेषां नः पशवो ऽसान् इति ते देवा असुरान् सञ्जयेन समजयन् यत् समजयंस् तस्मात् सञ्जयं पशूनाम् अवरुध्यै सञ्जयं क्रियते
13.6.m: The gods and the Asuras made an agreement: 'Whichever of us shall conquer, to them shall belong our cattle.' The gods conquered the Asuras by means of the Sañjaya. Because they conquered (samajayan), therefore it is the Sañjaya. The Sañjaya is performed for the acquisition of cattle.

13.6.s: dīrghajihvī vā idaṃ rakṣo yajñahā yajñiyān avalihaty acarat tām indraḥ kayācana māyayā hantuṃ nāśaṃsatātha ha sumitraḥ kutsaḥ kalyāṇa āsa tam abravīd imām acchā brūṣveti tām acchā brūta sainam abravīn nāhaitan na śuśruva priyam iva tu me hṛdayasyeti tām ajñapayat tāṃ saṃskṛte 'hatāṃ tad vāva tau tarhy akāmayetāṃ kāmasani sāma saumitraṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
13.6.d: दीर्घजिह्वी वा इदं रक्षो यज्ञहा यज्ञियान् अवलिहत्य् अचरत् ताम् इन्द्रः कयाचन मायया हन्तुं नाशंसताथ ह सुमित्रः कुत्सः कल्याण आस तम् अब्रवीद् इमाम् अच्छा ब्रूष्वेति ताम् अच्छा ब्रूत सैनम् अब्रवीन् नाहैतन् न शुश्रुव प्रियम् इव तु मे हृदयस्येति ताम् अज्ञपयत् तां संस्कृते ऽहतां तद् वाव तौ तर्ह्य् अकामयेतां कामसनि साम सौमित्रं कामम् एवैतेनावरुन्धे
13.6.m: Dīrghajihvī, a demoness, destroying the sacrifice, went about licking the offerings. Indra did not expect to slay her by any magical power. Now Sumitra Kutsa was handsome; Indra said to him, 'Address her.' He addressed her. She said to him, 'Never have I heard this, but it is as if dear to my heart.' He made her comply; having made her ready, they slew her. That very desire they then wished for. The Saumitra is a sāman that wins desire; through it he wins his desire.

13.6.s: sumitraḥ san krūram akar ity enaṃ vāg abhyavadat taṃ śug ārcchat sa tapo 'tapyata sa etat saumitram apaśyat tena śucam apāhatāpaśucaṃ hate saumitreṇa tuṣṭuvānaḥ
13.6.d: सुमित्रः सन् क्रूरम् अकर् इत्य् एनं वाग् अभ्यवदत् तं शुग् आर्च्छत् स तपो ऽतप्यत स एतत् सौमित्रम् अपश्यत् तेन शुचम् अपाहतापशुचं हते सौमित्रेण तुष्टुवानः
13.6.m: A voice addressed him: 'Being Sumitra, thou hast done a cruel deed.' Grief came upon him. He performed ascetic heat. He saw this Saumitra [sāman]; by means of it he struck off grief. He strikes off grief, who has praised with the Saumitra.

13.6.s: pāpmānaṃ hatvā yad amahīyanta tan mahāvaiśvāmitrasya mahāvaiśvāmitratvam
13.6.d: पाप्मानं हत्वा यद् अमहीयन्त तन् महावैश्वामित्रस्य महावैश्वामित्रत्वम्
13.6.m: Because they were magnified after having slain evil, that is the Mahāvaiśvāmitra-nature of the Mahāvaiśvāmitra.

13.6.s: hāyā ihayā ohā oheti paśūn evaitena nyauhanta
13.6.d: हाया इहया ओहा ओहेति पशून् एवैतेन न्यौहन्त
13.6.m: With 'Hāyā, ihayā, ohā, ohe' they drove the cattle together.
It has three iḍās, for the sustaining of the three-day period.

13.6.s: dravantīm iḍām uttamām upayanti ṣaṣṭhasyāhnaḥ santatyai
13.6.d: द्रवन्तीम् इडाम् उत्तमाम् उपयन्ति षष्ठस्याह्नः सन्तत्यै
13.6.m: They reach a flowing iḍā at the end, for the continuity of the sixth day.

13.6.s: triṇava eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai puṣṭyai trivṛd vā eṣa puṣṭhaḥ
13.6.d: त्रिणव एव स्तोमो भवति प्रतिष्ठायै पुष्ट्यै त्रिवृद् वा एष पुष्ठः
13.6.m: The stoma is the twenty-seven-fold, for stability, for prosperity; for this prosperity is threefold.

13.7.s: jyotir yajñasya pavate madhupriyam iti ṣaṣṭhasyāhnaḥ pratipad bhavati
13.7.d: ज्योतिर् यज्ञस्य पवते मधुप्रियम् इति षष्ठस्याह्नः प्रतिपद् भवति
13.7.m: 'The light of the sacrifice flows, dear as honey'—this is the introductory verse of the sixth day.

13.7.s: jyotir vai gāyatrī chandamāṃ jyotiḥ revatī sāmnāṃ jyotis trayastriṃśaḥ stomānāṃ jyotir eva tat samyak saṃdadhāsy api ha putrasya putro jyotiṣmān bhavati
13.7.d: ज्योतिर् वै गायत्री छन्दमां ज्योतिः रेवती साम्नां ज्योतिस् त्रयस्त्रिंशः स्तोमानां ज्योतिर् एव तत् सम्यक् संदधास्य् अपि ह पुत्रस्य पुत्रो ज्योतिष्मान् भवति
13.7.m: Light indeed is the gāyatrī among metres, light is the Revatī among sāmans, light is the thirty-three-fold stoma among stomas. He thus unites light completely; also the son of his son becomes endowed with light.

13.7.s: madhu priyam iti paśavo vai revatyo madhupriyaṃ tad eva tad abhivadati
13.7.d: मधु प्रियम् इति पशवो वै रेवत्यो मधुप्रियं तद् एव तद् अभिवदति
13.7.m: 'Dear as honey'—the Revatīs are cattle, and dear as honey; that is what he thereby expresses.

13.7.s: madintamo matsara indriyo rasa itīndriyaṃ vai vīryaṃ rasaḥ paśavas tad eva tad abhivadati
13.7.d: मदिन्तमो मत्सर इन्द्रियो रस इतीन्द्रियं वै वीर्यं रसः पशवस् तद् एव तद् अभिवदति
13.7.m: 'Most intoxicating, exhilarating, a vigorous sap'—vigour indeed is vital power, sap is cattle; that is what he thereby expresses.
'The swift ones have groomed [him]'—this is the corresponding verse.
For now the days are as if discharged.

13.7.s: pūrvam u caiva tad rūpam apareṇa rūpeṇānuvadati yat pūrvaṃ rūpam apareṇa rūpeṇānuvadati tad anurūpasyānurūpatvam anurūpa enaṃ putro jāyate ya evaṃ veda stotrīyānurūpau tṛcau bhavataḥ prāṇāpānānām avarudhyai
13.7.d: पूर्वम् उ चैव तद् रूपम् अपरेण रूपेणानुवदति यत् पूर्वं रूपम् अपरेण रूपेणानुवदति तद् अनुरूपस्यानुरूपत्वम् अनुरूप एनं पुत्रो जायते य एवं वेद स्तोत्रीयानुरूपौ तृचौ भवतः प्राणापानानाम् अवरुध्यै
13.7.m: And he repeats that earlier form with a later form; that he repeats the earlier form with a later form, that is the corresponding nature of the corresponding verse (anurūpa). A corresponding son is born to him who knows thus. The stotriya and anurūpa are triplets, for securing the in-breath and out-breath.

13.7.s: daśarcau bhavato daśākṣarā virāṭ vairājam annam annādyasyāvarudhyai
13.7.d: दशर्चौ भवतो दशाक्षरा विराट् वैराजम् अन्नम् अन्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै
13.7.m: They are ten-versed; the virāj has ten syllables, and food belongs to the virāj, for securing food.

13.7.s: uttaro daśarco bhavati sodarka indriyasya vīryasya rasasyānatikṣārāya
13.7.d: उत्तरो दशर्चो भवति सोदर्क इन्द्रियस्य वीर्यस्य रसस्यानतिक्षाराय
13.7.m: The latter is ten-versed, having a concluding refrain, so that power, strength, and sap do not overflow.

13.7.s: yatra ve devā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ rasam apaśyaṃs tad anunyatudan
13.7.d: यत्र वे देवा इन्द्रियं वीर्यं रसम् अपश्यंस् तद् अनुन्यतुदन्
13.7.m: Where indeed the gods saw power, strength, and sap, there they struck after it.
It has four verses, for support.

13.7.s: dhvasre vai puruṣantī tarantapurumīḍhābhyāṃ vaitadaśvibhyāṃ sahasrāṇy aditsatāṃ tāv aikṣetāṃ kathaṃ nāv idam āttam apratigṛhītaṃ syād iti tau praty etāṃ dhvasrayoḥ puruṣantyor ā sahasrāṇi dadmahe tarat sa mandī dhāvatīti tato vai tat tayor āttam apratigṛhītam abhavat
13.7.d: ध्वस्रे वै पुरुषन्ती तरन्तपुरुमीढाभ्यां वैतदश्विभ्यां सहस्राण्य् अदित्सतां ताव् ऐक्षेतां कथं नाव् इदम् आत्तम् अप्रतिगृहीतं स्याद् इति तौ प्रत्य् एतां ध्वस्रयोः पुरुषन्त्योर् आ सहस्राणि दद्महे तरत् स मन्दी धावतीति ततो वै तत् तयोर् आत्तम् अप्रतिगृहीतम् अभवत्
13.7.m: Dhvasra and Puruṣanti wished to give thousands to Taranta and Purumīḍha, or rather to the two Aśvins. They two considered: 'How may this be taken by us without being received [as a gift]?' They two chanted in response: 'Of Dhvasra and Puruṣanti we take the thousands; cross over, running exhilarated!' Thereby indeed it became taken by the two, not received [as a gift].

13.7.s: āttam asyāpratigṛhītaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda
13.7.d: आत्तम् अस्याप्रतिगृहीतं भवति य एवं वेद
13.7.m: It is taken by him, not received [as a gift], who knows thus.

13.7.s: vinārāśaṃso bhavaty ubhayasyānnādyasyāvarudhyai mānuṣasya ca daivasya ca
13.7.d: विनाराशंसो भवत्य् उभयस्यान्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै मानुषस्य च दैवस्य च
13.7.m: It is without a narāśaṃsa, for securing both kinds of food: human and divine.

13.7.s: tṛca uttamo bhavati yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
13.7.d: तृच उत्तमो भवति येनैव प्राणेन प्रयन्ति तम् अभ्युद्यन्ति
13.7.m: The last is a triplet; with whichever breath they proceed, that they rise up toward.

13.7.s: trayastriṃśa eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai devatāsu vā eṣa pratiṣṭhitaḥ
13.7.d: त्रयस्त्रिंश एव स्तोमो भवति प्रतिष्ठायै देवतासु वा एष प्रतिष्ठितः
13.7.m: The stoma is the thirty-three-fold stoma, for support; for it is supported among the deities.

13.8.s: imaṃ stomam arhate jātavedasa ity āgneyam ājyaṃ bhavati sodarkam indriyasya vīryasya rasasyānatikṣārāya yatra vai devā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ rasam apaśyaṃs tad anunyatudan
13.8.d: इमं स्तोमम् अर्हते जातवेदस इत्य् आग्नेयम् आज्यं भवति सोदर्कम् इन्द्रियस्य वीर्यस्य रसस्यानतिक्षाराय यत्र वै देवा इन्द्रियं वीर्यं रसम् अपश्यंस् तद् अनुन्यतुदन्
13.8.m: 'This stoma to the worthy Jātavedas' is the ājyastotra to Agni; it has a concluding refrain, so that power, strength, and sap do not overflow; where indeed the gods saw power, strength, and sap, there they struck after it.

13.8.s: prativāṃ sūra udita iti sūravan maitrāvaruṇam
13.8.d: प्रतिवां सूर उदित इति सूरवन् मैत्रावरुणम्
13.8.m: 'Against you two, as the sun has risen' is the [ājyastotra] to Mitra and Varuṇa, containing [the word] 'sun' (sūra).

13.8.s: anto vai sūro 'nta etat ṣaṣṭham ahar ahnām anta eva tad ante stuvate pratiṣṭhāyai
13.8.d: अन्तो वै सूरो ऽन्त एतत् षष्ठम् अहर् अह्नाम् अन्त एव तद् अन्ते स्तुवते प्रतिष्ठायै
13.8.m: The end indeed is the sun; this sixth day is the end of the days. Thus they praise at the end, for support.

13.8.s: bhindhi viśvā apadviṣa ity aindraṃ sodarkam indriyasya vīryasya rasasyānatikṣārāya yatra vai devā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ rasam apaśyaṃs tad anunyatudan
13.8.d: भिन्धि विश्वा अपद्विष इत्य् ऐन्द्रं सोदर्कम् इन्द्रियस्य वीर्यस्य रसस्यानतिक्षाराय यत्र वै देवा इन्द्रियं वीर्यं रसम् अपश्यंस् तद् अनुन्यतुदन्
13.8.m: 'Shatter all enemies' is the [ājyastotra] to Indra; it has a concluding refrain, so that power, strength, and sap do not overflow; where indeed the gods saw power, strength, and sap, there they struck after it.

13.8.s: yajñasya hi stha ṛtvija ity aindrāgnaṃ sodarkam indriyasya vīryasya rasasyānatikṣārāya yatra vai devā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ rasam apaśyaṃs tad anunyatudan stomaḥ
13.8.d: यज्ञस्य हि स्थ ऋत्विज इत्य् ऐन्द्राग्नं सोदर्कम् इन्द्रियस्य वीर्यस्य रसस्यानतिक्षाराय यत्र वै देवा इन्द्रियं वीर्यं रसम् अपश्यंस् तद् अनुन्यतुदन् स्तोमः
13.8.m: 'For you are the priests of the sacrifice' is the [ājyastotra] to Indra and Agni; it has a concluding refrain, so that power, strength, and sap do not overflow; where indeed the gods saw power, strength, and sap, there they struck after it. [Such is] the stoma.

13.9.s: indrāyendo marutvata iti marutvatyo gāyatryo bhavanti
13.9.d: इन्द्रायेन्दो मरुत्वत इति मरुत्वत्यो गायत्र्यो भवन्ति
13.9.m: 'For Indra, O Soma, accompanied by the Maruts' are gāyatrī verses accompanied by the Maruts.

13.9.s: marutvad dhi mādhyandinaṃ savanam
13.9.d: मरुत्वद् धि माध्यन्दिनं सवनम्
13.9.m: For the midday pressing belongs to the Maruts.

13.9.s: mṛjyamānaḥ suhastya iti simānāṃ rūpam
13.9.d: मृज्यमानः सुहस्त्य इति सिमानां रूपम्
13.9.m: 'Being cleansed, with good hands' is the form of the Simās.

13.9.s: samānaṃ vai simānāṃ rūpaṃ revatīnāṃ ca simābhyo hy adhirevatyaḥ prajāyante
13.9.d: समानं वै सिमानां रूपं रेवतीनां च सिमाभ्यो ह्य् अधिरेवत्यः प्रजायन्ते
13.9.m: The same indeed is the form of the Simās and of the Revatīs, for from the Simās the Revatīs are born.

13.9.s: etam u tyaṃ daśa kṣipa ity ādityā ādityā vā imāḥ prajās tāsām eva madhyataḥ pratitiṣṭhati
13.9.d: एतम् उ त्यं दश क्षिप इत्य् आदित्या आदित्या वा इमाः प्रजास् तासाम् एव मध्यतः प्रतितिष्ठति
13.9.m: 'This one indeed, the ten fingers' belongs to the Ādityas; these creatures indeed belong to Āditya; right in their midst he becomes established.

13.9.s: gāyatryaḥ satyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa tasmāt triṣṭubhāṃ loke kriyante
13.9.d: गायत्र्यः सत्यस् त्रिष्टुभो रूपेण तस्मात् त्रिष्टुभां लोके क्रियन्ते
13.9.m: Being gāyatrīs, they have the form of triṣṭubhs; therefore they are performed in the place of triṣṭubhs.

13.9.s: gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
13.9.d: गायत्रं भवति यद् एव गायत्रस्य ब्राह्मणम्
13.9.m: The Gāyatra is [employed], according to the Brahmana of the Gāyatra itself.

13.9.s: iṣovṛdhīyaṃ bhavati
13.9.d: इषोवृधीयं भवति

13.9.s: paśavo vā iṣovṛdhīyaṃ paśūnām avarudhyā iṣe vai pañcamam ahar vṛdhe ṣaṣṭham avardhanta hy etarhi yajamānam evaitena vardhayanti
13.9.d: पशवो वा इषोवृधीयं पशूनाम् अवरुध्या इषे वै पञ्चमम् अहर् वृधे षष्ठम् अवर्धन्त ह्य् एतर्हि यजमानम् एवैतेन वर्धयन्ति
13.9.m: Cattle indeed are the Iṣovṛdhīya, for securing cattle. For refreshment (iṣ) is the fifth day, for growth (vṛdh) the sixth; for they grew at this time; they cause the sacrificer himself to grow by it.

13.9.s: krauñcaṃ bhavati
13.9.d: क्रौञ्चं भवति

13.9.s: kruṅṅ eṣyam ahar avindad eṣyam iva vai ṣaṣṭham ahar evaitena vindanti
13.9.d: क्रुङ्ङ् एष्यम् अहर् अविन्दद् एष्यम् इव वै षष्ठम् अहर् एवैतेन विन्दन्ति
13.9.m: The curlew (kruṅ) found the day that was to be sought; as if to be sought is the sixth day; they find it by this.

13.9.s: vājadāvaryo bhavanti
13.9.d: वाजदावर्यो भवन्ति

13.9.s: annaṃ vai vājo 'nnādyasyāvarudhyai yadā hi vā annam atha gaur athāśvo 'tha puruṣo vājī
13.9.d: अन्नं वै वाजो ऽन्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै यदा हि वा अन्नम् अथ गौर् अथाश्वो ऽथ पुरुषो वाजी
13.9.m: Food indeed is booty (vāja), for securing food. For when there is food, then an ox, then a horse, then a man is vigorous (vājī).

13.9.s: revatyo bhavanti pratiṣṭhāyai
13.9.d: रेवत्यो भवन्ति प्रतिष्ठायै
13.9.m: The Revatīs are [employed], for support.

13.9.s: ṣaṇṇidhanī ṣaḍrātrasya dhṛtyai
13.9.d: षण्णिधनी षड्रात्रस्य धृत्यै
13.9.m: It has six cadences, for the holding fast of the six-day period.

13.9.s: āpo vai revatyas tā yat pṛṣṭhaṃ kuryur apaśur yajamānaḥ syāt paśūn asya nirdaheyur yatra vā āpo vivartante tad oṣadhayo jāyante 'tha yatrāvatiṣṭhante nirmṛtukās tatra bhavanti tasmāt pavamāne kurvanti parācā hi pavamānena stuvate
13.9.d: आपो वै रेवत्यस् ता यत् पृष्ठं कुर्युर् अपशुर् यजमानः स्यात् पशून् अस्य निर्दहेयुर् यत्र वा आपो विवर्तन्ते तद् ओषधयो जायन्ते ऽथ यत्रावतिष्ठन्ते निर्मृतुकास् तत्र भवन्ति तस्मात् पवमाने कुर्वन्ति पराचा हि पवमानेन स्तुवते
13.9.m: The waters indeed are the Revatīs; if they were to make them the pṛṣṭha, the sacrificer would be without cattle, [for] they would burn up his cattle. Where waters roll on, there plants grow; but where they stand still, things perish there. Therefore they perform them in the Pavamāna, for they praise with a forward-moving Pavamāna.

13.9.s: methī vā iṣovṛdhīyaṃ rajjuḥ krauñcaṃ vatso vājadāvaryo revatyo mātaro yad etāny evaṃ sāmāni kriyanta evam eva prattāṃ dugdhe
13.9.d: मेथी वा इषोवृधीयं रज्जुः क्रौञ्चं वत्सो वाजदावर्यो रेवत्यो मातरो यद् एतान्य् एवं सामानि क्रियन्त एवम् एव प्रत्तां दुग्धे
13.9.m: The hitching post indeed is the Iṣovṛdhīya; the rope is the Krauñca; the calf is the Vājadāvarīs; the mothers are the Revatīs. Because these sāmans are performed in this manner, he milks her just when she is surrendered.

13.9.s: aukṣṇorandhre bhavataḥ
13.9.d: औक्ष्णोरन्ध्रे भवतः
13.9.m: The two Aukṣṇorandhras are [employed].

13.9.s: ukṣṇorandhro vā etābhyāṃ kāvyo 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
13.9.d: उक्ष्णोरन्ध्रो वा एताभ्यां काव्यो ऽञ्जसा स्वर्गं लोकम् अपश्यत् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्यानुख्यात्यै स्वर्गाल् लोकान् न च्यवते तुष्टुवानः
13.9.m: Ukṣṇorandhra Kāvya, by these two, directly saw the world of heaven, for the revelation of the world of heaven; having praised, he does not fall from the world of heaven.

13.9.s: vājajid bhavati sarvasyāptyai sarvasya jityai sarvaṃ vā ete vājaṃ jayanti ye ṣaṣṭham ahar āgacchanti
13.9.d: वाजजिद् भवति सर्वस्याप्त्यै सर्वस्य जित्यै सर्वं वा एते वाजं जयन्ति ये षष्ठम् अहर् आगच्छन्ति
13.9.m: The Vājajit is [employed], for the attainment of everything, for the winning of everything; for all booty they win who come to the sixth day.

13.9.s: annaṃ vai vājo 'nnādyasyāvarudhyai
13.9.d: अन्नं वै वाजो ऽन्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै
13.9.m: Food indeed is booty, for securing food.

13.9.s: varuṇasāma bhavati
13.9.d: वरुणसाम भवति

13.9.s: etena vai varuṇo rājyam ādhipatyam agacchad yaśo 'bhavad rājyam ādhipatyaṃ gacchati yaśo bhavati varuṇasāmnā tuṣṭuvānaḥ
13.9.d: एतेन वै वरुणो राज्यम् आधिपत्यम् अगच्छद् यशो ऽभवद् राज्यम् आधिपत्यं गच्छति यशो भवति वरुणसाम्ना तुष्टुवानः
13.9.m: By this Varuṇa attained kingship and overlordship, and became famous; he attains kingship and overlordship, and becomes famous, who has praised with the Varuṇasāman.

13.9.s: aṅgirasāṃ goṣṭho bhavati
13.9.d: अङ्गिरसां गोष्ठो भवति
13.9.m: The Goṣṭha of the Aṅgirases is [employed].

13.9.s: paśavo vai revatyo gauṣṭham eva tat paśubhyaḥ paryasyanti tam evainān pravartayanty avisraṃsāya
13.9.d: पशवो वै रेवत्यो गौष्ठम् एव तत् पशुभ्यः पर्यस्यन्ति तम् एवैनान् प्रवर्तयन्त्य् अविस्रंसाय
13.9.m: Cattle indeed are the Revatīs; they cast a cowpen around the cattle; they drive them into it, so that they do not slip away.

13.9.s: ihavad vāmadevyaṃ bhavati
13.9.d: इहवद् वामदेव्यं भवति
13.9.m: The Vāmadevya containing [the word] 'iha' is [employed].

13.9.s: etena vai vāmadevo 'nnasya purodhām agacchad annaṃ vai brahmaṇaḥ purodhā annasyāvarudhyai
13.9.d: एतेन वै वामदेवो ऽन्नस्य पुरोधाम् अगच्छद् अन्नं वै ब्रह्मणः पुरोधा अन्नस्यावरुध्यै
13.9.m: By this Vāmadeva attained the primacy of food; food indeed is the primacy of the brahman, for securing food.

13.9.s: gāyatrīṣu stuvanti pratiṣṭhāyai brahmavarñcasāya yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
13.9.d: गायत्रीषु स्तुवन्ति प्रतिष्ठायै ब्रह्मवर्ञ्चसाय येनैव प्राणेन प्रयन्ति तम् अभ्युद्यन्ति
13.9.m: They praise on gāyatrī verses, for support, for brahminical lustre; with whichever breath they proceed, that they rise up toward.

13.9.s: marutvatyo gāyatryo bhavanti tad u traiṣṭubhād rūpān na yanti stomaḥ
13.9.d: मरुत्वत्यो गायत्र्यो भवन्ति तद् उ त्रैष्टुभाद् रूपान् न यन्ति स्तोमः
13.9.m: The gāyatrī verses are accompanied by the Maruts; and thus they do not depart from the form of the triṣṭubh. [Such is] the stoma.

13.10.s: yātayāmāny anyāni chandāṃsy ayātayāmā gāyatrī tasmād gāyatrīṣu stuvanti
13.10.d: यातयामान्य् अन्यानि छन्दांस्य् अयातयामा गायत्री तस्माद् गायत्रीषु स्तुवन्ति
13.10.m: Exhausted are the other metres, unexhausted is the gāyatrī; therefore they praise on gāyatrī verses.

13.10.s: surūpa kṛtnum ūtaya ity abhyārambheṇa ṣaṭpadāḥ ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpaṃ tena ṣaṣṭham ahar ārabhante santatyai
13.10.d: सुरूप कृत्नुम् ऊतय इत्य् अभ्यारम्भेण षट्पदाः षष्ठस्याह्नो रूपं तेन षष्ठम् अहर् आरभन्ते सन्तत्यै
13.10.m: 'For aid him who makes beautiful forms'—by this undertaking there are six-footed verses, the form of the sixth day; by it they undertake the sixth day, for continuity.

13.10.s: ubhe yad indra rodasī iti ṣaṭpadāḥ ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpaṃ tena ṣaṣṭham ahar ārabhante santatyai
13.10.d: उभे यद् इन्द्र रोदसी इति षट्पदाः षष्ठस्याह्नो रूपं तेन षष्ठम् अहर् आरभन्ते सन्तत्यै
13.10.m: 'When both heaven and earth, O Indra'—these are six-footed verses, the form of the sixth day; by it they undertake the sixth day, for continuity.
On the Revatī verses the Vāravantīya is the pṛṣṭha.

13.10.s: apāṃ vā eṣa raso yad revatyo revatīnāṃ raso yad vāravantīyaṃ sarasā eva tad revatīḥ prayuṅkte yad vāravantīyena pṛṣṭhena stuvate
13.10.d: अपां वा एष रसो यद् रेवत्यो रेवतीनां रसो यद् वारवन्तीयं सरसा एव तद् रेवतीः प्रयुङ्क्ते यद् वारवन्तीयेन पृष्ठेन स्तुवते
13.10.m: This sap of the waters is what the Revatīs are; the sap of the Revatīs is what the Vāravantīya is; full of sap indeed he employs the Revatīs when they praise with the Vāravantīya as the pṛṣṭha.

13.10.s: revad vā etad raivatyaṃ yad vāravantīyam asya revān revātyā jāyate
13.10.d: रेवद् वा एतद् रैवत्यं यद् वारवन्तीयम् अस्य रेवान् रेवात्या जायते
13.10.m: Wealthy indeed is this belonging to the Revatīs, which is the Vāravantīya; wealthy is he born to him through the Revatī.
He becomes wealthy who knows thus.

13.10.s: keśine vā etad dālbhyāya sāmāvir abhavat tad enam abravīd agātāro mā gāyanti mā mayodgāsiṣur iti kathaṃ ta āgā bhagava ity abravīd āgeyam evāsmy āgāyann iva gāyet pratiṣṭhāyai tad alammaṃ pārijānataṃ paścādakṣaṃ śayānam etām āgāṃ gāyantam ajānāt tam abravīt puras tvā dadhā iti tam abruvan ko nv ayaṃ kasmā alam ity alaṃ nu vai mahyam iti tad alammasyālammatvam
13.10.d: केशिने वा एतद् दाल्भ्याय सामाविर् अभवत् तद् एनम् अब्रवीद् अगातारो मा गायन्ति मा मयोद्गासिषुर् इति कथं त आगा भगव इत्य् अब्रवीद् आगेयम् एवास्म्य् आगायन्न् इव गायेत् प्रतिष्ठायै तद् अलम्मं पारिजानतं पश्चादक्षं शयानम् एताम् आगां गायन्तम् अजानात् तम् अब्रवीत् पुरस् त्वा दधा इति तम् अब्रुवन् को न्व् अयं कस्मा अलम् इत्य् अलं नु वै मह्यम् इति तद् अलम्मस्यालम्मत्वम्
13.10.m: This sāman revealed itself to Keśin Dālbhya. It said to him: 'Non-singers sing me; they have not sung out with me.' 'How is your song, O venerable one?' he said. 'I am indeed to be sung as an arrival; as if singing an arrival, one should sing, for support.' Then he recognized Alamma Pārijānata lying behind the axle, singing this arrival-song. He said to him: 'I place you in front.' They said to him: 'Who is this one now? For what is he sufficient (alam)?' 'He is indeed sufficient for me,' [he said]; that is the sufficiency of Alamma.
One should sing 'iha iha', for support.

There is the Ṛṣabha based on the Revatī verses.
Cattle, indeed, are connected with the Revatī; thus he unites a pair among cattle for procreation. Truly, cattle do not reproduce without a bull.

13.10.s: paśavo vai raivatyaḥ paśuṣv eva tan mithunam apyarjati prajātyai na ha vā anṛṣabhāḥ paśavaḥ prajāyante
13.10.d: पशवो वै रैवत्यः पशुष्व् एव तन् मिथुनम् अप्यर्जति प्रजात्यै न ह वा अनृषभाः पशवः प्रजायन्ते

13.10.s: śyeno ha vai pūrvapretāni vayāṃsy āpnoti pūrvapretānīva vai pūrvāṇy ahāni teṣām āptyai śyenaḥ kriyate
13.10.d: श्येनो ह वै पूर्वप्रेतानि वयांस्य् आप्नोति पूर्वप्रेतानीव वै पूर्वाण्य् अहानि तेषाम् आप्त्यै श्येनः क्रियते
13.10.m: The falcon (śyena) reaches the birds that have flown ahead. The preceding days are, as it were, those that have flown ahead; the Śyena is performed to attain them.

13.10.s: śyeno vā etad ahaḥ sampārayitum arhati sa hi vayasām āśiṣṭhas tasyānapahananāya sampāraṇāyaitat kriyate 'nto hi ṣaṣṭhaṃ cāhaḥ saptamaṃ ca
13.10.d: श्येनो वा एतद् अहः सम्पारयितुम् अर्हति स हि वयसाम् आशिष्ठस् तस्यानपहननाय सम्पारणायैतत् क्रियते ऽन्तो हि षष्ठं चाहः सप्तमं च
13.10.m: The falcon is able to carry this day across; for it is the swiftest of birds. This is performed so that it may carry it across without striking it down; for the sixth day and the seventh day are the end.

13.10.s: brahmavādino vadanti yad bṛhad āyatanāni pṛṣṭhāny athaite dve gāyatryau dve jagatyau kva tarhi bṛhatyo bhavantīti
13.10.d: ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति यद् बृहद् आयतनानि पृष्ठान्य् अथैते द्वे गायत्र्यौ द्वे जगत्यौ क्व तर्हि बृहत्यो भवन्तीति
13.10.m: The theologians say: 'Since the pṛṣṭhas have the bṛhatī as their base, and here there are two gāyatrī and two jagatī [verses], where then are the bṛhatīs?'

13.10.s: ye dve jagatyoḥ pade te gāyatryā upasampadyete tat sarvā bṛhatyo bhavanty āyatane pṛṣṭhāni yātayatyāyatanavān bhavati
13.10.d: ये द्वे जगत्योः पदे ते गायत्र्या उपसम्पद्येते तत् सर्वा बृहत्यो भवन्त्य् आयतने पृष्ठानि यातयत्यायतनवान् भवति
13.10.m: The two verses of the two jagatīs are added to the gāyatrī; thus they all become bṛhatīs. He sets the pṛṣṭhas in their proper place; he becomes possessed of a base.
They praise on six-line [verses] for the firm support of the six-day period.
He sacrifices with a seven-line [verse] for the continuity of the seventh day. [Such is] the stoma.

13.11.s: parisvāno giriṣṭhā iti parivatyo gāyatryo bhavanti sarvasya paryāptyai
13.11.d: परिस्वानो गिरिष्ठा इति परिवत्यो गायत्र्यो भवन्ति सर्वस्य पर्याप्त्यै
13.11.m: 'Sounding all around, dwelling on the mountain': there are gāyatrīs containing the word 'pari' ('around'), for the compassing of everything.

13.11.s: sasunveyo vasūnām iti paśavo vai vasu paśūnām avarudhyai
13.11.d: ससुन्वेयो वसूनाम् इति पशवो वै वसु पशूनाम् अवरुध्यै
13.11.m: 'To be pressed out, possessing goods': cattle, indeed, are goods; [it is] for the obtainment of cattle.

13.11.s: taṃ vassakhāyo madāya iti vālakhilyāḥ
13.11.d: तं वस्सखायो मदाय इति वालखिल्याः
13.11.m: 'Him, O friends, for exhilaration': these are the Vālakhilyas.

13.11.s: vālakhilyāv etau tṛcau ṣaṣṭhe cāhani saptame ca
13.11.d: वालखिल्याव् एतौ तृचौ षष्ठे चाहनि सप्तमे च
13.11.m: These two triplets are the Vālakhilyas on the sixth and on the seventh day.

13.11.s: yad etau vālakhilyau tṛcau bhavato 'hnor eva vyatiṣaṅgayāvyatisraṃsāya santatyai
13.11.d: यद् एतौ वालखिल्यौ तृचौ भवतो ऽह्नोर् एव व्यतिषङ्गयाव्यतिस्रंसाय सन्तत्यै
13.11.m: That there are these two Vālakhilya triplets is for the interlinking of the two days, for unloosening, for continuity.

13.11.s: somāḥ pavanta indava ity anuṣṭubho nibhasado bhavanti pratiṣṭhāyai
13.11.d: सोमाः पवन्त इन्दव इत्य् अनुष्टुभो निभसदो भवन्ति प्रतिष्ठायै
13.11.m: 'The somas, drops, purify themselves': these are anuṣṭubhs with broad seats, for a firm foundation.

13.11.s: ayā pavā pavasvainā vasūni iti triṣṭubhas satyo jagatyo rūpeṇa tasmāj jagatīnāṃ loke kriyante
13.11.d: अया पवा पवस्वैना वसूनि इति त्रिष्टुभस् सत्यो जगत्यो रूपेण तस्माज् जगतीनां लोके क्रियन्ते
13.11.m: 'With this [stream], clarify yourself, purify these goods': though being triṣṭubhs, they have the form of jagatīs; therefore they are performed in the place of jagatīs.

13.11.s: gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brahmāṇam
13.11.d: गायत्रं भवति यद् एव गायत्रस्य ब्रह्माणम्
13.11.m: There is the Gāyatra [sāman]; what belongs to the Gāyatra is the sacred power.

13.11.s: vaidanvātāni bhavanti
13.11.d: वैदन्वातानि भवन्ति
13.11.m: There are the Vaidanvata sāmans.

13.11.s: vidanvān vai bhārgava indrasya pratyahaṃs taṃ śug ārcchat sa tapo 'tapyata sa etāni vaidanvatāny apaśyat taiḥ śucam apāhatāpaśucaṃ hate vaidanvatais tuṣṭuvānaḥ
13.11.d: विदन्वान् वै भार्गव इन्द्रस्य प्रत्यहंस् तं शुग् आर्च्छत् स तपो ऽतप्यत स एतानि वैदन्वतान्य् अपश्यत् तैः शुचम् अपाहतापशुचं हते वैदन्वतैस् तुष्टुवानः
13.11.m: Vidanvat Bhārgava contradicted Indra; grief came upon him. He performed ascetic heat; he saw these Vaidanvata sāmans. With them he drove away his grief; having praised with the Vaidanvata sāmans, he drives away his grief.

13.11.s: bharadvājasya lomata bhavati
13.11.d: भरद्वाजस्य लोमत भवति
13.11.m: There is the Loma of Bharadvāja.

13.11.s: paśavo vai loma paśūnām avarudhyai
13.11.d: पशवो वै लोम पशूनाम् अवरुध्यै
13.11.m: Hair (loma) is cattle; [it is] for the obtainment of cattle.

13.11.s: tad u dīrgham ity āhur āyur vai dīrgham āyuṣo 'varudhyai
13.11.d: तद् उ दीर्घम् इत्य् आहुर् आयुर् वै दीर्घम् आयुषो ऽवरुध्यै
13.11.m: And they also call it long (dīrgha); life-span (āyus) is long; [it is] for the obtainment of life-span.

13.11.s: kārṇaśravasaṃ bhavati śṛṇvanti tuṣṭuvānam
13.11.d: कार्णश्रवसं भवति शृण्वन्ति तुष्टुवानम्
13.11.m: There is the Kārṇaśravasa sāman; they listen to him who has praised.

13.11.s: karṇaśravā vā etad āṅigarasaḥ paśukāmaḥ sāmāpaśyat tena sahasraṃ paśūn asṛjata yad etat sāma bhavati paśūnāṃ puṣṭyai
13.11.d: कर्णश्रवा वा एतद् आङिगरसः पशुकामः सामापश्यत् तेन सहस्रं पशून् असृजत यद् एतत् साम भवति पशूनां पुष्ट्यै
13.11.m: Karṇaśravas Āṅgirasa, desiring cattle, saw this sāman. By it he produced a thousand cattle. That this sāman is used is for the flourishing of cattle.

13.11.s: gaurīvitaṃ bhavati gaurivitasya brāhmaṇam
13.11.d: गौरीवितं भवति गौरिवितस्य ब्राह्मणम्
13.11.m: There is the Gaurīvita sāman; [this has] the brāhmaṇa of the Gaurīvita.

13.11.s: madhuścyunnidhanaṃ bhavati
13.11.d: मधुश्च्युन्निधनं भवति
13.11.m: There is a cadence dripping with honey.

13.11.s: paramasyānnādyasyāvarudhyai paramaṃ vā etad annādya yan madhu
13.11.d: परमस्यान्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै परमं वा एतद् अन्नाद्य यन् मधु
13.11.m: [It is] for the obtainment of the highest food; for honey is this highest food.

13.11.s: prajāpater vā etau stanau yad ghṛtaścyunnidhanaṃ ca madhuścyunnidhanaṃ ca yajño vai prajāpatis tam etābhyāṃ dugdhe yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate taṃ dugdhe
13.11.d: प्रजापतेर् वा एतौ स्तनौ यद् घृतश्च्युन्निधनं च मधुश्च्युन्निधनं च यज्ञो वै प्रजापतिस् तम् एताभ्यां दुग्धे यं कामं कामयते तं दुग्धे
13.11.m: These two udders of Prajāpati are that cadence dripping with ghee and that cadence dripping with honey. The sacrifice is Prajāpati; he milks it through these two; whatever desire he desires, that he milks.

13.11.s: krauñce bhavataḥ
13.11.d: क्रौञ्चे भवतः

13.11.s: śnauṣṭhaṃ bhavati
13.11.d: श्नौष्ठं भवति

13.11.s: śnuṣṭir vā etenāṅgiraso 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāt lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
13.11.d: श्नुष्टिर् वा एतेनाङ्गिरसो ऽञ्जसा स्वर्गं लोकम् अपश्यत् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्यानुख्यात्यै स्वर्गात् लोकान् न च्यवते तुष्टुवानः
13.11.m: By this Śnuṣṭi Āṅgirasa directly saw the world of heaven; [it is] for the perceiving of the heavenly world; he who has praised does not fall from the world of heaven.

13.11.s: agner vā etad vaiśvānaraṃ sāma dīdihīti nidhanam upayanti dīdā eva hy agnir vaiśvānaraḥ
13.11.d: अग्नेर् वा एतद् वैश्वानरं साम दीदिहीति निधनम् उपयन्ति दीदा एव ह्य् अग्निर् वैश्वानरः
13.11.m: This is the Vaiśvānara sāman of Agni. They use 'dīdihi' ('shine bright') as the cadence; for Agni Vaiśvānara is indeed shining.

13.11.s: nidhanāntāḥ pavamānā bhavanty ahno dhṛtyai stomaḥ
13.11.d: निधनान्ताः पवमाना भवन्त्य् अह्नो धृत्यै स्तोमः
13.11.m: The pavamāna [lauds] end in cadences for the firm support of the day. [Such is] the stoma.

13.12.s: brahmavādino vadanti prāyaṇato dvipadāḥ kāryā udayanatā3 iti
13.12.d: ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति प्रायणतो द्विपदाः कार्या उदयनता3 इति
13.12.m: The theologians say: 'Should two-footed [verses] be used at the beginning or at the conclusion?'

13.12.s: udayanata eva kāryāḥ puruṣo vai dvipadāḥ pratiṣṭhāyai
13.12.d: उदयनत एव कार्याः पुरुषो वै द्विपदाः प्रतिष्ठायै
13.12.m: They should be used only at the conclusion. Man is two-footed; [it is] for a firm foundation.

13.12.s: vācā vai sarvaṃ yajñaṃ tanvate tasmāt sarvāṃ vācaṃ puruṣo vadati sarvā hy asmin saṃstutā pratitiṣṭhati
13.12.d: वाचा वै सर्वं यज्ञं तन्वते तस्मात् सर्वां वाचं पुरुषो वदति सर्वा ह्य् अस्मिन् संस्तुता प्रतितिष्ठति
13.12.m: They perform the entire sacrifice with speech; therefore, man speaks all speech; for when fully praised, all [speech] is established in him.

13.12.s: gopāyanānāṃ vai sattram āsīnānāṃ kirātakulyāv asuramāye antaḥparidhy asūn prākiratāṃ te agre tvan no antama ity agnim upāsīdaṃs tenāsūn aspṛṇvaṃs tad vāva te tarhy akāmayanta kāmasani sāma gūrdaḥ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
13.12.d: गोपायनानां वै सत्त्रम् आसीनानां किरातकुल्याव् असुरमाये अन्तःपरिध्य् असून् प्राकिरतां ते अग्रे त्वन् नो अन्तम इत्य् अग्निम् उपासीदंस् तेनासून् अस्पृण्वंस् तद् वाव ते तर्ह्य् अकामयन्त कामसनि साम गूर्दः कामम् एवैतेनावरुन्धे
13.12.m: When the Gopāyanas were performing a sacrificial session, Kirāta and Ākuli, using Asura-magic, scattered their life-breaths inside the enclosing sticks. They approached Agni with 'Agni, be nearest to us'; thereby they saved their life-breaths. That indeed is what they then desired. The Gūrda sāman wins desires; by this he obtains desire.
There is the Bhanda sāman of Gotama.

13.12.s: āśiṣam evāsmā etenāśāste sāma hi satyāśīḥ
13.12.d: आशिषम् एवास्मा एतेनाशास्ते साम हि सत्याशीः
13.12.m: Thereby he invokes a blessing for him; for the sāman is a true blessing.

13.12.s: etena vai gotamo jemānaṃ mahimānam agacchat tasmād ye ca parāñco gotamād ye cārvāñcas ta ubhaye gotamā ṛṣayo bruvate
13.12.d: एतेन वै गोतमो जेमानं महिमानम् अगच्छत् तस्माद् ये च पराञ्चो गोतमाद् ये चार्वाञ्चस् त उभये गोतमा ऋषयो ब्रुवते
13.12.m: By this Gotama attained triumphant greatness; therefore, both those who are further and those who are nearer from Gotama call themselves Gotama sages.
What is the Udvaṃśīya, that is the Udvaṃśaputra.

13.12.s: tasmād ūdhardhārā ati carantīḍāyām antataḥ paśuṣu pratitiṣṭhati
13.12.d: तस्माद् ऊधर्धारा अति चरन्तीडायाम् अन्ततः पशुषु प्रतितिष्ठति
13.12.m: Therefore, streams go beyond the udder; in the end he finds a firm foundation in cattle at the iḍā.

13.12.s: kḷpta upariṣṭād ṛk sāma ca vimucyete abhy u svareṇa saptamam ahaḥ svarati santatyai
13.12.d: कॢप्त उपरिष्टाद् ऋक् साम च विमुच्येते अभ्य् उ स्वरेण सप्तमम् अहः स्वरति सन्तत्यै
13.12.m: Arranged above, the verse and the sāman are unyoked; and with the sound he intones towards the seventh day for continuity.

13.12.s: ūhuṣīva vā etarhi vāg yadā ṣaḍahaḥ santiṣṭhate na bahu vaden nānyaṃ pṛcchen nānyasmai prabrūyāt
13.12.d: ऊहुषीव वा एतर्हि वाग् यदा षडहः सन्तिष्ठते न बहु वदेन् नान्यं पृच्छेन् नान्यस्मै प्रब्रूयात्
13.12.m: Speech is as it were exhausted when the six-day rite concludes. He should not speak much, he should not ask another, he should not tell another.

13.12.s: madhu vāśayed ghṛtaṃ vā yathehuṣo bahaṃ pratyanakti tathā tat
13.12.d: मधु वाशयेद् घृतं वा यथेहुषो बहं प्रत्यनक्ति तथा तत्
13.12.m: He should eat honey or ghee; just as one anoints the shoulder of an ox that has drawn [a load], so is that.

13.12.s: trayastriṃśa eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai devatāsu vā eṣa pratiṣṭhitaḥ
13.12.d: त्रयस्त्रिंश एव स्तोमो भवति प्रतिष्ठायै देवतासु वा एष प्रतिष्ठितः
13.12.m: The stoma is the thirty-three-fold stoma alone, for a firm foundation; it is established among the deities.

14.1.s: āpyante vā etat stomāś chandāṃsi yat ṣaḍaha āpyate
14.1.d: आप्यन्ते वा एतत् स्तोमाश् छन्दांसि यत् षडह आप्यते
14.1.m: The stomas and metres are reached when the six-day rite is reached.

14.1.s: āpte ṣaḍahe chandāṃsi stomān kṛtvā prayanti
14.1.d: आप्ते षडहे छन्दांसि स्तोमान् कृत्वा प्रयन्ति
14.1.m: When the six-day rite is reached, they go forth making the metres into the stomas.

14.1.s: pra kāvyam uśanevara bruvāṇa iti gāyatryā rūpeṇa prayanti
14.1.d: प्र काव्यम् उशनेवर ब्रुवाण इति गायत्र्या रूपेण प्रयन्ति
14.1.m: 'Uttering wisdom like Uśanā', thus they go forth in the form of the gāyatrī.

14.1.s: iyaṃ vai gāyatry asyām eva pratiṣṭhāya prayanti
14.1.d: इयं वै गायत्र्य् अस्याम् एव प्रतिष्ठाय प्रयन्ति
14.1.m: This [earth] is the gāyatrī; having established themselves on this very [earth], they go forth.
The introductory verse is a triṣṭubh.

14.1.s: ojo vīryaṃ triṣṭubojasyeva vīrye parākramya prayanti
14.1.d: ओजो वीर्यं त्रिष्टुबोजस्येव वीर्ये पराक्रम्य प्रयन्ति
14.1.m: The triṣṭubh is force and heroic strength; having exerted themselves, as it were, in force and heroic strength, they go forth.
The chant of praise is a triplet, for the retention of out-breaths and in-breaths.
There are [verses] containing the word 'hari' ('bay/golden'), so that the chandomas do not become exhausted.

14.1.s: dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaram eva tatpūrvasmai ṣaḍahāya pratyudyacchati savīvadhatāyai
14.1.d: द्वादश मासाः संवत्सरः संवत्सरम् एव तत्पूर्वस्मै षडहाय प्रत्युद्यच्छति सवीवधतायै
14.1.m: The year consists of twelve months. He raises up the year against the preceding six-day rite, to form a carrying pole.

14.1.s: caturviṃśatir bhavanti caturviṃśatir ardhamāsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaram eva tatpūrvasmai ṣaḍahāya pratyudyacchati savīvadhatāyai
14.1.d: चतुर्विंशतिर् भवन्ति चतुर्विंशतिर् अर्धमासाः संवत्सरः संवत्सरम् एव तत्पूर्वस्मै षडहाय प्रत्युद्यच्छति सवीवधतायै
14.1.m: There are twenty-four [verses]; the year consists of twenty-four half-months. He raises up the year against the preceding six-day rite, to form a carrying pole.

14.1.s: dṛta aindrota iti hovācābhipratārī kākṣasenir ye mahāvṛkṣasyāgraṃ gacchanti ka te tato bhavanti prarājan pakṣiṇaḥ patanty avāpakṣāḥ padyante
14.1.d: दृत ऐन्द्रोत इति होवाचाभिप्रतारी काक्षसेनिर् ये महावृक्षस्याग्रं गच्छन्ति क ते ततो भवन्ति प्रराजन् पक्षिणः पतन्त्य् अवापक्षाः पद्यन्ते
14.1.m: Dṛta Aindrota—so said Abhipratārin Kākṣaseni—'Those who go to the top of a great tree, what becomes of them from there, O king? Birds fly off; the wingless fall down.'

14.1.s: ye vai vidvāṃsas te pakṣiṇo ye 'vidvāṃsas te 'pakṣās trivṛt pañcadaśāv eva stomau pakṣau kṛtvā svarga lokaṃ prayanti
14.1.d: ये वै विद्वांसस् ते पक्षिणो ये ऽविद्वांसस् ते ऽपक्षास् त्रिवृत् पञ्चदशाव् एव स्तोमौ पक्षौ कृत्वा स्वर्ग लोकं प्रयन्ति
14.1.m: Those who are wise are winged; those who are unwise are wingless. Having made the ninefold stoma and fifteenfold stoma their wings, they go forth to the world of heaven.

14.1.s: caturviṃśa eva stomo bhavati teja se brahmavarcasāya
14.1.d: चतुर्विंश एव स्तोमो भवति तेज से ब्रह्मवर्चसाय
14.1.m: The stoma is the twenty-four-fold [stoma], for splendour, for brahminical lustre.

14.2.s: mūrdhānaṃ divo aratim pṛthivyā ity āgreyam ājyaṃ bhavati
14.2.d: मूर्धानं दिवो अरतिम् पृथिव्या इत्य् आग्रेयम् आज्यं भवति
14.2.m: The ājyastotra addressed to Agni is [the triplet beginning]: "The head of heaven, the navel of the earth…"

14.2.s: mūrdhā vā eṣa divo yas tṛtīyas trirātraḥ
14.2.d: मूर्धा वा एष दिवो यस् तृतीयस् त्रिरात्रः
14.2.m: This head of heaven is the third three-day period.

14.2.s: vaiśvānaram ṛta ājātam agnim iti vaiśvānara iti vā agneḥ priyaṃ dhāma priyeṇaivainaṃ tad dhāmnā parokṣam upaśikṣati
14.2.d: वैश्वानरम् ऋत आजातम् अग्निम् इति वैश्वानर इति वा अग्नेः प्रियं धाम प्रियेणैवैनं तद् धाम्ना परोक्षम् उपशिक्षति
14.2.m: "[Agni] Vaiśvānara, born of the cosmic order"—Vaiśvānara is indeed Agni’s dear domain; by means of his dear domain he thus serves him indirectly.

14.2.s: pra vo mitrāya gāyata iti dyāvāpṛthivīyaṃ maitrāvaruṇaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī vai mitrāvaruṇayoḥ priyaṃ dhāma priyeṇaivainau tad dhāmnā parokṣam upaśikṣati
14.2.d: प्र वो मित्राय गायत इति द्यावापृथिवीयं मैत्रावरुणं द्यावापृथिवी वै मित्रावरुणयोः प्रियं धाम प्रियेणैवैनौ तद् धाम्ना परोक्षम् उपशिक्षति
14.2.m: "Sing forth to Mitra [and Varuṇa]…"—this [is the triplet] addressed to Heaven and Earth, belonging to the Maitrāvaruṇa; Heaven and Earth are indeed the dear domain of Mitra and Varuṇa; by means of their dear domain he thus serves them indirectly.

14.2.s: indrāyāhi citrabhānav ity ārbhavam aindram ṛbhavo vā indrasya priyaṃ dhāma priyeṇaivainaṃ tad dhāmnā parokṣam upaśikṣati
14.2.d: इन्द्रायाहि चित्रभानव् इत्य् आर्भवम् ऐन्द्रम् ऋभवो वा इन्द्रस्य प्रियं धाम प्रियेणैवैनं तद् धाम्ना परोक्षम् उपशिक्षति
14.2.m: "Come, O Indra, of wondrous splendour…"—this [is the triplet] addressed to the Ṛbhus, belonging to Indra; the Ṛbhus are indeed Indra's dear domain; by means of his dear domain he thus serves him indirectly.

14.2.s: tam īḍiṣva yo arciṣā ity aniruktam aindrāgnaṃ devatānām anabhidharṣāyottamārdhe 'nirāha devatānām apraṇāśāya stomaḥ
14.2.d: तम् ईडिष्व यो अर्चिषा इत्य् अनिरुक्तम् ऐन्द्राग्नं देवतानाम् अनभिधर्षायोत्तमार्धे ऽनिराह देवतानाम् अप्रणाशाय स्तोमः
14.2.m: "Praise him who with flame…"—this [is the triplet] belonging to Indra and Agni, unexpressed, so as not to overpower the deities; in the latter half he does not express it, so that the deities may not be lost, [thus is] the stoma.

14.3.s: vṛṣā pavasva dhāraya iti gāyatrī bhavaty ahno dhṛtyai
14.3.d: वृषा पवस्व धारय इति गायत्री भवत्य् अह्नो धृत्यै
14.3.m: "Flow as a bull with a stream…"—this is in the gāyatrī [metre], for the support of the day.

14.3.s: vṛṣaṇvatyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa traiṣṭubhaṃ hy etad ahaḥ
14.3.d: वृषण्वत्यस् त्रिष्टुभो रूपेण त्रैष्टुभं ह्य् एतद् अहः
14.3.m: [The verses] contain the word 'bull', in the form of the triṣṭubh; for this day belongs to the triṣṭubh.

14.3.s: punānaḥ soma dhāraya iti dhṛtyai
14.3.d: पुनानः सोम धारय इति धृत्यै
14.3.m: "Purifying yourself, O Soma, with a stream…"—[this is] for support.

14.3.s: pro ayāsīd indur indrasya niṣkṛtam iti pravatyo bhavanti praṇinīṣeṇyam iva hy etad ahaḥ
14.3.d: प्रो अयासीद् इन्दुर् इन्द्रस्य निष्कृतम् इति प्रवत्यो भवन्ति प्रणिनीषेण्यम् इव ह्य् एतद् अहः
14.3.m: "The drop has gone forth to Indra's rendezvous"—these [verses] contain the word 'forth'; for this day is, as it were, to be led forth.

14.3.s: jagatyaḥ satyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa tasmāt triṣṭubhāṃ loke kriyante
14.3.d: जगत्यः सत्यस् त्रिष्टुभो रूपेण तस्मात् त्रिष्टुभां लोके क्रियन्ते
14.3.m: Being jagatīs, they are in the form of the triṣṭubh; therefore they are performed in the place of the triṣṭubhs.

14.3.s: santani bhavati saptamasyāhnaḥ santatyai
14.3.d: सन्तनि भवति सप्तमस्याह्नः सन्तत्यै
14.3.m: There is the Santani [sāman], for the continuity of the seventh day.

14.3.s: yathā vai vyokasau vipradravata evam ete ṣaṣṭhaṃ cāhaḥ saptamaṃ ca vipradravatas tau yathā samānīya saṃyujyād evam evaite etena sāmnā saṃyunakti
14.3.d: यथा वै व्योकसौ विप्रद्रवत एवम् एते षष्ठं चाहः सप्तमं च विप्रद्रवतस् तौ यथा समानीय संयुज्याद् एवम् एवैते एतेन साम्ना संयुनक्ति
14.3.m: Just as two creatures lacking a common home run apart, so these two, the sixth day and the seventh day, run apart; just as one would bring them together and yoke them, even so does he yoke these two with this sāman.

14.3.s: yajño vai devebhyo 'pākrāmat sa suparṇarūpaṃ kṛtvācarat taṃ devā etaiḥ sāmabhirārabhanta yajña iva vā eṣa yac chandomā yajñasyaivaiṣa ārambhaḥ
14.3.d: यज्ञो वै देवेभ्यो ऽपाक्रामत् स सुपर्णरूपं कृत्वाचरत् तं देवा एतैः सामभिरारभन्त यज्ञ इव वा एष यच् छन्दोमा यज्ञस्यैवैष आरम्भः
14.3.m: The sacrifice departed from the gods; having assumed the form of an eagle, it flew about. The gods seized it by means of these sāmans. The sacrifice, as it were, is what the Chandomas are; this is the very seizing of the sacrifice.

14.3.s: rohitakūlīyaṃ bhavaty ājijityāyai
14.3.d: रोहितकूलीयं भवत्य् आजिजित्यायै
14.3.m: The Rohitakūlīya [sāman] is used, for winning the race.

14.3.s: etena vai viśvāmitro rohitābhyāṃ rohitakūla ājim ajayat
14.3.d: एतेन वै विश्वामित्रो रोहिताभ्यां रोहितकूल आजिम् अजयत्
14.3.m: By this [sāman] Viśvāmitra, with two red mares, won the race at Rohitakūla.

14.3.s: viśvāmitro bharatānāṃ manassatyāyāt so 'dantibhir nāma janatayāṃśaṃ prāsyate māṃ māṃ yūyaṃ astikāṃ jayāthemāni mahyaṃ yūyaṃ pūrayātha yadīmāv idaṃ rohitāv aśmācitaṃ kūlam udvahāta iti sa ete sāmanī apaśyat tābhyāṃ yuktvā prāsedhat sa udjayat
14.3.d: विश्वामित्रो भरतानां मनस्सत्यायात् सो ऽदन्तिभिर् नाम जनतयांशं प्रास्यते मां मां यूयं अस्तिकां जयाथेमानि मह्यं यूयं पूरयाथ यदीमाव् इदं रोहिताव् अश्माचितं कूलम् उद्वहात इति स एते सामनी अपश्यत् ताभ्यां युक्त्वा प्रासेधत् स उद्जयत्
14.3.m: Viśvāmitra went to the Bharatas for the fulfilment of a wish. He was about to cast lots with a people called the Adantis: "Do not conquer me! Fill these [stakes] for me, if these two red mares will carry [my chariot] up this bank heaped with stones!" He saw these two sāmans; having yoked [his chariot] with them, he drove on; he won.

14.3.s: ājir vā eṣa pratato yad dvādaśāhas tasyaite ujjityai
14.3.d: आजिर् वा एष प्रततो यद् द्वादशाहस् तस्यैते उज्जित्यै
14.3.m: This twelve-day rite is an extended race; these [sāmans] are for winning it.

14.3.s: kaṇvarathantaraṃ bhavati tejo vā etad rathantarasya yat kaṇvarathantaram
14.3.d: कण्वरथन्तरं भवति तेजो वा एतद् रथन्तरस्य यत् कण्वरथन्तरम्
14.3.m: The Kaṇvarathantara [sāman] is used; the Kaṇvarathantara is the splendour of the Rathantara.

14.3.s: sarasam eva tad rathantaraṃ prayuṅkte yat kaṇvarathantareṇa saptame 'hani stuvate
14.3.d: सरसम् एव तद् रथन्तरं प्रयुङ्क्ते यत् कण्वरथन्तरेण सप्तमे ऽहनि स्तुवते
14.3.m: Full of sap, indeed, he employs the Rathantara when they praise with the Kaṇvarathantara on the seventh day.

14.3.s: jāmi dvādaśāhasyāstīti ha smāhogradevo rājanir bārhataṃ ṣaṣṭham ahar bārhataṃ saptamaṃ yat kaṇvarathantaraṃ bhavati tenājāmi
14.3.d: जामि द्वादशाहस्यास्तीति ह स्माहोग्रदेवो राजनिर् बार्हतं षष्ठम् अहर् बार्हतं सप्तमं यत् कण्वरथन्तरं भवति तेनाजामि
14.3.m: "There is tautology in the twelve-day rite," Ugradeva Rājani used to say; "the sixth day is connected with the Bṛhat, the seventh day is connected with the Bṛhat. That there is the Kaṇvarathantara, thereby there is variation."

14.3.s: gauṅgavaṃ bhavati
14.3.d: गौङ्गवं भवति

14.3.s: agnir akāmayatānnādaḥ syām iti sa tapo 'tapyata sa etad gauṅgavam apaśyat tenānnādo 'bhavad yad annaṃ vitvā gardadyad agaṅgūyat tad gauṅgavasya gauṅgavatvam annādyasyāvarudhyai gauṅgavaṃ kiyate
14.3.d: अग्निर् अकामयतान्नादः स्याम् इति स तपो ऽतप्यत स एतद् गौङ्गवम् अपश्यत् तेनान्नादो ऽभवद् यद् अन्नं वित्वा गर्दद्यद् अगङ्गूयत् तद् गौङ्गवस्य गौङ्गवत्वम् अन्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै गौङ्गवं कियते
14.3.m: Agni desired: "May I be an eater of food." He performed ascetic heat; he saw this Gauṅgava; by it he became an eater of food. Because, having found food, he roared (agardat), because he gurgled (agaṅgūyat), that is the Gauṅgava-nature of the Gauṅgava. The Gauṅgava is performed for the acquisition of food.

14.3.s: yat sāma devatā praśaṃyati tena yajamānāḥ satyāśiṣaḥ satyāśiṣo 'sāmeti vai sattram āsate satyāśiṣa eva bhavanti
14.3.d: यत् साम देवता प्रशंयति तेन यजमानाः सत्याशिषः सत्याशिषो ऽसामेति वै सत्त्रम् आसते सत्याशिष एव भवन्ति
14.3.m: Because the deity praises the sāman, thereby the sacrificers have their wishes fulfilled. "May we have our wishes fulfilled," thus they sit at the sacrificial session; they truly have their wishes fulfilled.

14.3.s: āyāsyaṃ bhavati tiraścīnanidhanaṃ pratiṣṭhāyai
14.3.d: आयास्यं भवति तिरश्चीननिधनं प्रतिष्ठायै
14.3.m: The Āyāsya [sāman] is used, with a transverse cadence, for a firm foundation.

14.3.s: ayāsyo vā āṅgirasa ādityānāṃ dīkṣitānām annam āśnāt sa vyabhraṃśata sa etāny āyāsyāny apaśyat tair ātmānaṃ samaśrīṇād vibhraṣṭam iva vai saptamam ahar yad etat sāma bhavaty ahar eva tena saṃśrīṇāti
14.3.d: अयास्यो वा आङ्गिरस आदित्यानां दीक्षितानाम् अन्नम् आश्नात् स व्यभ्रंशत स एतान्य् आयास्यान्य् अपश्यत् तैर् आत्मानं समश्रीणाद् विभ्रष्टम् इव वै सप्तमम् अहर् यद् एतत् साम भवत्य् अहर् एव तेन संश्रीणाति
14.3.m: Ayāsya Āṅgirasa ate the food of the consecrated Ādityas; he fell away. He saw these Āyāsya [sāmans]; with them he restored himself. The seventh day is, as it were, fallen away; that this sāman is used, he thereby restores the day.

14.3.s: pravadbhargavaṃ bhavati
14.3.d: प्रवद्भर्गवं भवति
14.3.m: The Pravadbhārgava [sāman] is used.

14.4.s: vayaṃ ghatvā sutāvanta iti bṛhatyo varṣīyaśchanda ākramate 'napabhraṃśāya
14.4.d: वयं घत्वा सुतावन्त इति बृहत्यो वर्षीयश्छन्द आक्रमते ऽनपभ्रंशाय
14.4.m: "We [approach] you, who have the pressed juice…"—these are bṛhatīs; he mounts a higher metre, for avoiding a fall.

14.4.s: nakiṣ ṭaṃ karmaṇā naśad iti bṛhatyaḥ satyo 'bhyārambheṇa jagatyaḥ
14.4.d: नकिष् टं कर्मणा नशद् इति बृहत्यः सत्यो ऽभ्यारम्भेण जगत्यः
14.4.m: "No one shall attain it by work…"—these, being bṛhatīs, are jagatīs by repetition.

14.4.s: apabhraṃśa iva vā eṣa yaj jyāyasaḥ stomāt kanīyāṃsaṃ stomam upayanti yad etā abhyārambheṇa jagatyo bhavanty ahna eva pratyuttambhāya
14.4.d: अपभ्रंश इव वा एष यज् ज्यायसः स्तोमात् कनीयांसं स्तोमम् उपयन्ति यद् एता अभ्यारम्भेण जगत्यो भवन्त्य् अह्न एव प्रत्युत्तम्भाय
14.4.m: It is, as it were, a falling down when they go from a greater stoma to a lesser stoma; that these become jagatīs by repetition is for propping up the day.

14.4.s: abhinidhanena vā indro vṛtrāya vajraṃ prāharat tam astṛṇuta stṛṇute bhrātṛvyam abhinidhanena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
14.4.d: अभिनिधनेन वा इन्द्रो वृत्राय वज्रं प्राहरत् तम् अस्तृणुत स्तृणुते भ्रातृव्यम् अभिनिधनेन तुष्टुवानः
14.4.m: With the Abhinidhana Indra hurled the thunderbolt at Vṛtra; he laid him low. He who has praised with the Abhinidhana lays low his rival.

14.4.s: vaikhānasā vā ṛṣaya indrasya priyā āsaṃs tān rahasyur devamalimluḍ munimaraṇe 'mārayat taṃ devā abruvan kva tarṣayo 'bhūvānn iti tān praiṣam aicchat tān nāvindat sa imān lokān ekadhāreṇāpunāt tān munimaraṇe 'vindat tān etena sāmnā samairayat tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sāma vaikhānasaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe stomaḥ
14.4.d: वैखानसा वा ऋषय इन्द्रस्य प्रिया आसंस् तान् रहस्युर् देवमलिम्लुड् मुनिमरणे ऽमारयत् तं देवा अब्रुवन् क्व तर्षयो ऽभूवान्न् इति तान् प्रैषम् ऐच्छत् तान् नाविन्दत् स इमान् लोकान् एकधारेणापुनात् तान् मुनिमरणे ऽविन्दत् तान् एतेन साम्ना समैरयत् तद् वाव स तर्ह्य् अकामयत कामसनि साम वैखानसं कामम् एवैतेनावरुन्धे स्तोमः
14.4.m: The Vaikhānasa seers were dear to Indra. Rahasyu Devamalimluc killed them at Munimaraṇa. The gods said to him: "Where have the seers gone?" He sought them out; he did not find them. He purified these worlds with a single stream; he found them at Munimaraṇa. He revived them with this sāman. That is what he then desired. The Vaikhānasa is a wish-granting sāman; he secures his wish by it; [such is] the stoma.

14.5.s: yas te mado vareṇya iti gāyatrī bhavati madavad vai rasavat tṛtīyasavanaṃ madam eva tad rasaṃ dadhāti
14.5.d: यस् ते मदो वरेण्य इति गायत्री भवति मदवद् वै रसवत् तृतीयसवनं मदम् एव तद् रसं दधाति
14.5.m: "That exhilarating draught of yours which is the best…"—this is in the gāyatrī [metre]; exhilarating, full of sap is the third pressing; he thus puts exhilarating sap into it.

14.5.s: eṣasya dhārayā suta iti kakubhaḥ satyo 'bhyārambheṇa triṣṭubhaḥ
14.5.d: एषस्य धारया सुत इति ककुभः सत्यो ऽभ्यारम्भेण त्रिष्टुभः
14.5.m: "This [Soma] pressed in a stream…"—these, being kakubhs, are triṣṭubhs by repetition.

14.5.s: apabhraṃśa iva vā eṣa yat jyāyasaḥ stomāt kanīyāṃsaṃ stomam upayanti yad etā abhyārambheṇa triṣṭubho bhavanty ahna eva pratyuttambhāya
14.5.d: अपभ्रंश इव वा एष यत् ज्यायसः स्तोमात् कनीयांसं स्तोमम् उपयन्ति यद् एता अभ्यारम्भेण त्रिष्टुभो भवन्त्य् अह्न एव प्रत्युत्तम्भाय
14.5.m: It is, as it were, a falling down when they go from a greater stoma to a lesser stoma; that these become triṣṭubhs by repetition is for propping up the day.

14.5.s: sakhāya āniṣīdata iti vālakhilyā vālakhilyāv etau tṛcau ṣaṣṭhe cāhani saptame ca yad etau vākhilyau tṛcau bhavato 'hnor eva vyatiṣaṅgāyāvyavasraṃsāya santatyai
14.5.d: सखाय आनिषीदत इति वालखिल्या वालखिल्याव् एतौ तृचौ षष्ठे चाहनि सप्तमे च यद् एतौ वाखिल्यौ तृचौ भवतो ऽह्नोर् एव व्यतिषङ्गायाव्यवस्रंसाय सन्तत्यै
14.5.m: "O friends, sit down…"—these are the Vālakhilyā [verses]; these two triplets on the sixth day and on the seventh day are Vālakhilyās; that these two triplets are Vālakhilyās is for the interlinking of the two days, for avoiding slipping down, for continuity.

14.5.s: purojitī vo andhasa iti virāḍ annaṃ virāḍ annādyasyāvarudhyai
14.5.d: पुरोजिती वो अन्धस इति विराड् अन्नं विराड् अन्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै
14.5.m: "Conquering in the beginning, for your drink…"—this is the virāj; the virāj is food; [it is] for the acquisition of food.

14.5.s: pra vājy akṣār ity akṣarapaṅktiḥ stomānāṃ prabhūtiḥ
14.5.d: प्र वाज्य् अक्षार् इत्य् अक्षरपङ्क्तिः स्तोमानां प्रभूतिः
14.5.m: "Forth flowed the courser…"—this is the akṣarapaṅkti, the abundance of the stomas.

14.5.s: atho etad dhy evaitarhi chando 'yātayāma yad akṣarapaṅktis tena chandomā ayātayāmānaḥ kriyante
14.5.d: अथो एतद् ध्य् एवैतर्हि छन्दो ऽयातयाम यद् अक्षरपङ्क्तिस् तेन छन्दोमा अयातयामानः क्रियन्ते
14.5.m: Moreover, this metre, the akṣarapaṅkti, is unexhausted at this point; thereby the Chandomas are made unexhausted.

14.5.s: brahmavādino vadanti yat ṣaḍahe stomāś chandāṃsy āpyante kiṃ chandasaś chandomā ity etac chandaso yad etā akṣarapaṅktaya iti brūyāt
14.5.d: ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति यत् षडहे स्तोमाश् छन्दांस्य् आप्यन्ते किं छन्दसश् छन्दोमा इत्य् एतच् छन्दसो यद् एता अक्षरपङ्क्तय इति ब्रूयात्
14.5.m: The theologians say: "Since the stomas and the metres are exhausted in the six-day period, of what metre are the Chandomas?" One should say: "Of this metre, that they are these akṣarapaṅktis."

14.5.s: ye somāsaḥ parāvati iti parāvatam iva vā etarhi yajño gatas tam evaitenānvicchanti
14.5.d: ये सोमासः परावति इति परावतम् इव वा एतर्हि यज्ञो गतस् तम् एवैतेनान्विच्छन्ति
14.5.m: "The Somas that are far away…"—the sacrifice, as it were, has gone far away at this point; it is that which they seek after with this.

14.5.s: dakṣaṇidhanaṃ bhavati
14.5.d: दक्षणिधनं भवति
14.5.m: The Dakṣanidhana [sāman] is used.

14.5.s: prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tā asmāt sṛṣṭā abalā ivācchadayaṃs tāsv etena sāmnā dakṣāyety ojo vīryam adadhād yad etat sāma bhavaty oja eva vīryam ātman dhatte
14.5.d: प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत ता अस्मात् सृष्टा अबला इवाच्छदयंस् तास्व् एतेन साम्ना दक्षायेत्य् ओजो वीर्यम् अदधाद् यद् एतत् साम भवत्य् ओज एव वीर्यम् आत्मन् धत्ते
14.5.m: Prajāpati created creatures; created from him, they seemed weak. Into them, with this sāman, [saying] "For strength (dakṣāya)", he placed vigour and valour. That this sāman is used, he places vigour and valour in himself.

14.5.s: śārkaraṃ bhavati
14.5.d: शार्करं भवति

14.5.s: indraṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāny astuvan sa śarkaraṃ śiśumārarṣim upetyābravīt stuhi meti so 'paḥ praskandann abravīd etāvato 'haṃ tvāṃ stuyām iti tasmād apāṃ vegam avejayat sa hīna ivāmanyata sa etat sāmāpaśyat tenāpo 'nusamāśnuta tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sāma śārkaraṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
14.5.d: इन्द्रं सर्वाणि भूतान्य् अस्तुवन् स शर्करं शिशुमारर्षिम् उपेत्याब्रवीत् स्तुहि मेति सो ऽपः प्रस्कन्दन्न् अब्रवीद् एतावतो ऽहं त्वां स्तुयाम् इति तस्माद् अपां वेगम् अवेजयत् स हीन इवामन्यत स एतत् सामापश्यत् तेनापो ऽनुसमाश्नुत तद् वाव स तर्ह्य् अकामयत कामसनि साम शार्करं कामम् एवैतेनावरुन्धे
14.5.m: All beings praised Indra. He approached Śarkara, the dolphin-seer, and said, 'Praise me.' Leaping into the waters, he said, 'From as much [water as this] may I praise you.' Therefore he shook the rush of the waters. He considered himself as though left behind. He saw this sāman; by it he pervaded the waters. Truly that was what he desired at that time. The Śārkara sāman is wish-granting; he obtains [his] desire by it.

14.5.s: plavo bhavati
14.5.d: प्लवो भवति

14.5.s: samudraṃ vā ete prasnāntīty āhur ye dvādaśāham upayantīti yo vā aplavaḥ samudraṃ prarunāti na sa tata udeti yata plavo bhavati svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai
14.5.d: समुद्रं वा एते प्रस्नान्तीत्य् आहुर् ये द्वादशाहम् उपयन्तीति यो वा अप्लवः समुद्रं प्ररुनाति न स तत उदेति यत प्लवो भवति स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्ट्यै
14.5.m: They say: 'Those who undertake the twelve-day rite bathe across the ocean.' He who crosses the ocean without a boat (plava) does not emerge from it. That there is the Plava is for attaining the heavenly world.

14.5.s: ativiśvāni duritā taremeti yad evaiṣāṃ duṣṭutaṃ duśśastaṃ tad etena taranti
14.5.d: अतिविश्वानि दुरिता तरेमेति यद् एवैषां दुष्टुतं दुश्शस्तं तद् एतेन तरन्ति
14.5.m: 'May we cross over all misfortunes'—whatever has been ill-chanted or ill-recited by them, that they cross over by this.

14.5.s: ekādaśākṣaraṇidhano bhavaty ekādaśākṣarā triṣṭub ojīvīryaṃ triṣṭub ojasy eva vīrye pratitiṣṭhati
14.5.d: एकादशाक्षरणिधनो भवत्य् एकादशाक्षरा त्रिष्टुब् ओजीवीर्यं त्रिष्टुब् ओजस्य् एव वीर्ये प्रतितिष्ठति
14.5.m: It has an eleven-syllable cadence. The triṣṭubh has eleven syllables; the triṣṭubh is vigour and virility. He firmly establishes himself in vigour and virility.

14.5.s: gaurīvitaṃ bhavati yad eva gaurīvitasya brahmaṇam
14.5.d: गौरीवितं भवति यद् एव गौरीवितस्य ब्रह्मणम्
14.5.m: There is the Gaurīvita; whatever is the brāhmaṇa of the Gaurīvita [applies here].

14.5.s: kārtayaśaṃ bhavati
14.5.d: कार्तयशं भवति

14.5.s: hīti nidhanam upayanti pāpmano 'pahatyai
14.5.d: हीति निधनम् उपयन्ति पाप्मनो ऽपहत्यै
14.5.m: They undertake the cadence 'hī' for the destruction of evil.

14.5.s: apa pāpmānaṃ hate kārtayaśena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
14.5.d: अप पाप्मानं हते कार्तयशेन तुष्टुवानः
14.5.m: He who has praised with the Kārtayaśa smites away evil.

14.5.s: sāhaiviṣaṃ bhavati
14.5.d: साहैविषं भवति

14.5.s: suhavir vā etenāṅgiraso 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
14.5.d: सुहविर् वा एतेनाङ्गिरसो ऽञ्जसा स्वर्गं लोकम् अपश्यत् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्यानुख्यात्यै स्वर्गाल् लोकान् न च्यवते तुष्टुवानः
14.5.m: Suhavis Āṅgirasa indeed directly saw the heavenly world by this. It is for the beholding of the heavenly world. He who has praised [with it] does not fall from the heavenly world.

14.5.s: brahmāvādino vadanti yat ṣaḍahe stomāś chandāṃsy āpyante kiṃ chandasaś chandomā iti puruṣaś chandasa iti brūyāt puruṣo vai pāṅktaḥ puruṣo dvipadā chandomānām ayātayāmatāyai
14.5.d: ब्रह्मावादिनो वदन्ति यत् षडहे स्तोमाश् छन्दांस्य् आप्यन्ते किं छन्दसश् छन्दोमा इति पुरुषश् छन्दस इति ब्रूयात् पुरुषो वै पाङ्क्तः पुरुषो द्विपदा छन्दोमानाम् अयातयामतायै
14.5.m: The theologians say: 'Since the stomas and metres are exhausted in the six-day period, what metre do the Chandomas have?' One should say: 'Man is their metre.' Man indeed is fivefold; man is two-footed. [This is] for the non-exhaustion of the Chandomas.

14.5.s: jarābodhīyaṃ bhavaty annādyasyāvarudhyai
14.5.d: जराबोधीयं भवत्य् अन्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै
14.5.m: There is the Jarābodhīya, for the acquisition of food.

14.5.s: annaṃ vai jarābodhīyaṃ mukhaṃ gāyatrī mukha eva tad annaṃ dhatte 'nnam atti
14.5.d: अन्नं वै जराबोधीयं मुखं गायत्री मुख एव तद् अन्नं धत्ते ऽन्नम् अत्ति
14.5.m: Food indeed is the Jarābodhīya; the mouth is the gāyatrī. He places food right in the mouth; he eats food.

14.5.s: annādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda
14.5.d: अन्नादो भवति य एवं वेद
14.5.m: He who knows this becomes an eater of food.

14.5.s: gāyatrīṣu stuvanti pratiṣṭhāyai brahmavarcasāya yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
14.5.d: गायत्रीषु स्तुवन्ति प्रतिष्ठायै ब्रह्मवर्चसाय येनैव प्राणेन प्रयन्ति तम् अभ्युद्यन्ति
14.5.m: They praise on gāyatrī verses for firm support, for brahminical lustre. With whichever breath they go forth, to that they rise up.

14.5.s: iḍāntāḥ pāvamānā bhavanti paśavo vā iḍāḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśuṣv eva tat paśūn dadhāti stomaḥ
14.5.d: इडान्ताः पावमाना भवन्ति पशवो वा इडाः पशवश् छन्दोमाः पशुष्व् एव तत् पशून् दधाति स्तोमः
14.5.m: The Pavamāna chants end with Iḍā. Cattle are Iḍā; cattle are the Chandomas. Thereby the stoma places cattle in cattle.

14.6.s: ā te vatso mano yamad ity apacchid iva vā etad yajñakāṇḍaṃ yad ukthāni yad eti salomatvāyaiva
14.6.d: आ ते वत्सो मनो यमद् इत्य् अपच्छिद् इव वा एतद् यज्ञकाण्डं यद् उक्थानि यद् एति सलोमत्वायैव
14.6.m: 'Let the calf hold fast your mind'—this uktha-section of the sacrifice is, as it were, cut off. That he goes [to it] is for smoothness.

14.6.s: tvaṃ na indrābhara iti pūrṇāḥ kakubhaḥ
14.6.d: त्वं न इन्द्राभर इति पूर्णाः ककुभः
14.6.m: 'Bring to us, O Indra'—[these are] complete kakubh verses.

14.6.s: apabhraṃśa iva vā eṣa yaj jayāyasaḥ stomāt kanīyāṃsaṃ stomam upayanti yad etāḥ pūrṇāḥ kakubho bhavanty anapabhraṃśāya
14.6.d: अपभ्रंश इव वा एष यज् जयायसः स्तोमात् कनीयांसं स्तोमम् उपयन्ति यद् एताः पूर्णाः ककुभो भवन्त्य् अनपभ्रंशाय
14.6.m: It is like a falling off when they go from a greater stoma to a lesser stoma. That these are complete kakubh verses is to avoid falling off.

14.6.s: vatsaś ca vai medhātithiś ca kāṇvāv āstāṃ taṃ vatsaṃ medhātithir ākrośad abrāhmaṇo 'si śūdrāputra iti so 'bravīd ṛtenāgniṃ vyayāva yataro nau brahmīyān iti vātsena vatso vyain maidhātithena medhātithis tasya na loma ca nauṣat tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sāma vātsaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
14.6.d: वत्सश् च वै मेधातिथिश् च काण्वाव् आस्तां तं वत्सं मेधातिथिर् आक्रोशद् अब्राह्मणो ऽसि शूद्रापुत्र इति सो ऽब्रवीद् ऋतेनाग्निं व्ययाव यतरो नौ ब्रह्मीयान् इति वात्सेन वत्सो व्यैन् मैधातिथेन मेधातिथिस् तस्य न लोम च नौषत् तद् वाव स तर्ह्य् अकामयत कामसनि साम वात्सं कामम् एवैतेनावरुन्धे
14.6.m: Vatsa and Medhātithi were two Kāṇva descendants. Medhātithi reviled Vatsa: 'You are a non-brahmin, the son of a Śūdrā.' He said: 'Let us two walk through fire with truth, [to see] which of us is the better brahmin.' Vatsa walked through with the Vātsa, Medhātithi with the Maidhātitha. Not a single hair of his was scorched. Truly that was what he desired at that time. The Vātsa sāman is wish-granting; he obtains [his] desire by it.

14.6.s: upagur vai sauśravasaḥ kutsasyauravasya purohita āsīt sa kutsaḥ paryaśapad ya indraṃ yajātā iti sa indraḥ suśravasam upetyābravīd yajasva māśanāyāmivā iti tam ayajata sa indraḥ puroḍāśas taḥ kutsam upetyābravīd ayakṣata mā kva te pariśaptam abhūd iti kas tvā yaṣṭeti suśravā iti sa kutsa aurava upāgāḥ sauśravasasyodgāyata audumbaryā śiro 'cchinat sa śuśravā indram abravīt tvattanād vai medam īdṛg upāgād iti tam etena sāmnā samairayat tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sāma sauśravasaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
14.6.d: उपगुर् वै सौश्रवसः कुत्सस्यौरवस्य पुरोहित आसीत् स कुत्सः पर्यशपद् य इन्द्रं यजाता इति स इन्द्रः सुश्रवसम् उपेत्याब्रवीद् यजस्व माशनायामिवा इति तम् अयजत स इन्द्रः पुरोडाशस् तः कुत्सम् उपेत्याब्रवीद् अयक्षत मा क्व ते परिशप्तम् अभूद् इति कस् त्वा यष्टेति सुश्रवा इति स कुत्स औरव उपागाः सौश्रवसस्योद्गायत औदुम्बर्या शिरो ऽच्छिनत् स शुश्रवा इन्द्रम् अब्रवीत् त्वत्तनाद् वै मेदम् ईदृग् उपागाद् इति तम् एतेन साम्ना समैरयत् तद् वाव स तर्ह्य् अकामयत कामसनि साम सौश्रवसं कामम् एवैतेनावरुन्धे
14.6.m: Upagu Sauśravasa was the domestic priest of Kutsa Aurava. Kutsa cursed: 'Whoever shall sacrifice to Indra [shall be cursed].' Indra approached Suśravas and said: 'Sacrifice to me, [I am] afflicted by hunger.' He sacrificed to him. Indra, holding the sacrificial cake, approached Kutsa and said: '[He] has sacrificed to me; where is your curse gone?' 'Who sacrificed to you?' 'Suśravas.' Kutsa Aurava cut off the head of Upagu Sauśravasa, who was chanting, with an audumbarī pole. Suśravas said to Indra: 'Through your cause this has come upon me.' He restored him with this sāman. Truly that was what he desired at that time. The Sauśravasa sāman is wish-granting; he obtains [his] desire by it.

14.6.s: cyavano vai dādhīco 'śvinoḥ priya āsīt so 'jīryat tam etena sāmnāpsu vyaiṅkayatāṃ taṃ punaryuvānam akurutāṃ tad vāva tau tarhy akāmayetāṃ kāmasani sāma vīṅkaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
14.6.d: च्यवनो वै दाधीचो ऽश्विनोः प्रिय आसीत् सो ऽजीर्यत् तम् एतेन साम्नाप्सु व्यैङ्कयतां तं पुनर्युवानम् अकुरुतां तद् वाव तौ तर्ह्य् अकामयेतां कामसनि साम वीङ्कं कामम् एवैतेनावरुन्धे
14.6.m: Cyavana Dādhīca was dear to the Aśvins. He grew old. With this sāman they swung him in the waters; they made him young again. Truly that was what the two desired at that time. The Vīṅka sāman is wish-granting; he obtains [his] desire by it.

14.6.s: caturviṃśa eva stomo bhavati tejase brahmavarcasāya
14.6.d: चतुर्विंश एव स्तोमो भवति तेजसे ब्रह्मवर्चसाय
14.6.m: The stoma is the twenty-four-fold alone, for fiery energy, for brahminical lustre.

14.7.s: śiśuṃ jajñānaṃ haryataṃ mṛjanti ity aṣṭam asy āhnaḥ pratid bhavati
14.7.d: शिशुं जज्ञानं हर्यतं मृजन्ति इत्य् अष्टम् अस्य् आह्नः प्रतिद् भवति
14.7.m: 'They cleanse the newborn, lovely babe' is the introductory verse of the eighth day.

14.7.s: śiśur iva vā eṣa saptamenāhnā jāyate tam aṣṭamenāhnā mṛjanti
14.7.d: शिशुर् इव वा एष सप्तमेनाह्ना जायते तम् अष्टमेनाह्ना मृजन्ति
14.7.m: Like a newborn babe he is born on the seventh day; they cleanse him on the eighth day.
There is a chant-triplet, for the retention of out-breath and in-breath.
They contain the word 'hari', for the non-exhaustion of the Chandomas.

14.7.s: pañcarco bhavati pañcapadā paṅktiḥ pāṅktam annam annādyasyāvarudhyai
14.7.d: पञ्चर्चो भवति पञ्चपदा पङ्क्तिः पाङ्क्तम् अन्नम् अन्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै
14.7.m: There is a five-verse hymn. The paṅkti has five verses; food is fivefold, for the acquisition of food.

14.7.s: bāṇavān bhavaty anto vai bāṇo 'nta etad aṣṭamam ahnām anta eva tad antena stuvate pratiṣṭhāyai
14.7.d: बाणवान् भवत्य् अन्तो वै बाणो ऽन्त एतद् अष्टमम् अह्नाम् अन्त एव तद् अन्तेन स्तुवते प्रतिष्ठायै
14.7.m: There is [the hymn] with the bāṇa; the end indeed is the bāṇa. The eighth of the days is the end. They praise with the end at the end, for firm support.
There are three triplets, for the continuity of out-breath and in-breath.

14.8.s: agniṃ vo devam agnibhiḥ sajoṣā ity āgneyam ājyaṃ bhavati
14.8.d: अग्निं वो देवम् अग्निभिः सजोषा इत्य् आग्नेयम् आज्यं भवति
14.8.m: 'Your god Agni with the fires, in concord' is the ājyastotra to Agni.

14.8.s: agnibhir ity eva pūrvāṇy ahāni abhi samiddhāny aṣṭamam ahar abhisamindhe
14.8.d: अग्निभिर् इत्य् एव पूर्वाण्य् अहानि अभि समिद्धान्य् अष्टमम् अहर् अभिसमिन्धे
14.8.m: By 'with the fires', having kindled the previous days, he kindles the eighth day.

14.8.s: mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmaha iti bārhataṃ maitrāvaruṇam
14.8.d: मित्रं वयं हवामह इति बार्हतं मैत्रावरुणम्
14.8.m: 'Mitra we invoke' is the Maitrāvaruṇa chant in the bṛhatī metre.

14.8.s: ugragādham iva vā etac chandomās tad yathāta ugragādhe vyātiṣajya gāhanta evam evaitad rūpe vyatiṣajati chandomānām asaṃvyāthāya
14.8.d: उग्रगाधम् इव वा एतच् छन्दोमास् तद् यथात उग्रगाधे व्यातिषज्य गाहन्त एवम् एवैतद् रूपे व्यतिषजति छन्दोमानाम् असंव्याथाय
14.8.m: The Chandomas are indeed like a strong ford. Just as they plunge into a strong ford by crossing over [intertwined], so he intertwines in form, for the unsteadiness of the Chandomas [to be averted].
'We make that Indra strong' is [the ājyastotra] to Indra.

14.8.s: aṣṭamena vai devā ahnendram avājayan navamena pāpmānam aghnann ahar evaitena vājayanti
14.8.d: अष्टमेन वै देवा अह्नेन्द्रम् अवाजयन् नवमेन पाप्मानम् अघ्नन्न् अहर् एवैतेन वाजयन्ति
14.8.m: By the eighth day the gods invigorated Indra; by the ninth they slew evil. By this they invigorate the day.

14.8.s: indre agnā namo bṛhad iti bārhatam aindrāgnam
14.8.d: इन्द्रे अग्ना नमो बृहद् इति बार्हतम् ऐन्द्राग्नम्
14.8.m: 'To Indra and Agni great homage' is the Aindrāgna chant in the bṛhatī metre.

14.8.s: ugragādham iva vā etad yac chandomās tad yathāta ugragādhe vyatiṣajya gāhanta evam evaitad rape vyatiṣajati chandomānām asaṃvyāthāya stomaḥ
14.8.d: उग्रगाधम् इव वा एतद् यच् छन्दोमास् तद् यथात उग्रगाधे व्यतिषज्य गाहन्त एवम् एवैतद् रपे व्यतिषजति छन्दोमानाम् असंव्याथाय स्तोमः
14.8.m: The Chandomas are indeed like a strong ford. Just as they plunge into a strong ford by crossing over [intertwined], so the stoma intertwines in form, for the unsteadiness of the Chandomas [to be averted].

14.9.s: adhvaryo adribhiḥ sutam iti gāyatrī bhavaty ahno dhṛtyai
14.9.d: अध्वर्यो अद्रिभिः सुतम् इति गायत्री भवत्य् अह्नो धृत्यै
14.9.m: 'O Adhvaryu, [the soma] pressed with stones' is in the gāyatrī metre, for the holding fast of the day.

14.9.s: gāyatryaḥ satyas triṣṭubhorūpeṇa traiṣṭubhaṃ hy etad ahaḥ
14.9.d: गायत्र्यः सत्यस् त्रिष्टुभोरूपेण त्रैष्टुभं ह्य् एतद् अहः
14.9.m: Being gāyatrī verses, [they are recited] in the manner of triṣṭubh verses, for this day belongs to the triṣṭubh.

14.9.s: abhi somāsa āyava ity abhīti rathantarasya rūpaṃ bṛhad iti bṛhata ubhayoḥ saha rūpam upaity ubhau hi varṇāv etad ahaḥ
14.9.d: अभि सोमास आयव इत्य् अभीति रथन्तरस्य रूपं बृहद् इति बृहत उभयोः सह रूपम् उपैत्य् उभौ हि वर्णाव् एतद् अहः
14.9.m: 'Unto the Soma juices, the active ones'—'unto' is the form of the Rathantara; 'great' is that of the Bṛhat. He assumes the form of both together, for both colours belong to this day.

14.9.s: dhartā divaḥ pavate kṛtvyo rasa ity adhṛta iva vā eṣas tryaho yad dharteti dhṛtyā eva
14.9.d: धर्ता दिवः पवते कृत्व्यो रस इत्य् अधृत इव वा एषस् त्र्यहो यद् धर्तेति धृत्या एव
14.9.m: 'The upholder of heaven purifies himself, the active sap'—unsupported, as it were, is this three-day period; because it says 'upholder', it is for holding fast.

14.9.s: jagatyas satyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa tasmāt triṣṭubho loke kriyante
14.9.d: जगत्यस् सत्यस् त्रिष्टुभो रूपेण तस्मात् त्रिष्टुभो लोके क्रियन्ते
14.9.m: Being jagatī verses, [they are recited] in the manner of triṣṭubh verses; therefore they are performed in the place of the triṣṭubh.

14.9.s: gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
14.9.d: गायत्रं भवति यद् एव गायत्रस्य ब्राह्मणम्
14.9.m: There is the Gāyatra; whatever is the brāhmaṇa of the Gāyatra [applies here].

14.9.s: vairūpaṃ bhavati
14.9.d: वैरूपं भवति

14.9.s: paśavo vai vairūpaṃ paśūnām avarudhyai virūpaḥ saṃvatsaro virūpam annam annādyasyāvarudhyai
14.9.d: पशवो वै वैरूपं पशूनाम् अवरुध्यै विरूपः संवत्सरो विरूपम् अन्नम् अन्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै
14.9.m: The Vairūpa is cattle, for the acquisition of cattle. Diverse is the year; diverse is food, for the acquisition of food.

14.9.s: āśu bhārgavaṃ bhavati
14.9.d: आशु भार्गवं भवति

14.9.s: ahar vā etad avlīyata tad devā āśunābhyadhinvaṃs tad āśor āśutvam
14.9.d: अहर् वा एतद् अव्लीयत तद् देवा आशुनाभ्यधिन्वंस् तद् आशोर् आशुत्वम्
14.9.m: This day was collapsing; the gods refreshed it with the swift (āśu) [sāman]; that is the swiftness of the Āśu.

14.9.s: mārgīyavaṃ bhavati
14.9.d: मार्गीयवं भवति

14.9.s: devaṃ vā etaṃ mṛgayur iti vadanty etena vai sa ubhayeṣāṃ paśūnām ādhipatyam āśnutobhayeṣāṃ paśūnām ādhipatyam aśnute mārgīyaveṇa tuṣṭuvānaḥ
14.9.d: देवं वा एतं मृगयुर् इति वदन्त्य् एतेन वै स उभयेषां पशूनाम् आधिपत्यम् आश्नुतोभयेषां पशूनाम् आधिपत्यम् अश्नुते मार्गीयवेण तुष्टुवानः
14.9.m: They speak of this god as the hunter. By this [sāman] he indeed attained lordship over both kinds of cattle; he who has praised with the Mārgīyava attains lordship over both kinds of cattle.

14.9.s: saumitraṃ bhavati
14.9.d: सौमित्रं भवति

14.9.s: yad eva saumitrasya brāhmaṇam
14.9.d: यद् एव सौमित्रस्य ब्राह्मणम्
14.9.m: Whatever is the brāhmaṇa of the Saumitra [applies here].

14.9.s: aiṭataṃ bhavati
14.9.d: ऐटतं भवति

14.9.s: iṭan vā etena kāvyo 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
14.9.d: इटन् वा एतेन काव्यो ऽञ्जसा स्वर्गं लोकम् अपश्यत् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्यानुख्यात्यै स्वर्गाल् लोकान् न च्यवते तुष्टुवानः
14.9.m: By this, indeed, Iṭan Kāvya directly saw the heavenly world; it is for the sighting of the heavenly world. He who has praised [with it] does not fall from the heavenly world.

14.9.s: sākamaśvaṃ bhavati yad eva sākamaśvasya brāhmaṇam
14.9.d: साकमश्वं भवति यद् एव साकमश्वस्य ब्राह्मणम्
