14.9.m: There is the Sākamaśva [sāman]; whatever is the brāhmaṇa of the Sākamaśva [applies here].

14.9.s: tad u dhurāṃ sāmety āhuḥ prāṇā vai dhuraḥ prāṇānām avarudhyai
14.9.d: तद् उ धुरां सामेत्य् आहुः प्राणा वै धुरः प्राणानाम् अवरुध्यै
14.9.m: And they say: 'It is the sāman of the yokes.' The vital breaths indeed are the yokes, [it serves] for the securing of the vital breaths.

14.9.s: vilambasauparṇaṃ bhavati
14.9.d: विलम्बसौपर्णं भवति
14.9.m: There is the Vilambasauparṇa [sāman].

14.9.s: ātmā vā eṣa sauparṇānāṃ yad aṣṭame 'hani pakṣāv etāv abhito bhavato ye saptamanavamayor vīva vā antarātmā pakṣau lambate yadantarātmā pakṣau vilambate tasmād vilambasauparṇam
14.9.d: आत्मा वा एष सौपर्णानां यद् अष्टमे ऽहनि पक्षाव् एताव् अभितो भवतो ये सप्तमनवमयोर् वीव वा अन्तरात्मा पक्षौ लम्बते यदन्तरात्मा पक्षौ विलम्बते तस्माद् विलम्बसौपर्णम्
14.9.m: This is indeed the trunk of the Sauparṇa [chants], that which is on the eighth day; these two wings on both sides are those which belong to the seventh and ninth [days]. The trunk hangs down, as it were, between the two wings; because the trunk hangs down between the two wings, therefore it is called Vilambasauparṇa.

14.9.s: svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai sauparṇaṃ kriyate
14.9.d: स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्ट्यै सौपर्णं क्रियते
14.9.m: For the attainment of the heavenly world the Sauparṇa is performed.

14.9.s: dvitīyaṃ hy etad rūpaṃ yac chandomāḥ
14.9.d: द्वितीयं ह्य् एतद् रूपं यच् छन्दोमाः
14.9.m: For this is a second form, namely the Chandomas.

14.9.s: paśavo vai vāmadevyaṃ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśuṣv eva tat paśūn saṃdadhāti
14.9.d: पशवो वै वामदेव्यं पशवश् छन्दोमाः पशुष्व् एव तत् पशून् संदधाति
14.9.m: The Vāmadevya indeed is cattle; the Chandomas are cattle; thereby he firmly places cattle among cattle.

14.9.s: gāyatrapārśvaṃ bhavati
14.9.d: गायत्रपार्श्वं भवति
14.9.m: There is the Gāyatrapārśva [sāman].

14.9.s: ahar vā etad avlīyata tad devā gāyatrapārśvena samatanvaṃs tasmād gāyatrapārśvam
14.9.d: अहर् वा एतद् अव्लीयत तद् देवा गायत्रपार्श्वेन समतन्वंस् तस्माद् गायत्रपार्श्वम्
14.9.m: This day was indeed collapsing; the gods braced it with the Gāyatrapārśva; therefore it is called Gāyatrapārśva.

14.9.s: trirātro yad vyaśīryata tam etaiḥ sāmabhir abhiṣajyan gāyatrapārśvenopāyacchan santaninā samatanvan saṃkṛtinā samaskurvan pratiṣṭhitau pūrvau trirātrāv apratiṣṭhita eṣa yad etāny eva sāmāni kriyanta etasyaiva pratiṣṭhityai
14.9.d: त्रिरात्रो यद् व्यशीर्यत तम् एतैः सामभिर् अभिषज्यन् गायत्रपार्श्वेनोपायच्छन् सन्तनिना समतन्वन् संकृतिना समस्कुर्वन् प्रतिष्ठितौ पूर्वौ त्रिरात्राव् अप्रतिष्ठित एष यद् एतान्य् एव सामानि क्रियन्त एतस्यैव प्रतिष्ठित्यै
14.9.m: When the three-day period crumbled, they healed it with these sāmans: with the Gāyatrapārśva they supported it, with the Santani they stretched it, with the Saṃkṛti they put it in order. Firmly established were the two previous three-day periods; unestablished was this one. That these very sāmans are performed is solely for the establishing of this [period].

14.9.s: pauruhanmanaṃ bhavati
14.9.d: पौरुहन्मनं भवति
14.9.m: There is the Pauruhanmana [sāman].

14.9.s: puruhanmā vā etena vaikhānaso 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
14.9.d: पुरुहन्मा वा एतेन वैखानसो ऽञ्जसा स्वर्गं लोकम् अपश्यत् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्यानुख्यात्यै स्वर्गाल् लोकान् न च्यवते तुष्टुवानः
14.9.m: By this, indeed, Puruhanman Vaikhānasa directly saw the heavenly world; it is for the sighting of the heavenly world. He who has praised [with it] does not fall from the heavenly world.

14.9.s: abhyāghātyaṃ bhavaty abhyāghātyasāmāno hi chandomāḥ
14.9.d: अभ्याघात्यं भवत्य् अभ्याघात्यसामानो हि छन्दोमाः
14.9.m: There is the Abhyāghātya [sāman], for the Chandomas have sāmans that are struck upon.

14.9.s: dvaigataṃ bhavati
14.9.d: द्वैगतं भवति

14.9.s: dvigad vā etena bhārgavo dviḥ svargaṃ lokam agacchad āgatya punar agacchat dvayoḥ kāmayor avarudhyai dvaigataṃ kriyate
14.9.d: द्विगद् वा एतेन भार्गवो द्विः स्वर्गं लोकम् अगच्छद् आगत्य पुनर् अगच्छत् द्वयोः कामयोर् अवरुध्यै द्वैगतं क्रियते
14.9.m: By this, indeed, Dvigat Bhārgava went twice to the heavenly world: having returned, he went again. For the securing of two desires the Dvaigata is performed.

14.9.s: hārāyaṇaṃ bhavati
14.9.d: हारायणं भवति

14.9.s: indras tejaskāmo haraskāmas tapo 'tapyata sa etad dhārāyaṇam apaśyat tena tejo haro 'vārundha tejasvī harasvī bhavati hārāyaṇena tuṣtuvānaḥ
14.9.d: इन्द्रस् तेजस्कामो हरस्कामस् तपो ऽतप्यत स एतद् धारायणम् अपश्यत् तेन तेजो हरो ऽवारुन्ध तेजस्वी हरस्वी भवति हारायणेन तुष्तुवानः
14.9.m: Indra, desiring fiery brilliance, desiring lustre, performed ascetic heat. He saw this Hārāyaṇa; by it he secured fiery brilliance and lustre. He who has praised with the Hārāyaṇa becomes endowed with fiery brilliance and lustre.

14.9.s: achidraṃ bhavati
14.9.d: अछिद्रं भवति

14.9.s: yad vā etasyāhnaś chidram āsīt tad devā acchidreṇāpy auhaṃs tad acchidrasyācchidratvam
14.9.d: यद् वा एतस्याह्नश् छिद्रम् आसीत् तद् देवा अच्छिद्रेणाप्य् औहंस् तद् अच्छिद्रस्याच्छिद्रत्वम्
14.9.m: Whatever flaw this day had, that the gods covered over with the Achidra; that is the flawless nature of the Achidra.

14.9.s: bārhadukthaṃ bhavati
14.9.d: बार्हदुक्थं भवति

14.9.s: bṛhaduktho vā etena vāmneyo 'nnasya purodhām agacchad annaṃ vai brahmaṇaḥ purodhām annādyasyāvarudhyai
14.9.d: बृहदुक्थो वा एतेन वाम्नेयो ऽन्नस्य पुरोधाम् अगच्छद् अन्नं वै ब्रह्मणः पुरोधाम् अन्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै
14.9.m: By this, indeed, Bṛhaduktha Vāmneya attained pre-eminence in food. Food indeed is the pre-eminence of the brahmin; [it serves] for the securing of food.

14.9.s: udvad bhārgavaṃ bhavati
14.9.d: उद्वद् भार्गवं भवति
14.9.m: There is the Udvat-Bhārgava [sāman].

14.9.s: pravatā vai devāḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ prāyann udvatodāyan
14.9.d: प्रवता वै देवाः स्वर्गं लोकं प्रायन्न् उद्वतोदायन्
14.9.m: Along the downward slope the gods departed to the heavenly world; by the upward slope they mounted upward.

14.9.s: nidhanāntāḥ pavamānā bhavanty ahno dhṛtyai stomaḥ
14.9.d: निधनान्ताः पवमाना भवन्त्य् अह्नो धृत्यै स्तोमः
14.9.m: The Pavamāna [chants] have cadences at the end, for the upholding of the day; the stoma [is applied].

14.10.s: ka īṃ veda sute sacā iti satobṛhatyaḥ
14.10.d: क ईं वेद सुते सचा इति सतोबृहत्यः
14.10.m: 'Who knows him when the soma is pressed together—': these are satobṛhatī verses.

14.10.s: apabhraṃśa iva vā eṣa yas saptame 'hani satobṛhatyo bhavanti nāṣṭame tasmād aṣṭame kāryā anapabhraṃśāya
14.10.d: अपभ्रंश इव वा एष यस् सप्तमे ऽहनि सतोबृहत्यो भवन्ति नाष्टमे तस्माद् अष्टमे कार्या अनपभ्रंशाय
14.10.m: It is like a slipping down, that on the seventh day there are satobṛhatī verses, but not on the eighth; therefore on the eighth day they are to be used, to prevent slipping down.

14.10.s: tadāhuḥ śithilam iva vā etac chando yat satobṛhātīty eṣā vai pratiṣṭhitā bṛhatī yā punaḥpadā yad indra prāg apāg udag iti diśāṃ vimarśaḥ pratiṣṭityai
14.10.d: तदाहुः शिथिलम् इव वा एतच् छन्दो यत् सतोबृहातीत्य् एषा वै प्रतिष्ठिता बृहती या पुनःपदा यद् इन्द्र प्राग् अपाग् उदग् इति दिशां विमर्शः प्रतिष्टित्यै
14.10.m: As to this they say: 'Loose indeed is this metre, namely the satobṛhatī.' This, indeed, is the firmly established bṛhatī which has a repeated foot; that [verse begins]: 'O Indra, east, west, north'—this consideration of the quarters is for firm establishment.
On these [verses], the Naipātitha is the sāman of the brahman.

14.10.s: sāmārṣeyavat svargāya yujyate svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
14.10.d: सामार्षेयवत् स्वर्गाय युज्यते स्वर्गाल् लोकान् न च्यवते तुष्टुवानः
14.10.m: Possessed of the seer of the sāman, it is harnessed for heaven; he who has praised [with it] does not fall from the heavenly world.

14.10.s: yac ca pṛṣṭhāni yāni caitāny ahāni teṣām ubhayeṣāṃ santatyai
14.10.d: यच् च पृष्ठानि यानि चैतान्य् अहानि तेषाम् उभयेषां सन्तत्यै
14.10.m: Both what the pṛṣṭhas are and what these days are—it serves for the continuity of both of these.

14.10.s: vyaśvo vā etenāṅgiraso 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyā etat pṛṣṭhānām antataḥ kriyate stomaḥ
14.10.d: व्यश्वो वा एतेनाङ्गिरसो ऽञ्जसा स्वर्गं लोकम् अपश्यत् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्यानुख्यात्या एतत् पृष्ठानाम् अन्ततः क्रियते स्तोमः
14.10.m: By this, indeed, Vyaśva Āṅgirasa directly saw the heavenly world; for the sighting of the heavenly world this is performed at the end of the pṛṣṭhas; the stoma [is applied].

14.11.s: pavasva deva āyuṣag indraṃ gacchatu te mada iti gāyatrī bhavati madavad vai rasavat tṛtīyasavanaṃ madam eva tad rasaṃ dadhāti
14.11.d: पवस्व देव आयुषग् इन्द्रं गच्छतु ते मद इति गायत्री भवति मदवद् वै रसवत् तृतीयसवनं मदम् एव तद् रसं दधाति
14.11.m: 'Clarify yourself, O god, together with life; may your exhilaration reach Indra': this is a gāyatrī verse. Endowed with exhilaration, endowed with sap, indeed, is the third pressing; thereby he places exhilaration and sap [in it].

14.11.s: prāṇā śiśur mahīnām iti prāṇavatyo bhavanti prāṇān eva tad yajamāne dadhāti
14.11.d: प्राणा शिशुर् महीनाम् इति प्राणवत्यो भवन्ति प्राणान् एव तद् यजमाने दधाति
14.11.m: 'The breath, the child of the great ones': [verses] containing the word 'breath' they are; thereby he places breaths in the sacrificer.

14.11.s: abhī no vājasātamam ity abhīti rathantarasya rūpaṃ rāthantaraṃ hy etad ahaḥ
14.11.d: अभी नो वाजसातमम् इत्य् अभीति रथन्तरस्य रूपं राथन्तरं ह्य् एतद् अहः
14.11.m: 'Towards us, most winning of bounty': by the word 'towards' (abhi) there is the characteristic of the Rathantara, for this day belongs to the Rathantara.

14.11.s: pavasva soma mahān samudra ity akṣarapaṅktiḥ stomānāṃ prabhūtir atho etad dhy evaitarhi chando 'yātayāma yad akṣarapaṅktis tena chandomā ayātayāmānaḥ kriyante brahmavādino vadanti yat ṣaḍahe stomāś chandāṃsy āpyante kiṃ chandasaś chandomā ity etac chandaso yad etā akṣarapaṅktaya iti brūyāt
14.11.d: पवस्व सोम महान् समुद्र इत्य् अक्षरपङ्क्तिः स्तोमानां प्रभूतिर् अथो एतद् ध्य् एवैतर्हि छन्दो ऽयातयाम यद् अक्षरपङ्क्तिस् तेन छन्दोमा अयातयामानः क्रियन्ते ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति यत् षडहे स्तोमाश् छन्दांस्य् आप्यन्ते किं छन्दसश् छन्दोमा इत्य् एतच् छन्दसो यद् एता अक्षरपङ्क्तय इति ब्रूयात्
14.11.m: 'Clarify yourself, O Soma, as a great ocean': this akṣarapaṅkti is the abundance of the stomas; moreover, at this time the only metre not exhausted is the akṣarapaṅkti; thereby the Chandomas are made inexhaustible. The theological disputants say: 'Since at the six-day rite the stomas and metres are exhausted, what metre do the Chandomas have?' One should answer: 'They have this metre, namely these akṣarapaṅkti verses.'

14.11.s: hinvanti sūram usraya iti gāyatryaḥ satyo jagatyo rūpeṇa tasmāj jagatīnāṃ loke kriyante
14.11.d: हिन्वन्ति सूरम् उस्रय इति गायत्र्यः सत्यो जगत्यो रूपेण तस्माज् जगतीनां लोके क्रियन्ते
14.11.m: 'The beams drive on the hero': being gāyatrī verses, they have the form of jagatī verses; therefore they are performed in the place of jagatī verses.

14.11.s: gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
14.11.d: गायत्रं भवति यद् एव गायत्रस्य ब्राह्मणम्
14.11.m: There is the Gāyatra [sāman]; whatever is the brāhmaṇa of the Gāyatra [applies here].

14.11.s: svāśirām arko bhavati
14.11.d: स्वाशिराम् अर्को भवति

14.11.s: annaṃ vā arko 'nnādyasyāvarudhyai prāṇā vai svāśiraḥ prāṇānām arudhyai
14.11.d: अन्नं वा अर्को ऽन्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै प्राणा वै स्वाशिरः प्राणानाम् अरुध्यै
14.11.m: The arka is food, [it serves] for the securing of food; the svāśiras are the vital breaths, [it serves] for the securing of the vital breaths.

14.11.s: surūpaṃ bhavati
14.11.d: सुरूपं भवति

14.11.s: paśavo vai surūpaṃ paśūnām avarudhyai
14.11.d: पशवो वै सुरूपं पशूनाम् अवरुध्यै
14.11.m: The Surūpa is cattle, [it serves] for the securing of cattle. There is the Bhāsa [sāman]; he who has praised [with it] shines.

14.11.s: bhāsaṃ bhavati bhāti tuṣṭuvānaḥ
14.11.d: भासं भवति भाति तुष्टुवानः

14.11.s: padanidhanaṃ rāthantaraṃ hy etad ahaḥ
14.11.d: पदनिधनं राथन्तरं ह्य् एतद् अहः
14.11.m: It has its cadence on a word, for this day belongs to the Rathantara.

14.11.s: svarbhānur vā āsura ādityaṃ tamasāvidhyat sa na vyarocata tasyātrir bhāsena tamo 'pāhan sa vyarocata yad vai tad bhā abhavat tad bhāsasya bhāsatvam
14.11.d: स्वर्भानुर् वा आसुर आदित्यं तमसाविध्यत् स न व्यरोचत तस्यात्रिर् भासेन तमो ऽपाहन् स व्यरोचत यद् वै तद् भा अभवत् तद् भासस्य भासत्वम्
14.11.m: Svarbhānu, the Asura, pierced the sun with darkness; it did not shine forth. Atri struck away its darkness with the Bhāsa [sāman]; it shone forth. In that there came to be light (bhā), that is the nature of the Bhāsa [sāman].

14.11.s: tama iva vā etāny ahāni yac chandomās tebhya etena sāmnā vivāsayati
14.11.d: तम इव वा एतान्य् अहानि यच् छन्दोमास् तेभ्य एतेन साम्ना विवासयति
14.11.m: These days, namely the Chandomas, are darkness as it were; away from them he drives the darkness by means of this sāman.

14.11.s: kākṣīvataṃ bhavati
14.11.d: काक्षीवतं भवति

14.11.s: kākṣīvān vā etenauśijaḥ prajātiṃ bhūmānam agacchat prajāyate bahur bhavati kākṣīvatena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
14.11.d: काक्षीवान् वा एतेनौशिजः प्रजातिं भूमानम् अगच्छत् प्रजायते बहुर् भवति काक्षीवतेन तुष्टुवानः
14.11.m: By this, indeed, Kakṣīvant Auśija attained offspring and abundance; he who has praised with the Kākṣīvata is propagated and becomes abundant.

14.11.s: āsitaṃ bhavati
14.11.d: आसितं भवति

14.11.s: asito vā etena daivalas trayāṇāṃ lokānāṃ dṛṣṭim apaśyat trayāṇāṃ kāmānām avarudhyā āsitaṃ kriyate
14.11.d: असितो वा एतेन दैवलस् त्रयाणां लोकानां दृष्टिम् अपश्यत् त्रयाणां कामानाम् अवरुध्या आसितं क्रियते
14.11.m: By this, indeed, Asita Devala saw the vision of the three worlds; for the securing of three desires the Āsita is performed.

14.11.s: aiṣiraṃ bhavati
14.11.d: ऐषिरं भवति

14.11.s: traitaṃ bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai
14.11.d: त्रैतं भवति प्रतिष्ठायै
14.11.m: There is the Traita [sāman], for firm establishment.

14.11.s: padanidhanaṃ rāthantaraṃ rāthantaraṃ hy etad ahaḥ
14.11.d: पदनिधनं राथन्तरं राथन्तरं ह्य् एतद् अहः
14.11.m: It has its cadence on a word; it belongs to the Rathantara, for this day belongs to the Rathantara.

14.11.s: nāthavindu sāma vindate nāthaṃ nāthavindūny etāny ahāni yat chandomā nātham evaitair vindate
14.11.d: नाथविन्दु साम विन्दते नाथं नाथविन्दून्य् एतान्य् अहानि यत् छन्दोमा नाथम् एवैतैर् विन्दते
14.11.m: The Nāthavindu sāman: he finds help; these days, namely the Chandomas, are finding help; by these he finds help.

14.11.s: gaurīvitaṃ bhavati yad eva gaurīvitasya brāhmaṇam
14.11.d: गौरीवितं भवति यद् एव गौरीवितस्य ब्राह्मणम्
14.11.m: There is the Gaurīvita [sāman]; whatever is the brāhmaṇa of the Gaurīvita [applies here].

14.11.s: kautsaṃ bhavati
14.11.d: कौत्सं भवति

14.11.s: etena vai kutso 'ndhaso vipānam apaśyat sa ha sma vai surādṛtinopavasathaṃ dhārayaty ubhayasyānnādyasyāvarudhyai kautsaṃ kriyate
14.11.d: एतेन वै कुत्सो ऽन्धसो विपानम् अपश्यत् स ह स्म वै सुरादृतिनोपवसथं धारयत्य् उभयस्यान्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै कौत्सं क्रियते
14.11.m: By this, indeed, Kutsa saw the distinction in drinking the blind soma; he used to observe the fast-day with a skin of liquor. The Kautsa is performed for securing both kinds of food.

14.11.s: śuddhāśuddhīyaṃ bhavati
14.11.d: शुद्धाशुद्धीयं भवति
14.11.m: There is the Śuddhāśuddhīya [sāman].

14.11.s: indro yatīn sālāvṛkebhyaḥ prāyacchat tam aślīlā vāg abhyavadat so 'śuddho 'manyata sa etac chuddhāśuddhīyam apaśyat tenāśudhyac chudhyati śuddhāśuddhīyena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
14.11.d: इन्द्रो यतीन् सालावृकेभ्यः प्रायच्छत् तम् अश्लीला वाग् अभ्यवदत् सो ऽशुद्धो ऽमन्यत स एतच् छुद्धाशुद्धीयम् अपश्यत् तेनाशुध्यच् छुध्यति शुद्धाशुद्धीयेन तुष्टुवानः
14.11.m: Indra delivered the yatis to the wild dogs. An abusive voice spoke against him; he considered himself impure. He saw this Śuddhāśuddhīya; by it he became purified. He who has chanted with the Śuddhāśuddhīya becomes purified.

14.11.s: krauñcaṃ bhavati yad eva krauñcasya brāhmaṇaṃ yat dvitīye 'hani
14.11.d: क्रौञ्चं भवति यद् एव क्रौञ्चस्य ब्राह्मणं यत् द्वितीये ऽहनि
14.11.m: There is the Krauñca [sāman], according to the explanation of the Krauñca on the second day.

14.11.s: rayiṣṭhaṃ bhavati
14.11.d: रयिष्ठं भवति

14.11.s: paśavo vai rayiṣṭhaṃ paśūnām avarudhyai
14.11.d: पशवो वै रयिष्ठं पशूनाम् अवरुध्यै
14.11.m: Cattle, indeed, are the Rayiṣṭha, for securing cattle.

14.11.s: audalaṃ bhavati
14.11.d: औदलं भवति

14.11.s: udalo vā etena vaiśvāmitraḥ prajātiṃ bhūmānam agacchat prajāyate bahur bhavaty audalena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
14.11.d: उदलो वा एतेन वैश्वामित्रः प्रजातिं भूमानम् अगच्छत् प्रजायते बहुर् भवत्य् औदलेन तुष्टुवानः
14.11.m: Udala Vaiśvāmitra, indeed, by this attained procreation and abundance. He procreates and becomes abundant who has chanted with the Audala.

14.11.s: brahmavādino vadanti yat ṣaḍahe stomāś chandāṃsy āpyante kiṃ chandasaś chandomā iti puruṣachandasa iti brūyāt puruṣo vai pāṅktaḥ puruṣo dvipadāś chandomānām ayātayāmatayau
14.11.d: ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति यत् षडहे स्तोमाश् छन्दांस्य् आप्यन्ते किं छन्दसश् छन्दोमा इति पुरुषछन्दस इति ब्रूयात् पुरुषो वै पाङ्क्तः पुरुषो द्विपदाश् छन्दोमानाम् अयातयामतयौ
14.11.m: The theologians say: 'Since the stomas and metres are exhausted in the six-day period, of what metre are the Chandomas?' He should say: 'Of the human metre.' The human being is fivefold; the human being is two-footed; [it is] for the non-exhaustion of the Chandomas.

14.11.s: viśoviśīyaṃ bhavati
14.11.d: विशोविशीयं भवति

14.11.s: agnir akāmayata viśo viśo 'tithis syāṃ viśo viśa ātithyam aśnuvīyeti sa tapo 'tapyata sa etad viśoviśīyam apaśyat tena viśo viśo 'tithir abhavat viśo viśa ātithyam aśnuta viśo viśo 'tithir bhavati viśo viśa ātithyam aśnute viśoviśīyena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
14.11.d: अग्निर् अकामयत विशो विशो ऽतिथिस् स्यां विशो विश आतिथ्यम् अश्नुवीयेति स तपो ऽतप्यत स एतद् विशोविशीयम् अपश्यत् तेन विशो विशो ऽतिथिर् अभवत् विशो विश आतिथ्यम् अश्नुत विशो विशो ऽतिथिर् भवति विशो विश आतिथ्यम् अश्नुते विशोविशीयेन तुष्टुवानः
14.11.m: Agni desired: 'May I be the guest of clan after clan; may I receive hospitality from clan after clan.' He performed ascetic heat; he saw this Viśoviśīya; by it he became the guest of clan after clan; he received hospitality from clan after clan. He becomes the guest of clan after clan; he receives hospitality from clan after clan, who has chanted with the Viśoviśīya.

14.11.s: gāyatrīṣu stuvanti pratiṣṭāyai brahmavarcasāya yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
14.11.d: गायत्रीषु स्तुवन्ति प्रतिष्टायै ब्रह्मवर्चसाय येनैव प्राणेन प्रयन्ति तम् अभ्युद्यन्ति
14.11.m: They chant on gāyatrī verses for firm support, for brahminical lustre; by whatever breath they go forth, into that they rise.

14.11.s: iḍāntāḥ pavamānā bhavanti paśavo vā iḍā paśavaś chandomāḥ paśuṣv eva tat paśūn dadhāti stomaḥ
14.11.d: इडान्ताः पवमाना भवन्ति पशवो वा इडा पशवश् छन्दोमाः पशुष्व् एव तत् पशून् दधाति स्तोमः
14.11.m: The pavamānas end in iḍā. Cattle are iḍā; the Chandomas are cattle. Thus the stoma places cattle in cattle.

14.12.s: preṣṭhaṃ vo atithim ity ātithyasyaiva tad rūpaṃ kriyate
14.12.d: प्रेष्ठं वो अतिथिम् इत्य् आतिथ्यस्यैव तद् रूपं क्रियते
14.12.m: With 'The dearest guest of yours...', a manifestation of hospitality is thereby made.

14.12.s: aindra no gadhi priya itīndriyasya vīryasyāvarudhyai
14.12.d: ऐन्द्र नो गधि प्रिय इतीन्द्रियस्य वीर्यस्यावरुध्यै
14.12.m: With 'Indra, come to us, dear...', for securing Indra's heroic power.

14.12.s: purāṃ bhindur yuvā kavir amitaujā ajāyata | indro viśvasya karmaṇo dhartā vajrī puruṣṭuta iti dhṛtyā eva
14.12.d: पुरां भिन्दुर् युवा कविर् अमितौजा अजायत । इन्द्रो विश्वस्य कर्मणो धर्ता वज्री पुरुष्टुत इति धृत्या एव
14.12.m: With 'The shatterer of strongholds, youthful, wise, of unmeasured might was born; Indra, the upholder of every deed, thunderbolt-wielder, praised by many,' for firmness alone.

14.12.s: uśanā vai kāvyo 'kāmayata yāvān itareṣāṃ kāvyānāṃ lokas tāvantaṃ spṛṇuyām iti sa tapo 'tapyata sa etad auśanam apaśyat tena tāvantaṃ lokam aspṛṇod yāvān itareṣāṃ kāvyānām āsīt tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sāmauśanaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
14.12.d: उशना वै काव्यो ऽकामयत यावान् इतरेषां काव्यानां लोकस् तावन्तं स्पृणुयाम् इति स तपो ऽतप्यत स एतद् औशनम् अपश्यत् तेन तावन्तं लोकम् अस्पृणोद् यावान् इतरेषां काव्यानाम् आसीत् तद् वाव स तर्ह्य् अकामयत कामसनि सामौशनं कामम् एवैतेनावरुन्धे
14.12.m: Uśanas Kāvya desired: 'May I gain as much world as is the world of the other Kāvyas.' He performed ascetic heat; he saw this Auśana; by it he gained as much world as belonged to the other Kāvyas. For that is what he then desired. The Auśana sāman wins desire; by it he secures his desire.

14.12.s: devānāṃ vai yajñaṃ rakṣāṃsy ajighāṃsaṃs tāny etena indraḥ saṃvartam apāvapad yat saṃvartam apāvapat tasmāt sāṃvartaṃ pāpmā vāva sa tān asacata taṃ sāṃvartenāpāghnatāpa pāpmānaṃ hate sāṃvartena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
14.12.d: देवानां वै यज्ञं रक्षांस्य् अजिघांसंस् तान्य् एतेन इन्द्रः संवर्तम् अपावपद् यत् संवर्तम् अपावपत् तस्मात् सांवर्तं पाप्मा वाव स तान् असचत तं सांवर्तेनापाघ्नताप पाप्मानं हते सांवर्तेन तुष्टुवानः
14.12.m: The demons wished to destroy the sacrifice of the gods. Indra swept them away in a heap with this [sāman]. Because he swept them away in a heap, it is called Sāṃvarta. Evil clung to them; they struck it away with the Sāṃvarta. He strikes away evil who has chanted with the Sāṃvarta.

14.12.s: māsā vai raśmayo maruto raśmayo maruto vai devānāṃ bhūyiṣṭhā bhūyiṣṭhā asāmeti vai sattram āsate bhūyiṣṭhā eva bhavanty ṛtumanti pūrvāṇy ahāny anṛtavaḥ chandomā yad etat sāma bhavati tenaitāny ahāny ahāny ṛtumanti bhavanti
14.12.d: मासा वै रश्मयो मरुतो रश्मयो मरुतो वै देवानां भूयिष्ठा भूयिष्ठा असामेति वै सत्त्रम् आसते भूयिष्ठा एव भवन्त्य् ऋतुमन्ति पूर्वाण्य् अहान्य् अनृतवः छन्दोमा यद् एतत् साम भवति तेनैतान्य् अहान्य् अहान्य् ऋतुमन्ति भवन्ति
14.12.m: The months are rays; the Maruts are rays. The Maruts are the most numerous of the gods. 'May we become the most numerous,' thinking thus they sit for a sacrificial session. They indeed become the most numerous. The previous days have seasons; the Chandomas are without seasons. In that there is this sāman, these days thereby become endowed with seasons.

14.12.s: catuścatvāriṃśa eva stomo bhavaty ojasy eva tad vīrye pratitiṣṭhaty ojo vīrye triṣṭup
14.12.d: चतुश्चत्वारिंश एव स्तोमो भवत्य् ओजस्य् एव तद् वीर्ये प्रतितिष्ठत्य् ओजो वीर्ये त्रिष्टुप्
14.12.m: The stoma is forty-four-fold; he thereby stands firmly in might and heroic power; the triṣṭubh is might and heroic power.

15.1.s: akrān samudraḥ parame vidharmann iti navamasyāhnaḥ pratipad bhavati
15.1.d: अक्रान् समुद्रः परमे विधर्मन्न् इति नवमस्याह्नः प्रतिपद् भवति
15.1.m: 'The ocean has roared in the highest dispensation' is the introductory verse of the ninth day.

15.1.s: paramaṃ vā etad ahar vidharma vidharma vā etad anyair aharbhir ahar yan navamaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ hi variṣṭham
15.1.d: परमं वा एतद् अहर् विधर्म विधर्म वा एतद् अन्यैर् अहर्भिर् अहर् यन् नवमं ज्येष्ठं हि वरिष्ठम्
15.1.m: This day is the highest dispensation; this day, which is the ninth, is distinct from the other days, for it is the eldest and highest.

15.1.s: matsi vāyum iṣṭaye rādhase na iti vāruṇy eṣā bhavati yad vai yajñasya duriṣṭaṃ tad varuṇo gṛhṇati tad eva tad avayajati
15.1.d: मत्सि वायुम् इष्टये राधसे न इति वारुण्य् एषा भवति यद् वै यज्ञस्य दुरिष्टं तद् वरुणो गृह्णति तद् एव तद् अवयजति
15.1.m: With 'Exhilarate Vāyu for our wish, for wealth...', this [verse] belongs to Varuṇa. What is badly sacrificed in the sacrifice, that Varuṇa seizes; he thereby expiates it.
The chant-triplet is for securing the in-breaths and out-breaths.

15.1.s: daśarco bhavati daśākṣarā virāṭa vairājam annam annādyasyāvarudhyai
15.1.d: दशर्चो भवति दशाक्षरा विराट वैराजम् अन्नम् अन्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै
15.1.m: There is a ten-verse hymn. The virāj has ten syllables; food is of virāj-nature; [it is] for securing food.

15.1.s: saprabhṛtayo bhavāntīndriyasya vīryasya rasasyānaticārāya yatra vai devā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ rasam apaśyaṃs tad anunyatudan
15.1.d: सप्रभृतयो भवान्तीन्द्रियस्य वीर्यस्य रसस्यानतिचाराय यत्र वै देवा इन्द्रियं वीर्यं रसम् अपश्यंस् तद् अनुन्यतुदन्
15.1.m: There are verses with offerings for the non-passing away of Indra's heroic power and sap. Where the gods saw Indra's heroic power and sap, there they struck after.

15.1.s: aṣṭāśaphāḥ paśavaḥ śaphaśas tat paśūn āpnoti aṣṭākṣarā gāyatrī tejo brahmavarcasaṃ gāyatrī teja eva brahmavarcasam avarundhe
15.1.d: अष्टाशफाः पशवः शफशस् तत् पशून् आप्नोति अष्टाक्षरा गायत्री तेजो ब्रह्मवर्चसं गायत्री तेज एव ब्रह्मवर्चसम् अवरुन्धे
15.1.m: (Cattle have eight hoofs; hoof by hoof he thus obtains cattle.) The gāyatrī has eight syllables; the gāyatrī is splendour and brahminical lustre; he secures splendour and brahminical lustre.
There are six-verse hymns for maintaining the seasons.

15.1.s: catvāraḥ ṣaḍṛcā bhavanti caturviṃśatir ardhamāsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsara eva pratitiṣṭhati
15.1.d: चत्वारः षडृचा भवन्ति चतुर्विंशतिर् अर्धमासाः संवत्सरः संवत्सर एव प्रतितिष्ठति
15.1.m: There are four six-verse hymns; twenty-four half-months make a year; he firmly establishes himself in the year.

15.1.s: savān uttamaḥ ṣaḍṛco bhavaty ubhayasya parokṣapratyakṣasyāvarudhyai
15.1.d: सवान् उत्तमः षडृचो भवत्य् उभयस्य परोक्षप्रत्यक्षस्यावरुध्यै
15.1.m: The last six-verse hymn is with libations, for securing both the unmanifest and the manifest.

15.1.s: tṛca uttamo bhavati yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
15.1.d: तृच उत्तमो भवति येनैव प्राणेन प्रयन्ति तम् अभ्युद्यन्ति
15.1.m: The last is a triplet; by whatever breath they go forth, into that they rise.

15.1.s: aṣṭācatvāriṃśa eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai prajātyai
15.1.d: अष्टाचत्वारिंश एव स्तोमो भवति प्रतिष्ठायै प्रजात्यै
15.1.m: The stoma is forty-eight-fold, for firm support and procreation.

15.2.s: aganma mahā namasā yaviṣṭham ity āgneyam ājyaṃ bhavati
15.2.d: अगन्म महा नमसा यविष्ठम् इत्य् आग्नेयम् आज्यं भवति
15.2.m: 'We have approached the youngest with great homage' is the ājyastotra to Agni.

15.2.s: gacchantīva vā ete ye navamam ahar gacchanti
15.2.d: गच्छन्तीव वा एते ये नवमम् अहर् गच्छन्ति
15.2.m: They, as it were, truly go forth, who go to the ninth day.

15.2.s: yo dīdāya samiddhasve duroṇa iti dīdāyeva hy eṣa yo navabhir aharbhis tuṣṭuvānaḥ svāhutam iti svāhuto hy eṣa yo navabhir aharbhir āhuto viśvataḥ pratyañcam iti viśvato hy eṣa pratyaṅ
15.2.d: यो दीदाय समिद्धस्वे दुरोण इति दीदायेव ह्य् एष यो नवभिर् अहर्भिस् तुष्टुवानः स्वाहुतम् इति स्वाहुतो ह्य् एष यो नवभिर् अहर्भिर् आहुतो विश्वतः प्रत्यञ्चम् इति विश्वतो ह्य् एष प्रत्यङ्
15.2.m: With 'Who has shone, kindled in his own house...', he who has chanted with nine days shines as it were. With 'well-offered...', for he who has been offered to with nine days is well-offered. With 'turned towards all sides...', for he is turned towards all sides.

15.2.s: tvaṃ varuṇa uta mitro agna iti vāruṇy eṣā bhavati yad vai yajñasya duriṣṭaṃ tad varuṇo gṛhṇati tad eva tad avayajati
15.2.d: त्वं वरुण उत मित्रो अग्न इति वारुण्य् एषा भवति यद् वै यज्ञस्य दुरिष्टं तद् वरुणो गृह्णति तद् एव तद् अवयजति
15.2.m: With 'You, Agni, are Varuṇa and Mitra...', this [verse] belongs to Varuṇa. What is badly sacrificed in the sacrifice, that Varuṇa seizes; he thereby expiates it.

15.2.s: mitraṃ huve pūtadakṣam iti rāthantaraṃ maitrāvaruṇam
15.2.d: मित्रं हुवे पूतदक्षम् इति राथन्तरं मैत्रावरुणम्
15.2.m: 'I invoke Mitra of purified discernment' is the Rathantara-based [ājyastotra] to Mitra and Varuṇa.

15.2.s: ugragādham iva vā etad yac chandomās tad yathāta ugragādhe vyatiṣajya gāhanta evam evaitad rūpe vyatiṣajati chandomānām asaṃvyāthāya
15.2.d: उग्रगाधम् इव वा एतद् यच् छन्दोमास् तद् यथात उग्रगाधे व्यतिषज्य गाहन्त एवम् एवैतद् रूपे व्यतिषजति छन्दोमानाम् असंव्याथाय
15.2.m: The Chandomas are like a fierce ford. Just as they plunge into a fierce ford by joining together, in this same way he intertwines the two forms for the Chandomas not to be shaken.

15.2.s: mahāṃ indro ya ojasā ity aindram aṣṭamena vai devā ahnendram avājayann avamena pāpmānam aghnann ahar evaitena mahayanti
15.2.d: महां इन्द्रो य ओजसा इत्य् ऐन्द्रम् अष्टमेन वै देवा अह्नेन्द्रम् अवाजयन्न् अवमेन पाप्मानम् अघ्नन्न् अहर् एवैतेन महयन्ति
15.2.m: With 'Great is Indra, who by his might...', it belongs to Indra. By the eighth day, the gods invigorated Indra; by the ninth, they struck down evil. With this they magnify the day.

15.2.s: tā huve yayor idam iti rāthantaram aindrāgnam
15.2.d: ता हुवे ययोर् इदम् इति राथन्तरम् ऐन्द्राग्नम्
15.2.m: 'I invoke those two, to whom belongs this...' is the Rathantara-based [ājyastotra] to Indra and Agni.

15.2.s: ugragādham iva vā etad yac chandomās tad yathāta ugragādhe vyatiṣajya gāhanta evam evaitad rūpe vyatiṣajati chandomānām asaṃvyāthāya stomaḥ
15.2.d: उग्रगाधम् इव वा एतद् यच् छन्दोमास् तद् यथात उग्रगाधे व्यतिषज्य गाहन्त एवम् एवैतद् रूपे व्यतिषजति छन्दोमानाम् असंव्याथाय स्तोमः
15.2.m: The Chandomas are like a fierce ford. Just as they plunge into a fierce ford by joining together, in this same way he intertwines the two forms for the Chandomas not to be shaken; [such is] the stoma.

15.3.s: pavamānasya jighnato hareś candrā asṛkṣata iti harivatyo gāyatryo bhavanti chandomānām ayātayāmatāyai
15.3.d: पवमानस्य जिघ्नतो हरेश् चन्द्रा असृक्षत इति हरिवत्यो गायत्र्यो भवन्ति छन्दोमानाम् अयातयामतायै
15.3.m: With 'The bright drops of the soma flowing as it slays, of the tawny one, have poured forth...', these are gāyatrī verses containing the word 'tawny', for the non-exhaustion of the Chandomas.

15.3.s: pavamānasya jighnata iti vai bṛhato rūpaṃ hareś candrā asṛkṣata iti jagatyā ubhayoḥ saharūpam upaiti sāmnaś ca chandasaś ca
15.3.d: पवमानस्य जिघ्नत इति वै बृहतो रूपं हरेश् चन्द्रा असृक्षत इति जगत्या उभयोः सहरूपम् उपैति साम्नश् च छन्दसश् च
15.3.m: 'Of the soma flowing as it slays' is the form of the Bṛhat. 'The bright drops of the tawny one have poured forth' is of the jagatī. He brings together the forms of both, of the sāman and of the metre.

15.3.s: parīto ṣiñcatā sutam iti parivatyo bhavanty anto vai navamam ahas tasyaitāḥ paryāptyai
15.3.d: परीतो षिञ्चता सुतम् इति परिवत्यो भवन्त्य् अन्तो वै नवमम् अहस् तस्यैताः पर्याप्त्यै
15.3.m: With 'Pour around the pressed soma...', these are verses containing 'around'. The ninth day is an end; these are for its completion.

15.3.s: asāvi somo aruṣo vṛṣā harir iti jagatyas satyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa tasmāt triṣṭubhāṃ loke kriyante
15.3.d: असावि सोमो अरुषो वृषा हरिर् इति जगत्यस् सत्यस् त्रिष्टुभो रूपेण तस्मात् त्रिष्टुभां लोके क्रियन्ते
15.3.m: With 'The tawny, reddish bull, Soma, has been pressed...', being jagatī verses, they have the form of the triṣṭubh; therefore they are performed in the place of the triṣṭubh verses.

15.3.s: gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
15.3.d: गायत्रं भवति यद् एव गायत्रस्य ब्राह्मणम्
15.3.m: There is the Gāyatra; whatever is the brāhmaṇa of the Gāyatra [applies here].

15.3.s: bharadvājasyādārasṛd bhavati
15.3.d: भरद्वाजस्यादारसृद् भवति
15.3.m: There is the Adārasṛt of Bharadvāja.

15.3.s: divodāsaṃ vai bharadvājapurohitaṃ nanājanāḥ paryayanta sa upāsīdad ṛṣe gātuṃ me vindeti tasmā etena sāmnā gātum avindad gātuvid vā etatsāmānena dāre nāsṛnmeti tad adārasṛto 'dārasṛttvaṃ vindate gātuṃ na dāre dhāvaty adārasṛtā tuṣṭuvānaḥ
15.3.d: दिवोदासं वै भरद्वाजपुरोहितं ननाजनाः पर्ययन्त स उपासीदद् ऋषे गातुं मे विन्देति तस्मा एतेन साम्ना गातुम् अविन्दद् गातुविद् वा एतत्सामानेन दारे नासृन्मेति तद् अदारसृतो ऽदारसृत्त्वं विन्दते गातुं न दारे धावत्य् अदारसृता तुष्टुवानः
15.3.m: Various peoples surrounded Divodāsa whose purohita was Bharadvāja. He approached [Bharadvāja, saying]: 'O ṛṣi, find a way for me!' Through this sāman he found a way for him. This sāman indeed finds a way. [Saying]: 'By this we did not run into a cleft,' that is the reason why the Adārasṛt has the nature of the Adārasṛt. He who has praised with the Adārasṛt finds a way [and] does not run into a cleft.

15.3.s: surūpaṃ bhavati yad eva surūpasya brāhmaṇam
15.3.d: सुरूपं भवति यद् एव सुरूपस्य ब्राह्मणम्
15.3.m: There is the Surūpa; whatever is the brāhmaṇa of the Surūpa [applies here].

15.3.s: hariśrīnidhanaṃ bhavati
15.3.d: हरिश्रीनिधनं भवति
15.3.m: There is [the chant] with the cadence 'hariśrī'.

15.3.s: paśavo vai hariśriyaḥ paśūnām avarudhyai śriyaṃ ca haraś copaiti tuṣṭuvānaḥ
15.3.d: पशवो वै हरिश्रियः पशूनाम् अवरुध्यै श्रियं च हरश् चोपैति तुष्टुवानः
15.3.m: Cattle are indeed 'hariśrī' for the obtaining of cattle. He who has praised approaches both glory and lustre.

15.3.s: saindhukṣitaṃ bhavati yad eva saindhukṣitasya brāhmaṇam
15.3.d: सैन्धुक्षितं भवति यद् एव सैन्धुक्षितस्य ब्राह्मणम्
15.3.m: There is the Saindhukṣita; whatever is the brāhmaṇa of the Saindhukṣita [applies here].

15.3.s: gatanidhanaṃ vābhravaṃ bhavati gatyai
15.3.d: गतनिधनं वाभ्रवं भवति गत्यै
15.3.m: There is the Vābhrava with the cadence 'gatam' for going.

15.3.s: vabhrur vā etena kaumbhyo 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
15.3.d: वभ्रुर् वा एतेन कौम्भ्यो ऽञ्जसा स्वर्गं लोकम् अपश्यत् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्यानुख्यात्यै स्वर्गाल् लोकान् न च्यवते तुष्टुवानः
15.3.m: Vabhru, the son of Kumbha, saw the heavenly world straight away by means of this [sāman]; [it is] for the discerning of the heavenly world. He who has praised does not fall from the heavenly world.

15.3.s: iḍānāṃ saṃkṣāro bhavati
15.3.d: इडानां संक्षारो भवति
15.3.m: There is the Saṃkṣāra of the Iḍās.

15.3.s: paśavo vā iḍā paśavaś chandomāḥ paśuṣv eva tat paśūn dadhāti
15.3.d: पशवो वा इडा पशवश् छन्दोमाः पशुष्व् एव तत् पशून् दधाति
15.3.m: The iḍās are cattle, the chandomas are cattle; he thus places cattle in cattle.

15.3.s: ṛṣabhaḥ pāvamāno bhavati
15.3.d: ऋषभः पावमानो भवति
15.3.m: There is the Ṛṣabha-pāvamāna.

15.3.s: paśavo vai chandomāḥ paśuṣv eva tan mithunam apyarjati prajātyai na ha vā anṛṣabhāḥ paśavaḥ prajāyante
15.3.d: पशवो वै छन्दोमाः पशुष्व् एव तन् मिथुनम् अप्यर्जति प्रजात्यै न ह वा अनृषभाः पशवः प्रजायन्ते
15.3.m: The chandomas are cattle; he thus unites a productive pair among cattle for procreation. Indeed, cattle without a bull do not propagate.

15.3.s: pṛṣṭhaṃ bhavati
15.3.d: पृष्ठं भवति

15.3.s: pṛṣṭhaṃ vā etad ahnāṃ yan navamaṃ pṛṣṭha eva tat pṛṣṭhena stuvate pratiṣṭhāyai
15.3.d: पृष्ठं वा एतद् अह्नां यन् नवमं पृष्ठ एव तत् पृष्ठेन स्तुवते प्रतिष्ठायै
15.3.m: A pṛṣṭha indeed among the days is this ninth day. They thus praise with a pṛṣṭha on a pṛṣṭha for a firm standing.

15.3.s: kaulmalabarhiṣaṃ bhavati
15.3.d: कौल्मलबर्हिषं भवति
15.3.m: There is the Kaulmalabarhiṣa.

15.3.s: kulmalabarhir vā etena svargaṃ lokam apaśyat prajātiṃ bhūmānam agacchat prajāyate bahur bhavati kaulmalabarhiṣeṇa tuṣṭuvānaḥ
15.3.d: कुल्मलबर्हिर् वा एतेन स्वर्गं लोकम् अपश्यत् प्रजातिं भूमानम् अगच्छत् प्रजायते बहुर् भवति कौल्मलबर्हिषेण तुष्टुवानः
15.3.m: Kulmalabarhis saw the heavenly world by means of this [sāman] and attained procreation [and] abundance. He who has praised with the Kaulmalabarhiṣa propagates [and] becomes manifold.

15.3.s: arkapuṣpaṃ bhavati
15.3.d: अर्कपुष्पं भवति

15.3.s: annaṃ vai devā arka iti vadanti rasam asya puṣpām iti sarasam evānnādyam avarundhe 'rkapuṣpeṇa tuṣṭuvānaḥ
15.3.d: अन्नं वै देवा अर्क इति वदन्ति रसम् अस्य पुष्पाम् इति सरसम् एवान्नाद्यम् अवरुन्धे ऽर्कपुष्पेण तुष्टुवानः
15.3.m: The gods call food 'arka', [and] its sap 'puṣpa'. He who has praised with the Arkapuṣpa secures food together with its sap.

15.3.s: dairghyaśravasaṃ bhavati
15.3.d: दैर्घ्यश्रवसं भवति
15.3.m: There is the Dairghaśravasa.

15.3.s: dīrghaśravā vai rājanya ṛṣir jyog aparuddho 'śanāyaṃś caran sa etad dairghaśravasam apaśyat tena sarvābhyo digbhyo 'nnādyam avārundha sarvābhyo adigbhyo 'nnādyam avārundhe dairghaśravasena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
15.3.d: दीर्घश्रवा वै राजन्य ऋषिर् ज्योग् अपरुद्धो ऽशनायंश् चरन् स एतद् दैर्घश्रवसम् अपश्यत् तेन सर्वाभ्यो दिग्भ्यो ऽन्नाद्यम् अवारुन्ध सर्वाभ्यो अदिग्भ्यो ऽन्नाद्यम् अवारुन्धे दैर्घश्रवसेन तुष्टुवानः
15.3.m: Dīrghaśravas, a royal seer, being long excluded [from his kingdom] and wandering about hungry, saw this Dairghaśravasa. By it he secured food from all quarters. He who has praised with the Dairghaśravasa secures food from all quarters.

15.3.s: vaiyaśvaṃ bhavati yad eva vaiyaśvasya brāhmaṇam
15.3.d: वैयश्वं भवति यद् एव वैयश्वस्य ब्राह्मणम्
15.3.m: There is the Vaiyaśva; whatever is the brāhmaṇa of the Vaiyaśva [applies here].

15.3.s: abhīśavaṃ yad ābhīśavasya
15.3.d: अभीशवं यद् आभीशवस्य
15.3.m: The Ābhīśava; whatever [is the brāhmaṇa] of the Ābhīśava [applies here].

15.3.s: devasthānaṃ bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai saṃskṛti bhavati saṃṃskṛtyai
15.3.d: देवस्थानं भवति प्रतिष्ठायै संस्कृति भवति संंस्कृत्यै
15.3.m: There is the Devasthāna for a firm standing; there is the Saṃkṛti for proper preparation.

15.3.s: ahar vā etad avlīyata tad devā devasthāne tiṣṭhantaḥ saṃkṛtinā samaskurvaṃs tat saṃkṛteḥ saṃkṛtitvaṃ devasthānena vai devāḥ svarge loke pratyatiṣṭhan svarge loke pratitiṣṭām ety etat
15.3.d: अहर् वा एतद् अव्लीयत तद् देवा देवस्थाने तिष्ठन्तः संकृतिना समस्कुर्वंस् तत् संकृतेः संकृतित्वं देवस्थानेन वै देवाः स्वर्गे लोके प्रत्यतिष्ठन् स्वर्गे लोके प्रतितिष्टाम् एत्य् एतत्
15.3.m: This day collapsed; the gods, standing in the Devasthāna, repaired it with the Saṃkṛti; that is the reason why the Saṃkṛti has the nature of the Saṃkṛti. By the Devasthāna the gods stood firmly in the heavenly world; [it means]: 'Let us stand firmly in the heavenly world.'

15.3.s: varuṇāya devatā rājyāya nātiṣṭhanta sa etad devasthānam apaśyat tato vai tās tasmai rājyāyātiṣṭhanta tiṣṭhante 'smai samānāḥ śreṣṭhyāya
15.3.d: वरुणाय देवता राज्याय नातिष्ठन्त स एतद् देवस्थानम् अपश्यत् ततो वै तास् तस्मै राज्यायातिष्ठन्त तिष्ठन्ते ऽस्मै समानाः श्रेष्ठ्याय
15.3.m: The deities did not submit to Varuṇa for kingship. He saw this Devasthāna; thereupon they submitted to him for kingship. Equals submit to him for pre-eminence—

15.3.s: kṣatrasyevāsya prakāśo bhavati pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda
15.3.d: क्षत्रस्येवास्य प्रकाशो भवति प्रतितिष्ठति य एवं वेद
15.3.m: his manifestation becomes like that of the nobility, [and] he stands firmly, who knows this.

15.3.s: bhargo bhargeṇa tuṣṭuvāno bhavati yaśo yaśasā
15.3.d: भर्गो भर्गेण तुष्टुवानो भवति यशो यशसा
15.3.m: He who has praised with the Bharga becomes splendour; [he who has praised] with the Yaśas [becomes] glory.

15.3.s: vāsiṣṭhaṃ bhavati yad eva vāsiṣṭhasya brāhmaṇam
15.3.d: वासिष्ठं भवति यद् एव वासिष्ठस्य ब्राह्मणम्
15.3.m: There is the Vāsiṣṭha; whatever is the brāhmaṇa of the Vāsiṣṭha [applies here].

15.3.s: dīrghatamaso 'rko bhavaty annaṃ vā arko 'nnādyasyāvarudhyai
15.3.d: दीर्घतमसो ऽर्को भवत्य् अन्नं वा अर्को ऽन्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै
15.3.m: There is the Arka of Dīrghatamas. Food is arka, for the securing of food.

15.3.s: sāmarājaṃ bhavati sāmrājyam ādhipatyaṃ gacchati sāmarājñā tuṣṭuvānaḥ
15.3.d: सामराजं भवति साम्राज्यम् आधिपत्यं गच्छति सामराज्ञा तुष्टुवानः
15.3.m: There is the Sāmarāja. He who has praised with the Sāmarāja attains universal sovereignty and supreme overlordship.

15.3.s: tad u saṃvad ity āhuḥ saṃvatā vai devāḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ prāyann udvatodāyan
15.3.d: तद् उ संवद् इत्य् आहुः संवता वै देवाः स्वर्गं लोकं प्रायन्न् उद्वतोदायन्
15.3.m: Now they say: 'It is a gentle slope.' By a gentle slope the gods went forth to the heavenly world; they went up by an ascent.

15.3.s: nidhanāntāḥ pavamānā bhavanty ahno dhṛtyai stomaḥ
15.3.d: निधनान्ताः पवमाना भवन्त्य् अह्नो धृत्यै स्तोमः
15.3.m: The pavamāna [chants] end in cadences for the support of the day; the stoma [is completed].

15.4.s: śrāyanta iva sūryam iti sūryavatyo bhavanti
15.4.d: श्रायन्त इव सूर्यम् इति सूर्यवत्यो भवन्ति
15.4.m: [The verses beginning]: 'As if clinging to the sun' contain [the word] 'sun'.

15.4.s: ādityadevatyaṃ hy etad ahar anto vai sūro 'nta etan navamam ahnām anta eva tad antena stuvate pratiṣṭhāyai
15.4.d: आदित्यदेवत्यं ह्य् एतद् अहर् अन्तो वै सूरो ऽन्त एतन् नवमम् अह्नाम् अन्त एव तद् अन्तेन स्तुवते प्रतिष्ठायै
15.4.m: For this day has the Ādityas as deities. The sun is an end; this ninth of the days is an end. They thus praise with an end at the end, for a firm standing.

15.4.s: yata indra bhayāvahe tato no abhayaṃ kṛdhi | maghavañ chagdhi tava tan na ūtaye vidviṣo vimṛdho jahi iti dviṣaś caiva mṛdhaś ca navamenāhnā vihatya daśamenāhnottiṣṭhanti
15.4.d: यत इन्द्र भयावहे ततो नो अभयं कृधि । मघवञ् छग्धि तव तन् न ऊतये विद्विषो विमृधो जहि इति द्विषश् चैव मृधश् च नवमेनाह्ना विहत्य दशमेनाह्नोत्तिष्ठन्ति
15.4.m: 'Wherefrom, O Indra, we fear, therefrom make fearlessness for us; O generous one, be capable of that for our aid; slay the haters, the combatants'—having destroyed their haters and combatants on the ninth day, they rise on the tenth day.

15.4.s: śrīr vai śrāyantīyaṃ śrīr navamam ahaḥ śriyam eva tac chriyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati
15.4.d: श्रीर् वै श्रायन्तीयं श्रीर् नवमम् अहः श्रियम् एव तच् छ्रियां प्रतिष्ठापयति
15.4.m: The Śrāyantīya is prosperity; the ninth day is prosperity. He thus establishes prosperity in prosperity.

15.4.s: samantena paśukāmaḥ stuvīta purodhākāmaḥ samantena stuvīta
15.4.d: समन्तेन पशुकामः स्तुवीत पुरोधाकामः समन्तेन स्तुवीत
15.4.m: One who desires cattle should praise with the Samanta; one who desires the office of purohita should praise with the Samanta.

15.4.s: āgneyī pṛthivy āgneyo brāhmaṇa aindrī dyaur aindro rājanyo 'ntarikṣeṇa dyāvāpṛthivī samante antarikṣeṇaivainaṃ samantaṃ karoti vindate paśūn pra purodhām āpnoti ya evaṃ vidvān samantena stuvate stomaḥ
15.4.d: आग्नेयी पृथिव्य् आग्नेयो ब्राह्मण ऐन्द्री द्यौर् ऐन्द्रो राजन्यो ऽन्तरिक्षेण द्यावापृथिवी समन्ते अन्तरिक्षेणैवैनं समन्तं करोति विन्दते पशून् प्र पुरोधाम् आप्नोति य एवं विद्वान् समन्तेन स्तुवते स्तोमः
15.4.m: The earth belongs to Agni, the brāhmaṇa belongs to Agni; heaven belongs to Indra, the noble belongs to Indra; heaven and earth are contiguous through the atmosphere. Through the atmosphere he makes him contiguous [to both]; he who, knowing this, praises with the Samanta finds cattle [and] attains the office of purohita; the stoma [is completed].

15.5.s: tvaṃ somāsi dhārayur iti gāyatrī bhavaty ahno dhṛtyai tvam iti bṛhato rūpaṃ bārhataṃ hy etad ahaḥ
15.5.d: त्वं सोमासि धारयुर् इति गायत्री भवत्य् अह्नो धृत्यै त्वम् इति बृहतो रूपं बार्हतं ह्य् एतद् अहः
15.5.m: 'Thou, O Soma, art full of stream' is a gāyatrī, for the support of the day. 'Thou' is the characteristic of the Bṛhat, for this day belongs to the Bṛhat.

15.5.s: tvaṃ hy aṅga daivyā iti tvam iti bṛhato rūpaṃ bārhataṃ hy etad ahaḥ
15.5.d: त्वं ह्य् अङ्ग दैव्या इति त्वम् इति बृहतो रूपं बार्हतं ह्य् एतद् अहः
15.5.m: 'For thou, indeed, divine'—'thou' is the characteristic of the Bṛhat, for this day belongs to the Bṛhat.

15.5.s: pavasva deva vītaya iti bṛhato rūpaṃ bārhataṃ hy etad ahaḥ
15.5.d: पवस्व देव वीतय इति बृहतो रूपं बार्हतं ह्य् एतद् अहः
15.5.m: 'Flow, O god, for enjoyment' is the characteristic of the Bṛhat, for this day belongs to the Bṛhat.

15.5.s: parityaṃ haryataṃ harim iti parivatyo bhavanty anto vai navamam ahasyaitāḥ paryāptyai
15.5.d: परित्यं हर्यतं हरिम् इति परिवत्यो भवन्त्य् अन्तो वै नवमम् अहस्यैताः पर्याप्त्यै
15.5.m: 'The encircling, desirable tawny one'—they contain [the word] 'pari' ('around'). The ninth day is the end; [they serve] for the attainment of it.

15.5.s: pavasva soma mahe dakṣāya ity akṣarapaṅktiḥ stomānāṃ prabhūtir atho etad dhy evaitarhi chando 'yātayāma yad akṣarapaṅktis tena chandomā ayātayāmānaḥ kriyante brahmavādino vadanti yat ṣaḍahe stomāś chandāṃsy āpyante kiṃ chandasaś chandomā ity etac chandaso yad etā akṣarapaṅktaya iti brūyāt
15.5.d: पवस्व सोम महे दक्षाय इत्य् अक्षरपङ्क्तिः स्तोमानां प्रभूतिर् अथो एतद् ध्य् एवैतर्हि छन्दो ऽयातयाम यद् अक्षरपङ्क्तिस् तेन छन्दोमा अयातयामानः क्रियन्ते ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति यत् षडहे स्तोमाश् छन्दांस्य् आप्यन्ते किं छन्दसश् छन्दोमा इत्य् एतच् छन्दसो यद् एता अक्षरपङ्क्तय इति ब्रूयात्
15.5.m: 'Flow, O Soma, for great capacity'—the akṣarapaṅkti is the abundance of stomas; and also, this metre is fresh at this point, since it is an akṣarapaṅkti. Thereby the chandomas are rendered fresh. The theologians say: 'Since the stomas and metres are exhausted in the six-day period, of what metre are the chandomas?' One should answer: 'Of this metre, since these are akṣarapaṅktis.'

15.5.s: upoṣu jātam apturam iti gāyatryas satyo jagatyo rūpeṇa tasmāt jagatīnāṃ loke kriyante
15.5.d: उपोषु जातम् अप्तुरम् इति गायत्र्यस् सत्यो जगत्यो रूपेण तस्मात् जगतीनां लोके क्रियन्ते
15.5.m: 'Near to him that was born water-crossing'—being gāyatrīs, they have the characteristic of jagatīs; therefore they are performed in the place of jagatīs.

15.5.s: gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brahmaṇam
15.5.d: गायत्रं भवति यद् एव गायत्रस्य ब्रह्मणम्
15.5.m: There is the Gāyatra; whatever is the brāhmaṇa of the Gāyatra [applies here].

15.5.s: āśvasūktaṃ bhavati
15.5.d: आश्वसूक्तं भवति

15.5.s: agniṃ vai pūrvair aharbhir ājuhoty athaitad ādityadaivatyam ahaḥ śukra āhuta ity asau vā ādityaḥ śukras tam evaitenājuhoti
15.5.d: अग्निं वै पूर्वैर् अहर्भिर् आजुहोत्य् अथैतद् आदित्यदैवत्यम् अहः शुक्र आहुत इत्य् असौ वा आदित्यः शुक्रस् तम् एवैतेनाजुहोति
15.5.m: With the preceding days he pours libations to Agni; but this day has the Āditya as its deity. [Saying]: 'The bright [Soma] has been offered'—yonder Āditya is the bright one; to him he pours the libation with this.

15.5.s: śāmmadaṃ bhavati
15.5.d: शाम्मदं भवति

15.5.s: śammad vā etenāṅgiraso 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāl lokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
15.5.d: शम्मद् वा एतेनाङ्गिरसो ऽञ्जसा स्वर्गं लोकम् अपश्यत् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्यानुख्यात्यै स्वर्गाल् लोकान् न च्यवते तुष्टुवानः
15.5.m: Śammant the Āṅgirasa saw the heavenly world straight away by means of this [sāman]; [it is] for the discerning of the heavenly world. He who has praised does not fall from the heavenly world.

15.5.s: āśiṣam evāsmā etenāśāste sāma hi satyāśīḥ
15.5.d: आशिषम् एवास्मा एतेनाशास्ते साम हि सत्याशीः
15.5.m: With it he invokes a blessing upon him, for the sāman is a true blessing.

15.5.s: dāvasur vā etad āṅgirasaḥ paśukāmaḥ sāmāpaśyat tena sahasraṃ paśūn asṛjat yad etat sāma bhavati paśūnāṃ puṣṭyai
15.5.d: दावसुर् वा एतद् आङ्गिरसः पशुकामः सामापश्यत् तेन सहस्रं पशून् असृजत् यद् एतत् साम भवति पशूनां पुष्ट्यै
15.5.m: Dāvasu the Āṅgirasa, desiring cattle, saw this sāman; with it he brought forth a thousand cattle. Since this sāman is used, it is for the thriving of cattle.

15.5.s: pratīcīneḍaṃ kāśītaṃ bhavati
15.5.d: प्रतीचीनेडं काशीतं भवति
15.5.m: There is the Kāśīta with reversed iḍās.

15.5.s: parācībhir vā anyābhir iḍābhī reto dadhad athaitat pratīcīneḍaṃ kāśītaṃ prajātyai tasmāt parāñco garbhāḥ sambhavanti pratyañcaḥ prajāyante tasmād ute 'vācīnabilebhyo nāvapadyanta etena hy eva te dhṛtāḥ
15.5.d: पराचीभिर् वा अन्याभिर् इडाभी रेतो दधद् अथैतत् प्रतीचीनेडं काशीतं प्रजात्यै तस्मात् पराञ्चो गर्भाः सम्भवन्ति प्रत्यञ्चः प्रजायन्ते तस्माद् उते ऽवाचीनबिलेभ्यो नावपद्यन्त एतेन ह्य् एव ते धृताः
15.5.m: With the other iḍās turning forward he deposits the seed; then this Kāśīta has reversed iḍās for procreation. Therefore embryos come into being turning forward, [and] are born turning backward. And therefore they do not fall out of the orifices turned downward, for by this they are held.

15.5.s: hāviṣkṛtaṃ bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai kṛtānuvāda eva saḥ
15.5.d: हाविष्कृतं भवति प्रतिष्ठायै कृतानुवाद एव सः
15.5.m: There is the Hāviṣkṛta for a firm standing; it is a repetition of what has been accomplished.

15.5.s: sauparṇaṃ bhavati yad eva sauparṇasya brahmaṇam
15.5.d: सौपर्णं भवति यद् एव सौपर्णस्य ब्रह्मणम्
15.5.m: There is the Sauparṇa; whatever is the brāhmaṇa of the Sauparṇa [applies here].

15.5.s: vaiśvamanasaṃ bhavati
15.5.d: वैश्वमनसं भवति
15.5.m: There is the Vaiśvamanasa.

15.5.s: viśvamanasaṃ vā ṛṣim adhyāyam udvrajitaṃ rakṣo 'gṛhṇāt tam indro 'cāyad ṛṣiṃ vai rakṣo 'grahīd iti tam abhyavadad ṛṣe kas tvaiṣa iti sthāṇur iti brūhīti rakṣo 'bravīt sa sthāṇur ity abravīt tasmai vā etena praharety asmā iṣīkāṃ vajraṃ prayacchann abravīt tenāsya sīmānam abhinat saiṣendreṇateṣīkā pāpmā vāva sa tam agṛhṇāt taṃ vaiśvamanasenāpāhatāpapāpmānaṃ hate vaiśvamanasena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
15.5.d: विश्वमनसं वा ऋषिम् अध्यायम् उद्व्रजितं रक्षो ऽगृह्णात् तम् इन्द्रो ऽचायद् ऋषिं वै रक्षो ऽग्रहीद् इति तम् अभ्यवदद् ऋषे कस् त्वैष इति स्थाणुर् इति ब्रूहीति रक्षो ऽब्रवीत् स स्थाणुर् इत्य् अब्रवीत् तस्मै वा एतेन प्रहरेत्य् अस्मा इषीकां वज्रं प्रयच्छन्न् अब्रवीत् तेनास्य सीमानम् अभिनत् सैषेन्द्रेणतेषीका पाप्मा वाव स तम् अगृह्णात् तं वैश्वमनसेनापाहतापपाप्मानं हते वैश्वमनसेन तुष्टुवानः
15.5.m: A demon seized the seer Viśvamanas when he went forth to study. Indra noticed him: ‘A demon indeed has seized the seer.’ He said to him: ‘Seer, who is this by you?’ The demon said: ‘Say: “A post.”’ He said: ‘A post.’ Offering him a reed as a thunderbolt, [Indra] said: ‘Strike him with this!’ With it, he split his skull. That reed became an Indra-reed. Evil indeed it was that seized him; he smote away that evil with the Vaiśvamanasa [sāman]. He who praises with the Vaiśvamanasa smites away evil.

15.5.s: gaurīvitaṃ bhavati yad eva gaurīvitasya brāhmaṇam
15.5.d: गौरीवितं भवति यद् एव गौरीवितस्य ब्राह्मणम्
15.5.m: There is the Gaurīvita; [its purpose is] just what is the explanation of the Gaurīvita.

15.5.s: nihavo bhavaty annādyasyāvarudhyai
15.5.d: निहवो भवत्य् अन्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै
15.5.m: There is the Nihava, for the obtainment of food.

15.5.s: hīti vā annaṃ pradīyata īty āgrir annam atti
15.5.d: हीति वा अन्नं प्रदीयत ईत्य् आग्रिर् अन्नम् अत्ति
15.5.m: With 'Hā-i', indeed, food is offered; with 'I', the hungry man eats food.

15.5.s: ṛṣayo vā indraṃ pratyakṣa nāpaśyan sa vasiṣṭho 'kāmayata katham indraṃ pratyakṣaṃ paśyeyam iti sa etan nihavam apaśyat tato vai sa indraṃ pratyakṣam apaśyat sa enam abravīd brāhmaṇaṃ te vakṣyāmi yathā tvatpurohitā bharatāḥ prajaniṣyante 'tha mānyebhya ṛṣibhyo mā pravoca iti tasmā etān stomabhāgān abravīt tato vai vasiṣṭhapurohitā bharatāḥ prājāyanta sendraṃ vā etat sāma yad etat sāma bhavati sendratvāya
15.5.d: ऋषयो वा इन्द्रं प्रत्यक्ष नापश्यन् स वसिष्ठो ऽकामयत कथम् इन्द्रं प्रत्यक्षं पश्येयम् इति स एतन् निहवम् अपश्यत् ततो वै स इन्द्रं प्रत्यक्षम् अपश्यत् स एनम् अब्रवीद् ब्राह्मणं ते वक्ष्यामि यथा त्वत्पुरोहिता भरताः प्रजनिष्यन्ते ऽथ मान्येभ्य ऋषिभ्यो मा प्रवोच इति तस्मा एतान् स्तोमभागान् अब्रवीत् ततो वै वसिष्ठपुरोहिता भरताः प्राजायन्त सेन्द्रं वा एतत् साम यद् एतत् साम भवति सेन्द्रत्वाय
15.5.m: The seers did not see Indra face to face. Vasiṣṭha desired: ‘How may I see Indra face to face?’ He saw this Nihava [sāman]. Thence indeed he saw Indra face to face. He said to him: ‘I will tell you a sacred teaching so that the Bharatas will propagate with you as their family priest; but do not proclaim me to the other seers.’ He told him these shares of the stoma. Thence indeed the Bharatas propagated with Vasiṣṭha as their family priest. This sāman possesses Indra; that this sāman is [used] is for possessing Indra.

15.5.s: yad vāhiṣṭhīyaṃ bhavati
15.5.d: यद् वाहिष्ठीयं भवति
15.5.m: That there is the Vāhiṣṭhīya:

15.5.s: brahmayaśasaṃ vā etāni sāmāny ṛcā śrotrīyāṇi brahmāyaśasī bhavati yad vāhiṣṭhīyena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
15.5.d: ब्रह्मयशसं वा एतानि सामान्य् ऋचा श्रोत्रीयाणि ब्रह्मायशसी भवति यद् वाहिष्ठीयेन तुष्टुवानः
15.5.m: These sāmans are brahminical glory, learned by recitation through the verse. He who praises with the Vāhiṣṭhīya becomes possessed of brahminical glory.

15.5.s: āsitaṃ bhavati yad evāsitasya brāhmaṇam
15.5.d: आसितं भवति यद् एवासितस्य ब्राह्मणम्
15.5.m: There is the Āsita; [its purpose is] just what is the explanation of the Āsita.

15.5.s: sādhraṃ bhavati siddhyai
15.5.d: साध्रं भवति सिद्ध्यै
15.5.m: There is the Sādhra, for success.

15.5.s: ākūpāraṃ bhavati
15.5.d: आकूपारं भवति

15.5.s: akūpāro vā etena kaśyapo jemānaṃ mahimānam agacchaj jemānaṃ mahimānaṃ gacchaty ākūpāreṇa tuṣṭuvānaḥ
15.5.d: अकूपारो वा एतेन कश्यपो जेमानं महिमानम् अगच्छज् जेमानं महिमानं गच्छत्य् आकूपारेण तुष्टुवानः
15.5.m: By this [sāman], Akūpāra Kāśyapa attained superior greatness. He who praises with the Ākūpāra attains superior greatness.

15.5.s: vidharma bhavati dharmasya vidhṛtyai
15.5.d: विधर्म भवति धर्मस्य विधृत्यै
15.5.m: There is the Vidharma, for the maintenance of order.

15.5.s: brahmavādino vadanti yat ṣaḍahe stomāś chandāṃsy āpyante kiṃ chandasaś chandomā iti puruṣacchandasa iti brūyāt puruṣo vai pāṅktaḥ puruṣo dvipadā chandomānām ayātayāmatāyai
15.5.d: ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति यत् षडहे स्तोमाश् छन्दांस्य् आप्यन्ते किं छन्दसश् छन्दोमा इति पुरुषच्छन्दस इति ब्रूयात् पुरुषो वै पाङ्क्तः पुरुषो द्विपदा छन्दोमानाम् अयातयामतायै
15.5.m: The theologians say: ‘Since in the six-day period the stomas and metres are exhausted, what metre are the Chandomas?’ One should say: ‘They have the human metre.’ Man is fivefold; man is two-footed, for the freshness of the Chandomas.

15.5.s: śrudhyaṃ bhavati
15.5.d: श्रुध्यं भवति

15.5.s: paśavo vai śrudhyaṃ paśūnām avarudhyai
15.5.d: पशवो वै श्रुध्यं पशूनाम् अवरुध्यै
15.5.m: The Śrudhya is cattle, for the obtainment of cattle.

15.5.s: prajāpatiḥ paśūn asṛjata te 'smāt sṛṣṭā apākrāmaṃs tān etena sāmnā śrūdhiyā ehiyety anvahvayat ta enam upāvartanta yad etat sāma bhavati paśūnām upāvṛtyai
15.5.d: प्रजापतिः पशून् असृजत ते ऽस्मात् सृष्टा अपाक्रामंस् तान् एतेन साम्ना श्रूधिया एहियेत्य् अन्वह्वयत् त एनम् उपावर्तन्त यद् एतत् साम भवति पशूनाम् उपावृत्यै
15.5.m: Prajāpati created cattle. Created from him, they departed. With this sāman he called after them: ‘Listen, come!’ They turned back to him. That this sāman is [used] is for the turning back of cattle.

15.5.s: upainaṃ paśava āvartante ya evaṃ veda
15.5.d: उपैनं पशव आवर्तन्ते य एवं वेद
15.5.m: Cattle turn back to him who knows thus.

15.5.s: gāyatrīṣu stuvanti pratiṣṭhāyai brahmavarcasāya yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyantīḍāntāḥ pavamānā bhavanti paśavo vā iḍā paśavaś chandomāḥ paśuṣv eva tat paśūn dadhāti stomaḥ
15.5.d: गायत्रीषु स्तुवन्ति प्रतिष्ठायै ब्रह्मवर्चसाय येनैव प्राणेन प्रयन्ति तम् अभ्युद्यन्तीडान्ताः पवमाना भवन्ति पशवो वा इडा पशवश् छन्दोमाः पशुष्व् एव तत् पशून् दधाति स्तोमः
15.5.m: They praise on gāyatrī [verses], for support, for brahminical lustre. With the very vital breath with which they set out, to that they rise. The Pavamānas end in the iḍā; the iḍā is cattle, the Chandomas are cattle; the stoma places cattle in cattle.

15.6.s: āgreyīṣu pūrveṣām ahnām ukthāni praṇayanty athaitasyāhna āgneyy aindrayāṃ praṇayanty ubhayor eva rūpayoḥ pratitiṣṭhati
15.6.d: आग्रेयीषु पूर्वेषाम् अह्नाम् उक्थानि प्रणयन्त्य् अथैतस्याह्न आग्नेय्य् ऐन्द्रयां प्रणयन्त्य् उभयोर् एव रूपयोः प्रतितिष्ठति
15.6.m: They bring forward the ukthas of the previous days on Agni-verses; then of this day, they bring forward [the ukthas] on a verse addressed to Agni and Indra. He finds support in both forms.

15.6.s: āgneyy aindrīṣu stuvanti brahma caiva tat kṣatraṃ ca sayujīkaroti brahmaiva kṣatrasya purastān nidadhāti brāhmaṇe kṣatraṃ ca viśaṃ cānuge karoti
15.6.d: आग्नेय्य् ऐन्द्रीषु स्तुवन्ति ब्रह्म चैव तत् क्षत्रं च सयुजीकरोति ब्रह्मैव क्षत्रस्य पुरस्तान् निदधाति ब्राह्मणे क्षत्रं च विशं चानुगे करोति
15.6.m: They praise on verses addressed to Agni and Indra; thereby he unites the brahminical order and the royal power. He places the brahminical order in front of the royal power, and makes the royal power and the people follow the Brahmin.

15.6.s: ojasy eva tad vīrye pratitiṣṭhaty ojo vīryaṃ traikakubham
15.6.d: ओजस्य् एव तद् वीर्ये प्रतितिष्ठत्य् ओजो वीर्यं त्रैककुभम्
15.6.m: He thereby firmly supports himself in power and strength; power and strength is the Traikakubha.
There is the Udvaṃśīya; [its purpose is] just what is the explanation of the Udvaṃśīya.

15.6.s: aṣṭācatvāriṃśaṃ eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai prajātyai
15.6.d: अष्टाचत्वारिंशं एव स्तोमो भवति प्रतिष्ठायै प्रजात्यै
15.6.m: The stoma is forty-eight-fold, for support, for procreation.

15.7.s: gāyatraṃ vai saptamam ahas traiṣṭubham aṣṭamaṃ jāgataṃ navamam athaitad ānuṣṭubham ahar yad daśamam
15.7.d: गायत्रं वै सप्तमम् अहस् त्रैष्टुभम् अष्टमं जागतं नवमम् अथैतद् आनुष्टुभम् अहर् यद् दशमम्
15.7.m: The seventh day belongs to the gāyatrī, the eighth to the triṣṭubh, the ninth to the jagatī; then this tenth day belongs to the anuṣṭubh.

15.7.s: tad āhur yad ānuṣṭubhaṃ stomyāṃ pratyakṣam upeyuḥ parāṃ parāvataṃ yajamāno gacchen na pratitiṣṭhed iti yā vai caturviṃśatir gāyatryas tā aṣṭādaśānuṣṭubho 'nuṣṭubham eva tat stomyāṃ parokṣam upayanti pratiṣṭhāyai pratitiṣṭhati
15.7.d: तद् आहुर् यद् आनुष्टुभं स्तोम्यां प्रत्यक्षम् उपेयुः परां परावतं यजमानो गच्छेन् न प्रतितिष्ठेद् इति या वै चतुर्विंशतिर् गायत्र्यस् ता अष्टादशानुष्टुभो ऽनुष्टुभम् एव तत् स्तोम्यां परोक्षम् उपयन्ति प्रतिष्ठायै प्रतितिष्ठति
15.7.m: They say regarding this: ‘If they were to enter directly upon the stoma belonging to the anuṣṭubh, the sacrificer would go to the farthest distance and would not find support.’ The twenty-four gāyatrīs are eighteen anuṣṭubhs. They thereby enter indirectly upon the stoma belonging to the anuṣṭubh, for support. He finds support.

15.7.s: prajāpatiṃ vā etenāhnā pariveviṣati tatra vyavavadyaṃ yad vai śreṣṭhe pariviṣyamāṇo vadaty annādyasya so 'vagrahas tasmān na vyavavadyam annādyasyānavagrāhāya
15.7.d: प्रजापतिं वा एतेनाह्ना परिवेविषति तत्र व्यववद्यं यद् वै श्रेष्ठे परिविष्यमाणो वदत्य् अन्नाद्यस्य सो ऽवग्रहस् तस्मान् न व्यववद्यम् अन्नाद्यस्यानवग्राहाय
15.7.m: One waits upon Prajāpati through this day. There one must speak intermittently. If one speaks while waiting upon a superior, that is a hindrance to food. Therefore, one should not speak continuously, so as not to hinder food.

15.7.s: tad u vyavavadyaṃ yathā śreṣṭhāya baliṃ hriyamāṇaṃ panthānaṃ paryanuvedayati gatyai tathā tat
15.7.d: तद् उ व्यववद्यं यथा श्रेष्ठाय बलिं ह्रियमाणं पन्थानं पर्यनुवेदयति गत्यै तथा तत्
15.7.m: Yet one must speak intermittently, just as one announces the path for a tribute being brought to a superior, for the journey; so is that.

15.7.s: yāvaty anuṣṭup tāvatīṃ vācaṃ sampādya vibrūyus tad v anatiriktaṃ svasyo caiva yajñasyāriṣṭyai
15.7.d: यावत्य् अनुष्टुप् तावतीं वाचं सम्पाद्य विब्रूयुस् तद् व् अनतिरिक्तं स्वस्यो चैव यज्ञस्यारिष्ट्यै
15.7.m: Having made speech correspond in measure to an anuṣṭubh, they should speak out. That is not excessive, and it is for the unharmed condition of their own sacrifice.

15.7.s: abhi vā ete devān ārohantīty āhur ye daśabhir aharbhiḥ stuvata iti pañcānām ahnām anurūpaiḥ pratyavayanti yathābhyāruhya pratyavarohet tathā tan navarco bhavati yā evāmūḥ prayacchan yā avadadhāti tā etā udasyati
15.7.d: अभि वा एते देवान् आरोहन्तीत्य् आहुर् ये दशभिर् अहर्भिः स्तुवत इति पञ्चानाम् अह्नाम् अनुरूपैः प्रत्यवयन्ति यथाभ्यारुह्य प्रत्यवरोहेत् तथा तन् नवर्चो भवति या एवामूः प्रयच्छन् या अवदधाति ता एता उदस्यति
15.7.m: They say: ‘They mount up to the gods, who praise with ten days.’ With the corresponding verses of five days they descend. Just as one having mounted up would descend, so is that. It consists of nine verses. Those very ones which he holds forth, which he deposits, these he tosses upward.

15.7.s: vāruṇy eṣā bhavati yad vai yajñasya duriṣṭaṃ tad varuṇo gṛhṇāti tad eva tad avayajaty ādityaiṣā bhavatīyaṃ vā aditir asyām eva pratitiṣṭhati
15.7.d: वारुण्य् एषा भवति यद् वै यज्ञस्य दुरिष्टं तद् वरुणो गृह्णाति तद् एव तद् अवयजत्य् आदित्यैषा भवतीयं वा अदितिर् अस्याम् एव प्रतितिष्ठति
15.7.m: This [verse] is addressed to Varuṇa; whatever in the sacrifice is ill-offered, that Varuṇa seizes: that he thereby expiates by sacrifice. This [verse] is addressed to Aditi; this [earth] is Aditi: he finds support in this very [earth].

15.7.s: caturviṃśa eva stomo bhavati tejase brahmarcasāya
15.7.d: चतुर्विंश एव स्तोमो भवति तेजसे ब्रह्मर्चसाय
15.7.m: The stoma is the twenty-four-fold, for splendour, for brahminical lustre.

15.8.s: suṣamiddho na āvaha ity āpriya ājyāni bhavanti
15.8.d: सुषमिद्धो न आवह इत्य् आप्रिय आज्यानि भवन्ति
15.8.m: ‘Well-kindled, bring [the gods] to us’: these Āprī verses are the ājyastotras.

15.8.s: prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata sa dugdho riricānāmanyata sa etāny āpriya ājyāny apaśyat tair ātmānam āprīṇāt dugdha iva vā eṣa riricāno yo daśabhir aharbhis tuṣṭuvāno yad etāny āpriya ājyāni bhavanty ātmānam evaitair āprīṇāti
15.8.d: प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत स दुग्धो रिरिचानामन्यत स एतान्य् आप्रिय आज्यान्य् अपश्यत् तैर् आत्मानम् आप्रीणात् दुग्ध इव वा एष रिरिचानो यो दशभिर् अहर्भिस् तुष्टुवानो यद् एतान्य् आप्रिय आज्यानि भवन्त्य् आत्मानम् एवैतैर् आप्रीणाति
15.8.m: Prajāpati created creatures. Being milked out, he felt emptied. He saw these Āprī ājyastotras; with them he completely replenished himself. Milked out, as it were, and emptied is he who has praised with ten days. That these Āprī ājyastotras are [used], he completely replenishes himself with them.

15.8.s: yad adya sūra udita iti sūravan maitrāvaruṇam
15.8.d: यद् अद्य सूर उदित इति सूरवन् मैत्रावरुणम्
15.8.m: ‘When the sun has risen today’: this verse containing the word ‘sun’ belongs to Mitra and Varuṇa.

15.8.s: anto vai sūro 'nta etad daśamam ahnām anta eva tadantena stuvate pratiṣṭhāyai
15.8.d: अन्तो वै सूरो ऽन्त एतद् दशमम् अह्नाम् अन्त एव तदन्तेन स्तुवते प्रतिष्ठायै
15.8.m: The sun is the end; this tenth day is the end of the days. By the end they praise at the end, for support.

15.8.s: ut tvā madantu somā ity udvad aindram utthānasya rūpam
15.8.d: उत् त्वा मदन्तु सोमा इत्य् उद्वद् ऐन्द्रम् उत्थानस्य रूपम्
15.8.m: ‘Let the somas exhilarate you upward’: this verse containing the word ‘up’ belongs to Indra, a symbol of rising up.

15.8.s: indrāgnī āgataṃ sutam iti yenaiva rūpeṇa prayanti tad abhyudyanti stomaḥ
15.8.d: इन्द्राग्नी आगतं सुतम् इति येनैव रूपेण प्रयन्ति तद् अभ्युद्यन्ति स्तोमः
15.8.m: ‘O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed [juice]’: with the very form with which they set out, to that they rise; [such is] the stoma.

15.9.s: uccā te jātam andhasa ity udvatyo gāyatryo bhavanty utthānasya rūpam
15.9.d: उच्चा ते जातम् अन्धस इत्य् उद्वत्यो गायत्र्यो भवन्त्य् उत्थानस्य रूपम्
15.9.m: ‘High is your juice born’: there are gāyatrī verses containing the word ‘high’, a symbol of rising up.

15.9.s: punānas soma dhāraya iti panthānam eva tat paryavayanti
15.9.d: पुनानस् सोम धारय इति पन्थानम् एव तत् पर्यवयन्ति
15.9.m: ‘Purifying yourself, O Soma, with a stream’: they thereby come down around to the path.

15.9.s: ā jāgṛvir vipra ṛtaṃ matīnām iti yad āpte pravatīḥ kuryur atipadyer anyad āvatyo bhavanty anatipādāya
15.9.d: आ जागृविर् विप्र ऋतं मतीनाम् इति यद् आप्ते प्रवतीः कुर्युर् अतिपद्येर् अन्यद् आवत्यो भवन्त्य् अनतिपादाय
15.9.m: ‘Waking, wise, the cosmic order of thoughts’: if they were to make [verses] containing ‘pra-’ at the conclusion, they would go astray. Since they have [verses] containing ‘ā-’, it is for not going astray.

15.9.s: gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
15.9.d: गायत्रं भवति यद् एव गायत्रस्य ब्राह्मणम्
15.9.m: There is the Gāyatra; [its purpose is] just what is the explanation of the Gāyatra.

15.9.s: āmahīyavaṃ bhavati kḷptiś cānnādyaṃ ca kḷptiṃ caivaitenānnādyaṃ cābhyuttiṣṭhanti
15.9.d: आमहीयवं भवति कॢप्तिश् चान्नाद्यं च कॢप्तिं चैवैतेनान्नाद्यं चाभ्युत्तिष्ठन्ति
15.9.m: There is the Āmahīyava; [it is] proper order and food. Through this, they rise up to proper order and food.
There is the Ājiga, for winning the race.

15.9.s: ājir vā eṣa pratato yat dvādaśāhas tasyaitad ujjityai
15.9.d: आजिर् वा एष प्रततो यत् द्वादशाहस् तस्यैतद् उज्जित्यै
15.9.m: A race indeed is this twelve-day rite that is spread out; this is for winning it.
There is the Ābhīka, for overcoming.

15.9.s: āṅgirasas tapas tepānāḥ śucam aśocaṃs ta etat sāmāpaśyaṃs tān abhīke 'bhyavarṣat tena śucam aśamayanta yad abhīke 'bhyavarṣat tasmād ābhīkaṃ yām eva pūrvair aharbhiḥ śucaṃ śocanti tām etenānna śamayitvottiṣṭhanti
15.9.d: आङ्गिरसस् तपस् तेपानाः शुचम् अशोचंस् त एतत् सामापश्यंस् तान् अभीके ऽभ्यवर्षत् तेन शुचम् अशमयन्त यद् अभीके ऽभ्यवर्षत् तस्माद् आभीकं याम् एव पूर्वैर् अहर्भिः शुचं शोचन्ति ताम् एतेनान्न शमयित्वोत्तिष्ठन्ति
15.9.m: The descendants of Aṅgiras, practicing ascetic heat, experienced grief. They saw this sāman. It rained upon them in their immediate presence; by it they appeased their grief. Because it rained upon them in their immediate presence, therefore it is called the Ābhīka. The grief that they grieve during the previous days, they appease with this and then conclude [the rite].

15.9.s: utsedhena vai devāḥ paśūn udasedhan niṣedhena paryagṛhṇan
15.9.d: उत्सेधेन वै देवाः पशून् उदसेधन् निषेधेन पर्यगृह्णन्
15.9.m: By the Utsedha the gods drove up the cattle, and by the Niṣedha they enclosed them.
The Yajñāyajñīya is between the Utsedha and the Niṣedha.

15.9.s: paśavo 'nnādyaṃ yajñāyajñīyaṃ paśūn eva tad annādyam utsedhaniṣedhābhyāṃ parigṛhṇāti
15.9.d: पशवो ऽन्नाद्यं यज्ञायज्ञीयं पशून् एव तद् अन्नाद्यम् उत्सेधनिषेधाभ्यां परिगृह्णाति
15.9.m: The Yajñāyajñīya is cattle, [it is] food. By means of the Utsedha and the Niṣedha, he thereby encloses cattle and food.

15.9.s: mādhyandine vai pavamāne devā yajñāyajñīyena yajñaṃ saṃsthāpya svargaṃ lokam ārohaṃs tad ya evaṃ veda mādhyandina evaitat pavamāne yajñāyajñīyena yajñaṃ saṃsthāpya svargaṃ lokam ārohati
15.9.d: माध्यन्दिने वै पवमाने देवा यज्ञायज्ञीयेन यज्ञं संस्थाप्य स्वर्गं लोकम् आरोहंस् तद् य एवं वेद माध्यन्दिन एवैतत् पवमाने यज्ञायज्ञीयेन यज्ञं संस्थाप्य स्वर्गं लोकम् आरोहति
15.9.m: At the midday Pavamāna, the gods, having brought the sacrifice to completion with the Yajñāyajñīya, ascended to the heavenly world. He who knows this, having brought the sacrifice to completion with the Yajñāyajñīya at the midday Pavamāna, ascends to the heavenly world.

15.9.s: atho parokṣam anuṣṭubhaṃ sampadyate 'har eṣā vai pratyakṣam anuṣṭup yad yajñāyajñīyaṃ tad yat tṛtīyasavane kuryuḥ pratyakṣam anuṣṭubham ṛccheyus tasmān mādhyandine kurvanti tena parokṣam anuṣṭubham upayanti
15.9.d: अथो परोक्षम् अनुष्टुभं सम्पद्यते ऽहर् एषा वै प्रत्यक्षम् अनुष्टुप् यद् यज्ञायज्ञीयं तद् यत् तृतीयसवने कुर्युः प्रत्यक्षम् अनुष्टुभम् ऋच्छेयुस् तस्मान् माध्यन्दिने कुर्वन्ति तेन परोक्षम् अनुष्टुभम् उपयन्ति
15.9.m: Moreover, the day secretly attains the anuṣṭubh. This Yajñāyajñīya is openly the anuṣṭubh. If they should perform it at the third pressing, they would directly attain the anuṣṭubh. Therefore they perform it at the midday [pressing]; thereby they secretly approach the anuṣṭubh.

15.9.s: etad vai yajñasya śvastanaṃ yad gaurīvitam etad āyatano yajamāno yan madhyandino yad gaurīvitaṃ madhyandine bhavati śvastanam eva tad yajamāna ātman dhatte stomaḥ
15.9.d: एतद् वै यज्ञस्य श्वस्तनं यद् गौरीवितम् एतद् आयतनो यजमानो यन् मध्यन्दिनो यद् गौरीवितं मध्यन्दिने भवति श्वस्तनम् एव तद् यजमान आत्मन् धत्ते स्तोमः
15.9.m: The Gaurīvita is the morrow of the sacrifice. The midday is the abode of the sacrificer. That the Gaurīvita is at the midday, the sacrificer thereby establishes the morrow in himself. The stoma [is complete].

15.10.s: kayā naś citra ābhuvad iti kavatyas tena prājāpatyāḥ ko hi prajāpatiḥ prajāpater āptyai
15.10.d: कया नश् चित्र आभुवद् इति कवत्यस् तेन प्राजापत्याः को हि प्रजापतिः प्रजापतेर् आप्त्यै
15.10.m: [The verses beginning] 'By which wonderful [aid] has he become ours...' contain 'ka'; thereby they belong to Prajāpati, for Prajāpati is Ka, for obtaining Prajāpati.

15.10.s: mā cid anyad viśaṃsata ity utthānam eva tad āśiṣo hy etarhi
15.10.d: मा चिद् अन्यद् विशंसत इत्य् उत्थानम् एव तद् आशिषो ह्य् एतर्हि
15.10.m: 'Do not praise anything else...'—that is the concluding; for these are the blessings at this stage.

15.10.s: ud u tye madhumattamā ity udvatya udayanīye 'hany etad āśiṣo hy evaitarhi
15.10.d: उद् उ त्ये मधुमत्तमा इत्य् उद्वत्य उदयनीये ऽहन्य् एतद् आशिषो ह्य् एवैतर्हि
15.10.m: 'Upward indeed have these sweetest...' contains the word 'ud' ('upward') on the concluding day; for these are the blessings at this stage.

15.10.s: tarobhir vo vidadvasum iti stomo vai taro yajño vidadvasuḥ stomena vai yajño yujyate yat tarobhir vo vidadvasum ity āha yajñam eva tad yunakti
15.10.d: तरोभिर् वो विदद्वसुम् इति स्तोमो वै तरो यज्ञो विदद्वसुः स्तोमेन वै यज्ञो युज्यते यत् तरोभिर् वो विदद्वसुम् इत्य् आह यज्ञम् एव तद् युनक्ति
15.10.m: 'With energies [we approach] you who find wealth...'—energy is the stoma; finding wealth is the sacrifice. By means of the stoma the sacrifice is yoked. When he says, 'With energies [we approach] you who find wealth,' he thereby yokes the sacrifice.
The Rathantara is the pṛṣṭha on the verses of the Vāmadevya.

15.10.s: gāyatrī vai rathantarasya yoniḥ svāyām eva tad yonau rathantaraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati
15.10.d: गायत्री वै रथन्तरस्य योनिः स्वायाम् एव तद् योनौ रथन्तरं प्रतिष्ठापयति
15.10.m: The gāyatrī is the womb of the Rathantara. He thereby establishes the Rathantara in its own womb.

15.10.s: tejo vai gāyatrī chandasā tejo rathantaraṃ sāmnā tejaś caturviṃśastomānāṃ teja eva tat samyak saṃdadhāty api ha putrasya putras tejasvī bhavati
15.10.d: तेजो वै गायत्री छन्दसा तेजो रथन्तरं साम्ना तेजश् चतुर्विंशस्तोमानां तेज एव तत् सम्यक् संदधात्य् अपि ह पुत्रस्य पुत्रस् तेजस्वी भवति
15.10.m: Splendour is the gāyatrī among the metres; splendour is the Rathantara among the sāmans; splendour is the twenty-fourfold stoma among the stomas. He thereby completely joins splendour to splendour; also the grandson becomes possessed of splendour.

15.10.s: aṣṭākṣareṇa prathamāyā ṛcaḥ prastauty aṣṭāśaphāṃs tatpaśūn avarundhe
15.10.d: अष्टाक्षरेण प्रथमाया ऋचः प्रस्तौत्य् अष्टाशफांस् तत्पशून् अवरुन्धे
15.10.m: He chants the prastāva of the first verse with eight syllables; he thereby obtains eight-hoofed cattle.

15.10.s: dyvakṣareṇottarayor ṛcoḥ prastauti dvipād yajamāno yajamānam eva yajñe paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati
15.10.d: द्य्वक्षरेणोत्तरयोर् ऋचोः प्रस्तौति द्विपाद् यजमानो यजमानम् एव यज्ञे पशुषु प्रतिष्ठापयति
15.10.m: He chants the prastāva of the two subsequent verses with two syllables; the sacrificer is two-footed; he thereby establishes the sacrificer in the sacrifice, in cattle.

15.10.s: gāyatraṃ vai rathantaraṃ gāyatracchando yad gāyatrīṣu rathantaram bhavati tena svāyāṃ janatāyām ṛdhnotīme vai lokā gāyatrī yad gāyatrīṣu rathantaraṃ bhavatīmān eva tal lokān samāpyottiṣṭhanti
15.10.d: गायत्रं वै रथन्तरं गायत्रच्छन्दो यद् गायत्रीषु रथन्तरम् भवति तेन स्वायां जनतायाम् ऋध्नोतीमे वै लोका गायत्री यद् गायत्रीषु रथन्तरं भवतीमान् एव तल् लोकान् समाप्योत्तिष्ठन्ति
15.10.m: The Rathantara is of gāyatra nature; the gāyatrī is the metre. That the Rathantara is on gāyatrī verses, thereby he thrives among his own people. These worlds are the gāyatrī. That the Rathantara is on gāyatrī verses, having attained these worlds they conclude [the rite].

15.10.s: etena vai medhātithiḥ kāṇvo vibhindukād vyūdhnīr gā udasṛjata paśūnām avarudhyai maidhātithaṃ kriyate
15.10.d: एतेन वै मेधातिथिः काण्वो विभिन्दुकाद् व्यूध्नीर् गा उदसृजत पशूनाम् अवरुध्यै मैधातिथं क्रियते
15.10.m: By this [sāman], Medhātithi Kāṇva produced cows with full udders from Vibhinduka. The Maidhātitha is performed for obtaining cattle.
The Abhīvarta is the chant for the Brahman, having a single-syllable cadence, for firm support.

15.10.s: ekākṣarā vai vāg vācy eva pratiṣṭhāyottiṣṭhanti
15.10.d: एकाक्षरा वै वाग् वाच्य् एव प्रतिष्ठायोत्तिष्ठन्ति
15.10.m: Speech consists of one syllable. Having firmly supported themselves in speech, they conclude [the rite].
The Kāleya is the chant for the acchāvāka.

15.10.s: samānaloke vai kāleyaṃ ca rathantaraṃ ceyaṃ vai rathantaraṃ paśavaḥ kāleyam asyāṃ caiva paśuṣu ca pratiṣṭhāyottiṣṭhanti stomaḥ
15.10.d: समानलोके वै कालेयं च रथन्तरं चेयं वै रथन्तरं पशवः कालेयम् अस्यां चैव पशुषु च प्रतिष्ठायोत्तिष्ठन्ति स्तोमः
15.10.m: The Kāleya and the Rathantara have a common world. This [earth] is the Rathantara, and the Kāleya is cattle. Having firmly supported themselves in this [earth] and in cattle, they conclude [the rite]. The stoma [is complete].

15.11.s: svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā iti gāyatrī bhavati madavad vai rasavat tṛtīyasavanaṃ madam eva tad rasaṃ dadhāti
15.11.d: स्वादिष्ठया मदिष्ठया इति गायत्री भवति मदवद् वै रसवत् तृतीयसवनं मदम् एव तद् रसं दधाति
15.11.m: [The verse beginning] 'With the sweetest, most exhilarating...' is a gāyatrī. The third pressing is intoxicating, full of sap. He thereby places intoxication and sap [into it].

15.11.s: gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
15.11.d: गायत्रं भवति यद् एव गायत्रस्य ब्राह्मणम्
15.11.m: It is the Gāyatra [sāman], as is the brāhmaṇa of the Gāyatra.
It is the Saṃhita [sāman], having a two-syllable cadence, for firm support. Having firmly supported themselves, they conclude [the rite].

15.11.s: saphena vai devā imān lokān samāpnuvant samāpnuvaṃs tat saphasya saphatvam imān evaitena lokān samāpyottiṣṭhanti
15.11.d: सफेन वै देवा इमान् लोकान् समाप्नुवन्त् समाप्नुवंस् तत् सफस्य सफत्वम् इमान् एवैतेन लोकान् समाप्योत्तिष्ठन्ति
15.11.m: By the Śapha the gods reached these worlds; because they reached them (samāpnuvan), that is the nature of the Śapha (śaphatvam). Having reached these worlds with it, they conclude [the rite].

15.11.s: rohitakūlīyaṃ bhavati yad eva rohitakūlīyasya brāhmaṇam
15.11.d: रोहितकूलीयं भवति यद् एव रोहितकूलीयस्य ब्राह्मणम्
15.11.m: There is the Rohitakūlīya [sāman], as is the brāhmaṇa of the Rohitakūlīya.

15.11.s: śyāvāśvāndhīgave bhavataḥ samīcyau virājau dadhāty annādyāya
15.11.d: श्यावाश्वान्धीगवे भवतः समीच्यौ विराजौ दधात्य् अन्नाद्याय
15.11.m: There are the Śyāvāśva and the Āndhīgava [sāmans]; he arranges two harmonious virāj verses for food.
They chant praise on pipīlikāmadhyā verses.

15.11.s: indro vṛtraṃ hatvā nāstṛṣīti manyamānaḥ parāṃ parāvatam agacchat sa etām anuṣṭubhaṃ vyauhat tāṃ madhye vyavāsarpad indragṛhe vā eṣo 'bhaye yajate abhaya uttiṣṭhati ya evaṃ vidvān etāsu stuvate
15.11.d: इन्द्रो वृत्रं हत्वा नास्तृषीति मन्यमानः परां परावतम् अगच्छत् स एताम् अनुष्टुभं व्यौहत् तां मध्ये व्यवासर्पद् इन्द्रगृहे वा एषो ऽभये यजते अभय उत्तिष्ठति य एवं विद्वान् एतासु स्तुवते
15.11.m: Indra, having slain Vṛtra, thinking, 'I have not overcome him,' went to the farthest distance. He unfolded this anuṣṭubh; he crept into its middle. He sacrifices in the fearless abode of Indra, he departs fearless, who knowing thus chants praise on these [verses].

15.11.s: yajñāyajñīyanidhanaṃ sauhaviṣaṃ bhavati yajñāyajñīyād eva tat tṛtīyasavene na yanti
15.11.d: यज्ञायज्ञीयनिधनं सौहविषं भवति यज्ञायज्ञीयाद् एव तत् तृतीयसवेने न यन्ति
15.11.m: The Sauhaviṣa [sāman] has the cadence of the Yajñāyajñīya. They do not depart from the Yajñāyajñīya at the third pressing.

15.11.s: sarvasyāptyai sarvasya jityai sarvaṃ vā ete vājaṃ jayanti ye daśamam ahar āgacchanty annaṃ vai vājo 'nnādyasyāvarudhyai
15.11.d: सर्वस्याप्त्यै सर्वस्य जित्यै सर्वं वा एते वाजं जयन्ति ये दशमम् अहर् आगच्छन्त्य् अन्नं वै वाजो ऽन्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै
15.11.m: For obtaining everything, for winning everything. All the prize indeed do they win who reach the tenth day. The prize is food, for the securing of food.

15.11.s: daśākṣaraṃ nidhanam upayanti daśarātrasya dhṛtyai daśākṣarā virāḍ vairājam annam annādyasyāvarudhyai
15.11.d: दशाक्षरं निधनम् उपयन्ति दशरात्रस्य धृत्यै दशाक्षरा विराड् वैराजम् अन्नम् अन्नाद्यस्यावरुध्यै
15.11.m: They adopt a ten-syllable cadence, for the holding fast of the ten-day rite. The virāj has ten syllables; food belongs to the virāj, for the securing of food.

15.11.s: sūryavatīṣu stuvanty anto vai sūro 'nta etad daśamam ahnām anta eva tad antena stuvate pratiṣṭhāyai
15.11.d: सूर्यवतीषु स्तुवन्त्य् अन्तो वै सूरो ऽन्त एतद् दशमम् अह्नाम् अन्त एव तद् अन्तेन स्तुवते प्रतिष्ठायै
15.11.m: They chant praise on verses containing the word 'sūrya' ('sun'). The sun is the end; this tenth day is the end of the days. By the end they thereby chant praise at the end, for firm support.

15.11.s: upavatyo bhavanti pratiṣṭhāyai parivatyo bhavanti sarvasya paryāptyai
15.11.d: उपवत्यो भवन्ति प्रतिष्ठायै परिवत्यो भवन्ति सर्वस्य पर्याप्त्यै
15.11.m: There are verses containing the prefix 'upa', for firm support; there are verses containing the prefix 'pari', for the encompassing of all.

15.11.s: caturviṃśa eva stomo bhavati tejase brahmavarcasāya
15.11.d: चतुर्विंश एव स्तोमो भवति तेजसे ब्रह्मवर्चसाय
15.11.m: The stoma is the twenty-fourfold stoma, for splendour, for brahminical lustre.

15.12.s: virāṭsu vāmadevyam agniṣṭomasāma bhavati śāntyai kḷptyai
15.12.d: विराट्सु वामदेव्यम् अग्निष्टोमसाम भवति शान्त्यै कॢप्त्यै
15.12.m: The Vāmadevya is the Agniṣṭoma-sāman on virāj verses, for appeasement, for proper arrangement.

15.12.s: sad vai vāmadevyaṃ sāmnāṃ sad virāṭ chandasāṃ sat trayastriṃśaḥ stomānāṃ satām antān saṃdhāyottiṣṭhanty api ha putrasya sattvam aśnute
15.12.d: सद् वै वामदेव्यं साम्नां सद् विराट् छन्दसां सत् त्रयस्त्रिंशः स्तोमानां सताम् अन्तान् संधायोत्तिष्ठन्त्य् अपि ह पुत्रस्य सत्त्वम् अश्नुते
15.12.m: The Vāmadevya is the true among the sāmans, the virāj is the true among the metres, the thirty-threefold stoma is the true among the stomas. Having joined the ends of the true, they conclude [the rite]; he also attains the truth of a son.

15.12.s: brahmavādino vadanti yatas sattrād udasthātā3 sthitā3d iti yad yata iti brūyur apratiṣṭhānā aprajaso bhaviṣyantīty enān brūyād yat sthitād iti brūyuḥ sthāyukaiṣāṃ śrīr bhaviṣyati na vasīyāṃso bhaviṣyantīty enān brūyāt pūrṇād eva pūrṇam abhyudasthāmeti brūyuḥ
15.12.d: ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति यतस् सत्त्राद् उदस्थाता3 स्थिता3द् इति यद् यत इति ब्रूयुर् अप्रतिष्ठाना अप्रजसो भविष्यन्तीत्य् एनान् ब्रूयाद् यत् स्थिताद् इति ब्रूयुः स्थायुकैषां श्रीर् भविष्यति न वसीयांसो भविष्यन्तीत्य् एनान् ब्रूयात् पूर्णाद् एव पूर्णम् अभ्युदस्थामेति ब्रूयुः
15.12.m: The theologians say: 'From what did you conclude the session? from one in progress, or from one completed?' If they should say, 'from one in progress,' he should say to them, 'They will be without firm support, without offspring.' If they should say, 'from one completed,' he should say to them, 'Their prosperity will remain stationary, they will not become wealthier.' They should say: 'From the full to the full did we conclude.'

15.12.s: ete vai pūrṇāt pūrṇam abhyuttiṣṭhanti ye vāmadevyena stutvottiṣṭhanti
15.12.d: एते वै पूर्णात् पूर्णम् अभ्युत्तिष्ठन्ति ये वामदेव्येन स्तुत्वोत्तिष्ठन्ति
15.12.m: They indeed conclude from the full to the full who conclude having praised with the Vāmadevya.

15.12.s: antarikṣaṃ vai vāmadevyam antarikṣeṇedaṃ sarvaṃ pūrṇam
15.12.d: अन्तरिक्षं वै वामदेव्यम् अन्तरिक्षेणेदं सर्वं पूर्णम्
15.12.m: The Vāmadevya is the intermediate space; by the intermediate space all this is filled.

15.12.s: eṣa vai samṛddhaḥ stomo yat trayastriṃśas trayastriṃśadakṣarāsu samṛddhāv eva pratitiṣṭhanti
15.12.d: एष वै समृद्धः स्तोमो यत् त्रयस्त्रिंशस् त्रयस्त्रिंशदक्षरासु समृद्धाव् एव प्रतितिष्ठन्ति
15.12.m: The thirty-threefold stoma is a fully completed stoma. On verses of thirty-three syllables they firmly support themselves in full completion.

15.12.s: sarveṣāṃ vā etāś chandasāṃ rūpaṃ yāt tripadās tena gāyatryo yad ekādaśākṣarāṇi padāni tena triṣṭubho yat dvādaśākṣaraṃ padaṃ tena jagatyo yat trayastriṃśadakṣarās tena virājas tenaiva cānuṣṭubho na hy ekasmād akṣarād virādhayanti
15.12.d: सर्वेषां वा एताश् छन्दसां रूपं यात् त्रिपदास् तेन गायत्र्यो यद् एकादशाक्षराणि पदानि तेन त्रिष्टुभो यत् द्वादशाक्षरं पदं तेन जगत्यो यत् त्रयस्त्रिंशदक्षरास् तेन विराजस् तेनैव चानुष्टुभो न ह्य् एकस्माद् अक्षराद् विराधयन्ति
15.12.m: These indeed are the form of all the metres: in that they have three lines, thereby they are gāyatrīs; in that they have eleven-syllable lines, thereby they are triṣṭubhs; in that they have a twelve-syllable line, thereby they are jagatīs; in that they have thirty-three syllables, thereby they are virājs, and thereby also anuṣṭubhs, for they do not fail on account of a single syllable.

15.12.s: trayastriṃśa eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai devatāsu vā eṣa pratiṣṭhitaḥ
15.12.d: त्रयस्त्रिंश एव स्तोमो भवति प्रतिष्ठायै देवतासु वा एष प्रतिष्ठितः
15.12.m: The stoma is the thirty-three-fold stoma for firm establishment; firmly established indeed is this [stoma] among the deities.

16.1.s: prajāpatir vā idam eka āsīn nāhar āsīn na rātrir āsīt so 'sminn andhe tamasi prāsarpat sa aicchat sa etam abhyapadyata tato vai tasmai vyaucchad vyuṣṭir vā eṣa āhriyate yad vai taj jyotir abhavat tat jyotiṣo jyotiṣṭvam
16.1.d: प्रजापतिर् वा इदम् एक आसीन् नाहर् आसीन् न रात्रिर् आसीत् सो ऽस्मिन्न् अन्धे तमसि प्रासर्पत् स ऐच्छत् स एतम् अभ्यपद्यत ततो वै तस्मै व्यौच्छद् व्युष्टिर् वा एष आह्रियते यद् वै तज् ज्योतिर् अभवत् तत् ज्योतिषो ज्योतिष्ट्वम्
16.1.m: Prajāpati, indeed, was alone here. There was no day, there was no night. He crawled about in this blind darkness. He searched. He arrived at this [rite]. Thereupon, indeed, it dawned for him.
